definition_zh: 古气候；遥远地质时期的气候
definition_en: the climate of a distant period in Earth's past, studied from preserved records and from models

senses.title: Climate of the distant past
senses.definition: the overall weather conditions of a period long before instrumental records
senses.definitionCN: 仪器记录出现很久之前某一时期的总体天气状况
senses.example: The paleoclimate of the Jurassic was far warmer than today.
senses.exampleCN: 侏罗纪的古气候远比今天温暖。
senses.why: The first half of the word means ancient, so the noun begins as climate pushed back beyond memory.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的前一半意为「古老」，所以它最初指被推回记忆之外的气候。

senses.title: A specific ancient climate state
senses.titleCN: 某一时期的具体气候状态
senses.definition: the particular temperature, rainfall and wind pattern that prevailed in a chosen interval
senses.definitionCN: 在某一选定时间段内占主导的具体温度、降水与风型
senses.example: The paleoclimate of that basin was dry and windy.
senses.exampleCN: 那个盆地在当时的古气候干燥多风。
senses.why: Once a time window is fixed, the word stops naming a vague past and names one describable state.
senses.whyCN: 一旦时间窗口固定，这个词就不再指模糊的过去，而指一个可描述的状态。

senses.title: An object of scientific study
senses.definition: the subject matter that paleoclimatologists reconstruct and compare
senses.definitionCN: 古气候学家加以重建与比较的研究对象
senses.example: Paleoclimate is the central object of study in this laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 古气候是这间实验室的核心研究对象。
senses.why: A field needs a name for what it studies, and the noun becomes that name.
senses.whyCN: 一个学科需要为它所研究的东西命名，这个词就成了那个名字。

senses.title: A preserved ancient record
senses.definition: the traces of old climate kept in ice, sediment, tree rings or fossils
senses.definitionCN: 保存在冰、沉积物、树木年轮或化石中的旧气候痕迹
senses.example: Tree rings preserve a paleoclimate record spanning three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 树木年轮保存着跨越三个世纪的古气候记录。
senses.why: Because the climate itself is gone, the word often shifts to the material that still carries its signal.
senses.whyCN: 气候本身已经消失，因此这个词常转到仍然携带其信号的材料上。

senses.title: A simulated ancient climate
senses.definition: a climate of the past produced by a computer model rather than measured directly
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机模型生成而非直接测量得到的过去气候
senses.example: The simulated paleoclimate shows a sudden cooling at the poles.
senses.exampleCN: 模拟出的古气候显示两极曾突然变冷。
senses.why: Models produce a climate that never leaves a direct reading, so the same noun covers the output.
senses.whyCN: 模型产生的气候从未留下直接读数，因此同一个名词也指这种输出。

senses.title: Regional difference in ancient climate
senses.definition: the contrast between the ancient climates of different regions at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同一时期不同地区古代气候之间的差别
senses.example: Regional paleoclimate differs sharply between the coast and the interior.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海与内陆的区域古气候差异很大。
senses.why: Climate is always uneven, so the word multiplies into regional versions that must be compared.
senses.whyCN: 气候从来不均匀，于是这个词分化为必须相互比较的区域版本。

senses.title: Climate of another planet
senses.definition: the ancient climate of a world other than Earth, inferred from its surface and atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 从地表与大气推断出的地球以外世界的古代气候
senses.example: Mars has its own paleoclimate, written in ice and dust layers.
senses.exampleCN: 火星有自己的古气候，写在冰层与尘层里。
senses.why: The prefix means ancient rather than earthly, so planetary scientists can borrow the word freely.
senses.whyCN: 前缀只表示「古老」而不表示「地球」，因此行星科学家可以自由借用这个词。

senses.title: An ancient baseline for comparison
senses.definition: a past climate used as a reference against which present or modelled conditions are judged
senses.definitionCN: 用来衡量当前状况或模型状况的过去气候参照
senses.example: The modern climate serves as a paleoclimate benchmark for the model.
senses.exampleCN: 现代气候充当该模型的古气候基准。
senses.why: Comparison needs a fixed older state, and the noun takes on the role of the yardstick.
senses.whyCN: 比较需要一个固定的较旧状态，这个词便承担起尺子的角色。

intro.en: Paleoclimate joins Greek palaios, ancient, to Greek klima, a slope or zone, the word that reached English as climate through Latin clima. Paleo- became a scientific prefix in the nineteenth century, and the whole word belongs to the twentieth century; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊语「palaios」「古老」与希腊语「klima」「倾斜、地带」结合起来，后者经拉丁语「clima」进入英语作「climate」。前缀在十九世纪成为科学构词成分，整词属于二十世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Palaios meant ancient or long ago, and it became the first element of many scientific words.
items.cn: 这个词意为古老的、很久以前的，后来成为许多科学词的第一成分。

items.en: Klima first named a slope or a zone of the earth, because the angle of the sun was thought to shape each region.
items.cn: 这个词最初指斜坡或地表的地带，因为太阳的角度被认为塑造了每个区域。

items.en: Latin took klima as clima, keeping the sense of a zone and the conditions that went with it.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊词取作「clima」，保留了地带以及与之相伴的状况之意。

items.en: English climate descends from Latin clima and gradually narrowed to the weather of a region.
items.cn: 英语的「climate」源自拉丁语「clima」，逐渐收窄为某一地区的天气。

items.en: In the nineteenth century paleo- became a productive scientific prefix meaning ancient or prehistoric.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个表示「古老」的成分成为能产的科技术语前缀，义为远古的。

items.en: The whole word paleoclimate is a twentieth-century formation; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 整词「paleoclimate」是二十世纪的构造，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like paleoclimate; the second group names neighbouring ideas of ancient environments and climate records.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「paleoclimate」相近；第二组是与「古环境、气候记录」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning of or relating to an ancient climate.
entries.definitionCN: 指与古气候有关的形容词。

entries.definition: The science that reconstructs ancient climates from natural records.
entries.definitionCN: 指从自然记录重建古代气候的学科。

entries.definition: A researcher who works in that science.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事这门学科的研究者。

entries.definition: The long-term weather pattern of a region, the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地区的长期天气型，是复合词的后一半。

entries.definition: The study of ancient ecosystems; it shares the prefix but not the climate element.
entries.definitionCN: 指对古代生态系统的研究；共用前缀，但不含气候成分。

entries.definition: A plainer phrase for climate before the present, without the scientific prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指当前之前的气候，说法更朴素，不带科学前缀。

entries.definition: The whole ancient setting, including land, water and air, of which climate is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整的古代环境，包括陆地、水与空气，气候只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: A natural archive such as ice or sediment that stands in for direct measurements.
entries.definitionCN: 指冰、沉积物等代替直接测量的自然档案。

entries.definition: The sequence of climates through time, close to the recorded sense of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 指气候随时间变化的序列，接近这个词的记录义。

entries.definition: A computer simulation of climate, including versions run for ancient periods.
entries.definitionCN: 指气候的计算机模拟，也包括为古代时期运行的版本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek pieces inside the word, its real records and its real research phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词内部的希腊成分、真实记录与真实研究搭配。

normal.en: Paleo- means ancient and climate means climate, so the word says ancient climate outright.
normal.cn: 前成分意为「古老」，后成分意为「气候」，词义直接就是古气候。

normal.en: Greek palaios gave the ancient half, and Greek klima, a zone, gave the climate half.
normal.cn: 希腊语的「palaios」给出「古老」那一半，希腊语的「klima」「地带」给出「气候」那一半。

normal.en: A paleoclimate record is read from ice cores, tree rings, corals and lake sediment.
normal.cn: 古气候记录是从冰芯、树木年轮、珊瑚与湖泊沉积物中读出来的。

normal.en: Regional paleoclimate reminds you that one date can hold several different climates.
normal.cn: 区域古气候提醒你，同一个年代可以有好几种不同的气候。

normal.en: Paleoclimatology and paleoclimatologist are the science and the person built on the same stem.
normal.cn: 古气候学与古气候学家是同一词干上长出的学科与人。

abstract.en: A paleoclimate is a climate with no thermometer, read from what the earth kept by accident.
abstract.cn: 古气候是一种没有温度计的气候，只能从大地偶然留下的东西里读。

abstract.en: Ice remembers air the way paper remembers ink, and the word names that memory as climate.
abstract.cn: 冰记住空气，就像纸记住墨，而这个词把那段记忆称作气候。

abstract.en: Every model of the future is checked against a paleoclimate, a past used as a ruler.
abstract.cn: 每一个关于未来的模型都要对照一个古气候，把过去当作尺子。

examples.en: Researchers used tree rings to infer the paleoclimate of the plateau.
examples.cn: 研究人员用树木年轮推断高原的古气候。

examples.en: The model reproduces the paleoclimate of the last glacial maximum.
examples.cn: 该模型重现了末次冰盛期的古气候。

examples.en: Mars missions search for evidence of a warmer paleoclimate.
examples.cn: 火星探测任务在寻找更温暖古气候的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佩里欧 克莱美特」——「佩里欧」听成「怕离欧」，远古的欧陆早已远离：古气候。

root: 希腊语「palaios」「古老」加希腊语「klima」「倾斜、地带」，后者经拉丁语「clima」进入英语作「climate」；「paleo-」是十九世纪的科学构词成分，整词属二十世纪，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a distant climate to a fixed ancient state, a field of study, a preserved record, a simulated output, a regional contrast, another planet and a baseline for comparison.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从遥远气候走向某一固定古代状态、学科对象、留存记录、模拟输出、区域差异、其他行星，以及用作比较的基准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drill lifts an ice core and the bubbles inside it hold air from a hundred thousand years ago.
core.cn: 核心意象：钻机提上一截冰芯，里面的气泡封着十万年前的空气。

branches.en: THE DISTANT CLIMATE: weather pushed back beyond any thermometer or written log.
branches.cn: 遥远气候：被推到任何温度计与文字记录之外的天气。

branches.en: THE FIXED STATE: one chosen interval with its own temperature, rain and wind.
branches.cn: 固定状态：一个选定的时间段，带着自己的温度、降水与风。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE AND ITS EVIDENCE: what the field studies, and the ice, rings and sediment that carry it.
branches.cn: 学科与证据：该领域研究的东西，以及携带它的冰、年轮与沉积物。

branches.en: THE MODEL AND THE RULER: a simulated past climate, and a past climate used to judge the present.
branches.cn: 模型与尺子：模拟出的过去气候，以及用来衡量当下的过去气候。

branches.en: THE UNEVEN AND THE ALIEN: one date with different regional climates, and a climate beyond Earth.
branches.cn: 不均匀与异星：同一年代的不同区域气候，以及地球之外的气候。

intro.en: Paleoclimate is built from two Greek elements that English still uses to make new technical words.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个希腊成分构成，英语至今仍用它们造新的技术词。

latinIntro.en: Greek klima passed into Latin as clima before English took it, so Latin clima belongs to this family.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语「klima」先进入拉丁语作「clima」，英语才借用，因此拉丁语「clima」属于这一族。

items.exampleCN: 这个词提供了复合词中表示「古老」的那一半。

items.example: The zone word later became the climate word.

items.example: Latin carried the Greek zone word into Europe.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个希腊地带词带到了欧洲。

items.example: It forms the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 它构成复合词的后一半。

items.example: The prefix marks the great age of the subject.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出研究对象的久远年代。

items.example: The compound is the ordinary technical name.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是普通的专业名称。

items.example: The adjective describes data or evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用来描述数据或证据。

items.example: The suffix turns the subject into a field.

definition_zh: 脱氧核糖核酸；遗传物质；遗传信息的载体

scene: 实验室里一条双螺旋模型在灯下旋转，彩色条带一段段咬合。 DNA carries the instructions that cells use to build and copy themselves.

senses.title: The double-stranded molecule
senses.definition: the long molecule made of two paired strands wound into a double helix
senses.definitionCN: 指由两条配对链缠绕成双螺旋的长分子
senses.example: DNA is a double helix held together by paired bases.
senses.exampleCN: 脱氧核糖核酸是双螺旋，由配对碱基维系。
senses.why: The abbreviation names a chemical, and its shape is the first thing anyone learns about it.
senses.whyCN: 这个缩写指一种化学物质，而它的形状是任何人最先学到的东西。

senses.title: The material of inheritance
senses.definition: the substance that passes genetic information from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指把遗传信息由亲代传给子代的物质
senses.example: DNA transmits traits from one generation to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 脱氧核糖核酸把性状从一代传到下一代。
senses.why: Once it was shown to carry genes, the molecule became the physical basis of heredity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦证明它携带基因，这个分子就成了遗传的物理基础。

senses.title: A sequence or genetic code
senses.definition: the ordered string of bases that spells out a gene or a whole genome
senses.definitionCN: 指拼出一个基因或整个基因组的碱基顺序
senses.example: The DNA of this species has been sequenced.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的脱氧核糖核酸已被测序。
senses.why: The molecule is also a text, and the word often means the message rather than the paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个分子也是一段文本，因此这个词常指信息而非载体。

senses.title: A sample or a test
senses.definition: material taken for identification, as in forensic or paternity testing
senses.definitionCN: 指用于身份识别而采集的材料，如法医或亲子鉴定
senses.example: The lab compared DNA from the two samples.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室比对了两个样本中的脱氧核糖核酸。
senses.why: A test turns the abstract molecule into evidence that can be compared.
senses.whyCN: 检测把这个抽象分子变成可供比对的证据。

senses.title: The essential character of something
senses.definition: the core pattern that makes an organization, style or idea what it is
senses.definitionCN: 指使一个组织、风格或想法成其为自身的核心模式
senses.example: Innovation is in the DNA of the company.
senses.exampleCN: 创新已写在这家公司的根本特质里。
senses.why: The code image invites metaphor: whatever is copied faithfully becomes a genetic text.
senses.whyCN: 密码的意象引出比喻：凡被忠实复制的东西都可说成一段遗传文本。

senses.title: Engineered or recombinant DNA
senses.titleCN: 被工程改造的脱氧核糖核酸
senses.definition: DNA cut and rejoined in the laboratory to combine sequences from different sources
senses.definitionCN: 指在实验室中被切割并重新连接、以组合不同来源序列的脱氧核糖核酸
senses.example: Recombinant DNA made human insulin possible.
senses.exampleCN: 重组脱氧核糖核酸使生产人胰岛素成为可能。
senses.why: Once the molecule could be cut and pasted, it became a construction material.
senses.whyCN: 这个分子一旦能被剪切与拼接，就成了一种建筑材料。

senses.title: DNA as a storage medium
senses.titleCN: 作为存储介质的脱氧核糖核酸
senses.definition: the use of synthetic DNA to encode digital data at very high density
senses.definitionCN: 指用合成脱氧核糖核酸以极高密度编码数字数据
senses.example: Researchers wrote a film into DNA and read it back.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把一部影片写入脱氧核糖核酸，再读回来。
senses.why: The same property that makes it a good archive, stability, makes it slow to read.
senses.whyCN: 使它成为优良档案的稳定性，也使它读取缓慢。

senses.title: The spelled-out chemical name
senses.definition: the full name deoxyribonucleic acid, used when the abbreviation needs defining
senses.definitionCN: 指在需要解释缩写时使用的全称「脱氧核糖核酸」
senses.example: The report defines DNA in its first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 报告在第一段就给出脱氧核糖核酸的全称。
senses.why: An abbreviation is only useful if it is unpacked once, and dictionaries do that work.
senses.whyCN: 缩写只有被展开一次才有用，词典承担这项工作。

intro.en: DNA is an abbreviation, not a root. It shortens deoxyribonucleic acid: nucleic from Latin nucleus, a kernel or the core of a cell; ribo from ribose, the sugar in the chain; deoxy marking the loss of one oxygen atom; acid from Latin acidus, sour. The abbreviation became standard in the mid-twentieth century, and its exact first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这是一个缩写而非词根。它缩短了「脱氧核糖核酸」这一全称：其中「核酸」出自拉丁语 nucleus「核、果核」，指细胞核；「核糖」指链中的糖；「脱氧」标记少了一个氧原子；「酸」出自拉丁语 acidus「酸的」。这个缩写在二十世纪中期成为通用写法，确切首见时间不确定。

items.en: Nucleus meant a kernel or a nut, and it gave the name to the cell's core.
items.cn: 这个词意为果核、坚果，后来用来命名细胞核。

items.en: Chemists found an acid rich in phosphorus inside cell nuclei and named it after the nucleus.
items.cn: 化学家在细胞核内发现一种富含磷的酸，便按「核」给它命名。

items.en: The five-carbon sugar in the chain gave the element ribo-.
items.cn: 链中的五碳糖提供了「核糖」这一成分。

items.en: The prefix marks the removal of one oxygen atom from the sugar, a difference from RNA.
items.cn: 这一前缀标记糖上少了一个氧原子，这正是与核糖核酸的区别。

items.en: The initials replaced the full chemical name as knowledge of heredity grew; the precise first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着遗传知识的发展，首字母缩写取代了化学全称；确切首见时间不确定。

items.en: The published structure gave the abbreviation a shape that could be drawn, taught and remembered.
items.cn: 结构的发表使这个缩写有了可绘制、可教学、可记忆的形状。

note.en: The first group shares the abbreviation or the chemical family; the second group names the things DNA is confused with or the units it contains.
note.cn: 第一组共享这一缩写或同一化学家族；第二组是容易与它混淆的概念，以及它所包含的单位。

entries.definition: Ribonucleic acid, which carries and translates instructions rather than storing them long-term.
entries.definitionCN: 核糖核酸，负责传递与翻译指令，而非长期储存。

entries.definition: Complementary DNA copied from an RNA template.
entries.definitionCN: 指以核糖核酸为模板复制出的互补脱氧核糖核酸。

entries.definition: The small DNA genome inside mitochondria, inherited from the mother.
entries.definitionCN: 指线粒体内的小型基因组，由母方遗传。

entries.definition: An enzyme that cuts DNA strands.
entries.definitionCN: 指切割脱氧核糖核酸链的酶。

entries.definition: The single unit, base plus sugar plus phosphate, that builds the chain.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成链的单个单位，即碱基加糖加磷酸。

entries.definition: A stretch of DNA that codes for a product or a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 指编码一种产物或一个性状的一段脱氧核糖核酸。

entries.definition: The complete set of genetic material in an organism.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个生物体的全部遗传物质。

entries.definition: The packaged structure in which DNA is carried.
entries.definitionCN: 指承载脱氧核糖核酸的包装结构。

entries.definition: The chemical family to which DNA and RNA belong.
entries.definitionCN: 指脱氧核糖核酸与核糖核酸所属的化学家族。

entries.definition: The twisted two-strand shape of the molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 指该分子两条链缠绕的形状。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations unpack the initials: sugar, nucleus, acid, and the paired strands.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想把首字母展开：糖、核、酸，以及配对的链。

normal.en: The D means one oxygen has been removed from the sugar.
normal.cn: 开头的字母表示糖上少了一个氧原子。

normal.en: The N points to the nucleus, where the acid was first found.
normal.cn: 中间的字母指向细胞核，那种酸最早在那里被发现。

normal.en: The A is acid, from the Latin word for sour.
normal.cn: 末尾的字母是「酸」，出自拉丁语表示「酸」的词。

normal.en: Two strands pair their bases and twist into a double helix.
normal.cn: 两条链让碱基配对，再缠成双螺旋。

normal.en: Recombinant DNA is cut and pasted, like text in an editor.
normal.cn: 重组脱氧核糖核酸被剪切拼接，就像在编辑器里改文本。

abstract.en: An abbreviation is a promise that everyone already knows the long name.
abstract.cn: 缩写是一个约定：大家都已知道那个全称。

abstract.en: A molecule that copies itself is also a message that outlives its sender.
abstract.cn: 一个能自我复制的分子，也是一条比发送者活得更久的讯息。

abstract.en: Saying something is in the DNA means it will be copied whether you like it or not.
abstract.cn: 说某事物「写在基因里」，意思是它不管你喜欢与否都会被复制。

examples.en: DNA was extracted from the bone and compared with a reference sample.
examples.cn: 从骨骼中提取脱氧核糖核酸，并与参考样本比对。

examples.en: Errors copied into DNA can be repaired by the cell's own enzymes.
examples.cn: 复制进脱氧核糖核酸的错误可由细胞自身的酶修复。

examples.en: The company treats careful testing as part of its DNA.
examples.cn: 这家公司把谨慎测试视为自身根本特质的一部分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「地恩埃」——三个字母像双螺旋的三段台阶，记住全称「脱氧核糖核酸」即可

root: 这是缩写，并非词根：全称由「脱氧」「核糖」「核酸」组合，其中「核酸」出自拉丁语 nucleus「核、果核」，「酸」出自拉丁语 acidus「酸的」；缩写于二十世纪中期通用，确切首见时间不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from the molecule and its hereditary role to its sequence, its sample, its metaphorical use, its engineered form, its archival use and its spelled-out name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从分子本身与遗传作用出发，走向序列、样本、比喻用法、工程形式、存档用途，以及展开的全称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit double helix on a lab bench, coloured rungs pairing one by one.
core.cn: 核心意象：实验台上被灯照亮的双螺旋，彩色横档一节节配对。

branches.en: THE NAME AND THE SHAPE: the molecule, and the full chemical name behind the initials.
branches.cn: 名称与形状：分子本身，以及首字母背后的化学全称。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: the material of inheritance, and the base sequence that spells it.
branches.cn: 信息：遗传物质，以及拼出信息的碱基序列。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: a sample taken and compared.
branches.cn: 证据：被采集并比对的样本。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: the copied core of an organization or style.
branches.cn: 比喻：一个组织或风格中被复制的核心。

branches.en: THE TOOL: DNA cut and rejoined, and DNA used as a dense archive.
branches.cn: 工具：被剪切重接的脱氧核糖核酸，以及被当作高密度档案的脱氧核糖核酸。

intro.en: The word is an abbreviation, so its parts are the parts of the full chemical name rather than old roots.
intro.cn: 这是一个缩写，因此它的部件是全称中的化学部件，而不是古老词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes the nucleus and the acid; the sugar and the oxygen prefix belong to modern chemical naming.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语贡献了「核」与「酸」，糖与「脱氧」前缀则属于现代化学命名。

items.example: It gives nucleic, the acid of the nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「核酸」，即细胞核中的酸。

items.example: It forms nucleic from nucleus.
items.exampleCN: 它由「核」构成「核酸的」。

items.example: It gives acid, the final word of the full name.
items.exampleCN: 它构成全称末尾的「酸」。

items.example: It gives the ribo- element.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「核糖」这一成分。

items.example: It marks the difference from the RNA sugar.
items.exampleCN: 它标记与核糖核酸所用糖的差别。

items.example: The initials are read letter by letter.
items.exampleCN: 这三个字母逐字母读出。

items.example: It forms DNase, an enzyme that cuts DNA.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「脱氧核糖核酸酶」。

items.example: It names the twisted shape of the two strands.
items.exampleCN: 它指两条链缠绕的形状。

derivatives.zh: 由缩写加酶名词尾构成，义为「脱氧核糖核酸酶」
由缩写加「以……为基础」成分构成，义为「基于脱氧核糖核酸的」
由缩写加「结合」成分构成，义为「结合脱氧核糖核酸的」
由「线粒体的」与缩写复合而成，义为「线粒体脱氧核糖核酸」
由「重组的」与缩写复合而成，义为「重组脱氧核糖核酸」
由缩写与「指纹分析」复合而成，义为「脱氧核糖核酸指纹分析」

definition_zh: 错综复杂的；繁复精细的；盘根错节的；精巧的
definition_en: having many small parts or connections arranged in a way that is hard to follow
core_image: 老式钟表被打开的瞬间，一层层齿轮彼此咬合，每一枚都牵动另一枚
scene: 老式钟表被打开，里面一层层齿轮彼此咬合，每一枚都牵动另一枚。 Restorers spent weeks on the intricate gearing inside the old clock.
sceneCN: 这里指部件繁多、彼此交错（第 1 个义项：部件彼此咬合的）；句意为修复师花了数周处理这只旧钟表繁复精细的齿轮结构。图中可辨识物件：打开的钟表、层层齿轮、咬合齿纹、放大镜。

pos.zh: 错综复杂的；繁复精细的；盘根错节的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「错综；繁复」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「错综复杂地；精细地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「错综」，较少用
由表示「向外」的前缀加同一拉丁词干构成，义为「解脱；拔出」，是同一词根的相反方向

senses.title: Many interlocking parts
senses.definition: having many parts that depend on one another
senses.definitionCN: 拥有许多相互依赖的部件
senses.example: The engine's intricate parts had to be numbered before it was opened.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机拆开之前，那些彼此咬合的零件都得编号。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to entangle, and this sense keeps the picture of threads crossed over one another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「缠结」，这一义项保留的就是线彼此交叉的画面。

senses.title: A detailed pattern
senses.definition: a design with many fine lines woven together
senses.definitionCN: 由许多细线交织而成的图样
senses.example: The shawl is famous for its intricate border of vines and birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这条披肩以藤鸟交织的繁复花边闻名。
senses.why: The pattern is intricate because the eye must travel along every line.
senses.whyCN: 图案错综，因为眼睛必须沿着每一条线走。

senses.title: Fine details
senses.definition: small features that must be followed one by one
senses.definitionCN: 必须逐一追究的细小特征
senses.example: The agreement is full of intricate details about who pays for what.
senses.exampleCN: 协议里满是关于谁付哪笔钱的繁复细节。
senses.why: Details are intricate when they cannot be understood one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 细节错综，是因为它们无法一件一件地单独理解。

senses.title: A tangled plot
senses.definition: a story whose threads cross and return
senses.definitionCN: 线索彼此交叉又回返的故事
senses.example: The novel's intricate plot keeps three families in view at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说情节错综，同时盯着三个家庭。
senses.why: A plot is intricate when its threads return to the same scene from different sides.
senses.whyCN: 情节错综，是当它的线索从不同方向回到同一场景。

senses.title: Complex machinery
senses.definition: a machine with many small linked mechanisms
senses.definitionCN: 由许多相互连接的小机构组成的机器
senses.example: The loom's intricate mechanism was rebuilt from a single photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 这台织机的复杂机构是凭一张照片重建的。
senses.why: Machinery earns the word when every part seems to be holding another.
senses.whyCN: 当每个部件似乎都在托住另一个，机器就用得上这个词。

senses.title: A complicated problem
senses.definition: a problem with many causes that cannot be separated easily
senses.definitionCN: 原因众多且难以分开的问题
senses.example: Land rights in the valley are intricate, with claims overlapping for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这一河谷的土地权属盘根错节，各方主张重叠了数百年。
senses.why: Problems are intricate when the causes cannot be pulled apart without breaking them.
senses.whyCN: 当原因一拆就断，问题就是盘根错节的。

senses.title: An involved relationship
senses.definition: a relationship with many overlapping obligations
senses.definitionCN: 义务彼此重叠的关系
senses.example: The two firms share an intricate web of suppliers and loans.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司共享一张由供应商与贷款组成的错综网络。
senses.why: Relationships become intricate through obligations that overlap rather than multiply.
senses.whyCN: 关系因义务重叠、而不是数量增多，才变得错综。

senses.title: Fine workmanship
senses.definition: made with delicate, careful work on a small scale
senses.definitionCN: 在小尺度上以细致功夫完成的
senses.example: The intricate carving on the door took a craftsman a whole winter.
senses.exampleCN: 门上精细的雕刻花了工匠一整个冬天。
senses.why: Workmanship is intricate when smallness and care appear together.
senses.whyCN: 当细小与用心同时出现，工艺就是精细的。

intro.en: Intricate comes from Latin intricatus, the past participle of intricare, to entangle, built on in- and tricae, trifles or perplexities. The word entered English through the idea of a knot rather than through that of size, so intricacy is about threads crossing, not merely about many pieces.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 intricatus，是动词 intricare「缠结」的过去分词，由「进入」与 tricae「琐碎、纠葛」构成。它经「打结」的观念而非「数量多」的观念进入英语，所以「错综」讲的是线交叉，而不只是零件多。

items.en: Tricae meant trifles, tricks or perplexities, the stuff that catches a person up.
items.cn: 这个词意为琐事、诡计或纠葛，也就是把人缠住的东西。

items.en: The verb meant to entangle or involve, literally to put someone into the tricae.
items.cn: 该动词意为缠住、卷入，字面就是把人放进纠葛之中。

items.en: The participle described something entangled, and it passed into English as an adjective.
items.cn: 该分词形容被缠住之物，作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: English used it for plots, designs and arguments that are hard to follow.
items.cn: 英语用它指难以追循的情节、图样与论证。

items.en: Craft writing applied it to carving and metalwork of many fine parts.
items.cn: 工艺写作把它用于多细部的雕刻与金工。

items.en: Systems and law gave it new subjects; the relation of English trick to the same Latin word is debated rather than settled.
items.cn: 制度与法律给出新的对象；英语中表示「诡计」的形近词是否同出这一拉丁词，各家有争论而无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the tangle root or looks close; the second names other kinds of complexity. The note also separates intricate from complicated and warns about intrinsic, which looks close but has a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「缠结」词根或形近；第二组指其他「复杂」的说法。这里也把「错综」与「复杂」辨析，并提醒形近的「内在的」一词出自另一词根。

entries.definition: The quality of being entangled or finely detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 指错综或精细的性质。

entries.definition: In a way that is finely woven or detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 指以精细交织的方式。

entries.definition: To free from a tangle; the prefix means out of.
entries.definitionCN: 指从缠结中解脱；前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: To fascinate or to plot secretly; from the same tangle word through French or Italian, though the route is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人着迷或暗中谋划；经法语或意大利语同出这一「缠结」词，具体路径有争论。

entries.definition: Belonging to a thing by its own nature; its root means inward, not entangled.
entries.definitionCN: 指按本性属于某物；其词根意为「向内」，与「缠结」无关。

entries.definition: Made hard to understand by many parts folded together; it stresses difficulty rather than fine work.
entries.definitionCN: 指因许多部分折在一起而难懂；强调的是难，而非精细。

entries.definition: Having parts that are closely connected, often as a neutral description.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分紧密相连，常为中性描述。

entries.definition: Worked out with many carefully arranged details.
entries.definitionCN: 指经过精心安排、细节繁多。

entries.definition: Showing many small facts, without implying that they interlock.
entries.definitionCN: 指呈现许多细小事实，不暗示彼此咬合。

entries.definition: Twisted and hard to follow, often with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 指曲折难循，常含贬义。

entries.definition: Having many parts or connections, sometimes hard to explain.
entries.definitionCN: 指部分或关联很多，有时难以说明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the opened clock, the vine border, the tangled land claims and the winter of carving.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用打开的钟表、藤蔓花边、缠结的土地主张与雕了一冬的门。

normal.en: Intricate things are not just many; they are tied to one another.
normal.cn: 错综之物不只是多，而是彼此拴在一起。

normal.en: Turn one gear and the next answers, which is what makes the whole thing intricate.
normal.cn: 转动一枚齿轮，下一枚就应声而动，这才让整体错综。

normal.en: A shawl's border is intricate because the vines hold the birds.
normal.cn: 披肩花边错综，是因为藤蔓把鸟扣在了一起。

normal.en: Intricate details are the ones you must follow in order, not just count.
normal.cn: 繁复的细节要按顺序追究，而不只是数一数。

normal.en: Intricate praises the weaving; complicated complains about the difficulty.
normal.cn: 「错综」在称许织法，「复杂」在抱怨难度。

abstract.en: A tangle is order that has not yet been read.
abstract.cn: 缠结是尚未被读懂的秩序。

abstract.en: The same root gives extricate, because every knot also implies a way out.
abstract.cn: 同一词根给出「解脱」，因为每个结都暗示着一条出路。

abstract.en: What is intricate rewards patience and punishes haste, which is why it survives in craft.
abstract.cn: 错综之物奖赏耐心、惩罚急躁，所以它在工艺里留了下来。

examples.en: The carpet's intricate pattern was copied from a sixteenth-century drawing.
examples.cn: 这块地毯的繁复图案摹自一幅十六世纪的图样。

examples.en: The case involves an intricate set of overlapping contracts.
examples.cn: 该案涉及一组盘根错节、彼此重叠的合同。

examples.en: Restorers spent weeks on the intricate gearing inside the old clock.
examples.cn: 修复师花了数周处理这只旧钟表繁复精细的齿轮结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因吹卡特」：线一「缠」就成结，结里又有结，越看越细，越细越难拆

root: 源于拉丁语表示「琐事、纠葛」的名词，其动词义为「缠住、使卷入」，过去分词进入英语作形容词。同族有表示「错综」的名词与表示「解脱」的动词；形近而表示「内在的」的词出自表示「向内」的另一词根。英语中表示「诡计」的词是否同出这一拉丁词，各家有争论而无定论。十五世纪进入英语；各技术用法首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the tangle: interlocking parts, a woven pattern, fine details, a tangled plot, complex machinery, a problem with many causes, an overlapped relationship, and delicate workmanship.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「缠结」展开：彼此咬合的部件、交织的图案、繁复细节、错综情节、复杂机械、多因问题、重叠的关系与精细工艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the clock opens and every gear is held by the teeth of the next one.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟表打开，每一枚齿轮都被下一枚的齿咬住。

branches.en: THE INTERLOCKED MACHINE: parts that hold one another, from clocks to looms.
branches.cn: 咬合的机器：彼此扣住的部件，从钟表到织机。

branches.en: THE FINE HAND: woven patterns and carving that reward close looking.
branches.cn: 精细的手：值得细看的织纹与雕刻。

branches.en: THE DETAILS IN ORDER: small features that must be followed one by one.
branches.cn: 按序的细节：必须逐一追究的细小特征。

branches.en: THE RETURNING PLOT: threads that cross and come back to the same scene.
branches.cn: 回返的情节：交叉之后又回到同一场景的线索。

branches.en: THE KNOTTED WORLD: problems and relationships whose causes overlap.
branches.cn: 打结的世界：原因彼此重叠的问题与关系。

intro.en: Intricate is a Latin tangle verb with a participle ending; its family covers the noun of tangling and the verb of getting free.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「缠结」动词加分词词尾；词族覆盖「缠结」的名词与「解脱」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tricae and intricare supply the knot, and the participle intricatus gives the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「纠葛」与「缠住」提供那个结，分词给出英语形容词。

items.example: The knot at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是词中央的那个结。

items.example: It marks putting someone into the tangle.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「把人放进缠结」。

items.example: The verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是形容词背后的动词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective directly.
items.exampleCN: 它直接给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the participle shape.
items.exampleCN: 它标出分词的形态。

items.example: It forms intricacy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「错综」。

items.example: It forms intricately.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「错综地」。

items.example: It forms extricate, the way out of the tangle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「解脱」，即从缠结里出来的路。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「错综；繁复」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「错综复杂地」
由表示「向外」的前缀加同一拉丁词干构成，义为「解脱」

definition_zh: 草地；草原；以草本植物为主的土地；牧场
definition_en: land covered mainly by grasses, with few or no trees
core_image: 一片望不到边的草地，草根在土里织成厚垫，地面上几乎看不到树
scene: 草根在土中织成厚厚一层垫子，使这片草原熬过几乎无雨的一年。 Deep roots let this grassland survive a year of almost no rain.
sceneCN: 这里 grassland 指「以草本植物为主的土地」（第 1 个义项：草占优势、乔木稀少的植被覆盖）；句意为深长的草根让这片草原熬过几乎无雨的一年。图中可辨识物件：草穗、交错的根系、干裂表土、远处低平的地平线。

pos.zh: 草地；草原；牧场（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 草；在……上种草
长满草的；草色的
草根；基层的（词义已转移）

senses.title: Land dominated by grass
senses.definition: a tract of ground whose main plant cover is grasses, with trees absent or too few to form a canopy
senses.definitionCN: 主要植物覆盖为草、乔木缺失或稀少到无法形成树冠的一片土地
senses.example: Deep roots let this grassland survive a year of almost no rain.
senses.exampleCN: 深长的草根让这片草原熬过几乎无雨的一年。
senses.why: grass plus land names ground by its dominant plant, exactly as woodland is named by trees.
senses.whyCN: grass 加 land 按优势植物给土地命名，正如 woodland 按树命名。

senses.title: Pasture and rangeland
senses.definition: grassland used for grazing livestock, whether sown or natural
senses.definitionCN: 用于放牧家畜的草地，无论人工播种还是天然
senses.example: The farm keeps two hundred ewes on the lower grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 农场在低处草地养着两百只母羊。
senses.why: once grass is harvested by animals rather than by machines, the word takes on the working sense of pasture.
senses.whyCN: 当草由牲畜而非机器收获，这个词就带上了「牧场」这一作业含义。

senses.title: The temperate grassland biome
senses.definition: the mid-latitude grass biome with hot summers, cold winters and too little rain for forest, as prairie, steppe or pampas
senses.definitionCN: 中纬度草地生物群系，夏热冬冷、降水不足以成林，如北美草原、干草原与潘帕斯
senses.example: Temperate grassland stores much of its carbon below ground.
senses.exampleCN: 温带草原把大部分碳储在地下。
senses.why: biogeography groups all such regions into one biome, so grassland becomes a global class rather than a local field.
senses.whyCN: 生物地理学把这类地区归为一个生物群系，于是 grassland 从本地田块变成全球类别。

senses.title: Tropical grassland with scattered trees
senses.definition: the tropical grass formation with a dry season and scattered drought-resistant trees, usually called savanna
senses.definitionCN: 有旱季、散生耐旱乔木的热带草地，通常称 savanna
senses.example: Tropical grassland turns brown within weeks of the last rain.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一场雨过后几周，热带草原就变成褐色。
senses.why: the same cover word serves the tropics, where grass is still dominant even when trees are present.
senses.whyCN: 同一个覆盖词也适用于热带：即使有树，草仍占优势。

senses.title: Grassland ecosystem services
senses.definition: the soil formation, water regulation and carbon storage that grass cover provides
senses.definitionCN: 草覆盖所提供的地壤形成、水分调节与碳储存
senses.example: Grassland holds water that bare fields would shed.
senses.exampleCN: 草地能蓄住裸地会流走的水。
senses.why: the dense root mat makes grassland a service provider, not merely a place where grass grows.
senses.whyCN: 密集根垫使草地成为服务提供者，而不只是长草的地方。

senses.title: Grassland restoration
senses.definition: the deliberate return of arable or degraded land to species-rich grass cover
senses.definitionCN: 有意把耕地或退化地恢复为物种丰富的草覆盖
senses.example: Sowing local seed is the first step in grassland restoration.
senses.exampleCN: 播下本地种子是草地恢复的第一步。
senses.why: conservation turned the cover word into a target: what was ploughed can be made grassland again.
senses.whyCN: 保护工作把这个覆盖词变成目标：被犁过的地可以重新变回草地。

senses.title: A land-cover class
senses.titleCN: 土地覆盖分类中的草地类
senses.definition: a mapped category for ground whose dominant cover is grass, distinct from crop and shrub classes
senses.definitionCN: 优势覆盖为草、与作物类和灌丛类相区别的制图类别
senses.example: The national map counts grassland and cropland separately.
senses.exampleCN: 全国地图把草地与耕地分开统计。
senses.why: mapping needs thresholds, so a loose botanical description becomes a labelled class with percentage rules.
senses.whyCN: 制图需要阈值，于是宽松的植物描述变成带百分比规则的标签类别。

senses.title: Managed turf and amenity grass
senses.titleCN: 人工管理的草坪与运动场草
senses.definition: grass kept short by mowing and irrigation for lawns, parks and sports pitches
senses.definitionCN: 通过修剪与灌溉保持低矮、用于草坪、公园与运动场的草
senses.example: The stadium grassland is mown three times a week.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场的草坪每周修剪三次。
senses.why: the same cover word extends to the most artificial grass of all, where management replaces climate.
senses.whyCN: 同一个覆盖词也延伸到最人工的草地：管理取代了气候。

intro.en: Grassland is a native English compound of grass and land; grass is Germanic and has a known Indo-European link to 'grow, green'.
intro.cn: grassland 是 grass 与 land 构成的英语本族复合词；grass 属日耳曼语，其印欧语联系「生长、绿色」较为可信。

items.en: Græs meant 'grass, herb'. It descends from Germanic *grasam, connected by the usual sound laws to the root that also gives grow and green.
items.cn: græs 意为「草、草本」。它来自日耳曼语 *grasam，按常规音变可联系到也产生 grow 与 green 的词根。

items.en: Land 'ground, territory' is Germanic *landam; its pre-Germanic origin is uncertain and any deeper form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: land「土地、领土」是日耳曼语 *landam；其在日耳曼语之前的来源不确定，更深形式均属重构。

items.en: The compound grassland is recorded in Middle English, naming ground grown to grass rather than the grass itself.
items.cn: 复合词 grassland 见于中古英语，指长草的地面，而非草本身。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century ecology fixed grassland as a biome and land-cover class beside forest and desert.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的生态学把 grassland 固定为与森林、荒漠并列的生物群系与覆盖类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation of grassland is not securely dated, and land's pre-Germanic root remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：grassland 的最早书证年代不可靠，land 的日耳曼语之前词根仍无定论。

note.en: Group one separates the parallel -land cover compounds; group two separates the working and regional words for grass cover.
note.cn: 第一组区分并列的 -land 覆盖复合词；第二组区分草地的作业词与地区词。

entries.definition: Land covered by trees; it is the cover class above grassland in the height ladder.
entries.definitionCN: 树木覆盖的土地；在高度阶梯上位于草地之上。

entries.definition: Land covered by low woody plants; it often replaces grassland when grazing or fire changes.
entries.definitionCN: 低矮木本植物覆盖的土地；放牧或火改变时，它常取代草地。

entries.definition: Land saturated or covered by water; the limiting factor is water, not plant form.
entries.definitionCN: 被水饱和或覆盖的土地；限制因子是水，而非植物形态。

entries.definition: Land sown to crops and harvested annually; it is a land-use class rather than a natural cover.
entries.definitionCN: 播种作物并每年收获的土地；是土地利用类别，而非自然覆盖。

entries.definition: Grassland managed for livestock; it stresses use, while grassland stresses cover.
entries.definitionCN: 为家畜经营的地；强调用途，而 grassland 强调覆盖。

entries.definition: Grassland kept for hay or left unmown for flowers, usually moist and small-scale.
entries.definitionCN: 用于制干草或任其开花不割的草地，通常湿润且面积较小。

entries.definition: The vast short-grass plain of Eurasia; a regional name for temperate grassland.
entries.definitionCN: 欧亚大陆广阔的短草平原；温带草原的地区名称。

entries.definition: Unenclosed land grazed extensively, including grass, shrub and open forest; broader than grassland.
entries.definitionCN: 广泛放牧的未围封土地，含草地、灌丛与疏林；比 grassland 宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: grass + land: land whose crop is grass.
normal.cn: grass + land：以草为作物的土地。

normal.en: The family runs grass, grassy, grassland, greensward.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 grass、grassy、grassland、greensward。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: temperate grassland, tropical grassland, native grassland, grassland restoration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：温带草原、热带草原、原生草地、草地恢复。

normal.en: The world's regional names: prairie, steppe, pampas, savanna.
normal.cn: 世界各地的地区名称：prairie、steppe、pampas、savanna。

normal.en: The image is a thick mat of roots holding soil under a flat sea of grass.
normal.cn: 意象是草海之下，一层厚根垫把土壤抓住。

abstract.en: Think of a carpet that repairs itself whenever it is cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被剪后能自行修补的地毯。

abstract.en: Think of a community that lives mostly underground and sends up thin green antennae.
abstract.cn: 想象一个多数成员住在地下、只伸出细绿触角的群落。

abstract.en: Think of a fire that clears the roof but leaves the floor intact.
abstract.cn: 想象一场火清掉了屋顶，却让地板完好。

examples.en: Ploughing up the grassland released carbon that had taken centuries to store.
examples.cn: 犁开草地释放了储存数百年之久的碳。

examples.en: The grassland bird needs grass tall enough to hide its nest.
examples.cn: 草原鸟类需要足够高的草来藏巢。

examples.en: Grazing at the right season keeps the grassland from scrubbing over.
examples.cn: 在合适季节放牧，可以防止草地被灌丛侵占。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「grass（草）+ land（土地）」——长草的土地 → 草地、草原

root: grass（古英语 græs「草」，日耳曼语 *grasam，与 grow/green 同根）+ land（古英语 land「土地」，日耳曼语 *landam）。英语复合词，无拉丁成分；land 的更深词源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from simple grass cover to grazing land, global biome, ecosystem service, restoration target and finally mown turf.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从简单的草覆盖，走向放牧地、全球生物群系、生态服务、恢复目标，最后到修剪的草坪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat sea of grass over a dense mat of roots.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片平展的草海，下面是一层密集的根垫。

branches.en: COVER: grass dominance defines the ground, whether seen in the field or on a map.
branches.cn: 覆盖：草占优势定义这块地，无论在地头还是在图上。

branches.en: USE: animals harvest the grass, and the cover becomes pasture.
branches.cn: 用途：牲畜收获草，覆盖便成为牧场。

branches.en: CLIMATE: the same formation appears as temperate prairie or tropical savanna.
branches.cn: 气候：同一群系表现为温带草原或热带草原。

branches.en: VALUE: roots build soil and hold water, and lost grass can be restored.
branches.cn: 价值：根建造土壤、蓄住水，失去的草可以恢复。

branches.en: ARTIFICE: mowing and irrigation push the cover to its most managed form.
branches.cn: 人工：修剪与灌溉把覆盖推到最受管理的形态。

intro.en: Grassland is a native two-word compound; its family is built by suffixes added to grass rather than by prefixes.
intro.cn: grassland 是本族两词复合；其词族主要靠在 grass 上加后缀构成，而非加前缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: grass and land are Germanic, so no Latin relatives are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁语：grass 与 land 属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: The grass was grazed down to the root.
items.exampleCN: 草被啃到根部。

items.example: The land lies low and wet.
items.exampleCN: 这块地低洼潮湿。

items.example: The grassland runs to the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 草地一直延伸到地平线。

items.example: A grassy bank borders the stream.
items.exampleCN: 一道长草的岸贴着溪流。

items.example: The grassed bund held the water.
items.exampleCN: 播过草的土埂拦住了水。

items.example: Overgrazing left a grassless slope.
items.exampleCN: 过牧留下了一片无草的坡。

items.meaning: the ordinary level of an organization
items.meaningCN: 基层；草根层（词义已转移）
items.example: The movement began at the grassroot level.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动从基层开始。

items.example: Grass-fed cattle need wide grassland.
items.exampleCN: 草饲牛需要宽阔的草地。

definition_zh: 干扰；扰动；扰乱；（生态）扰动事件
definition_en: the act of interrupting order or peace, and in ecology any event that changes the structure of a habitat
core_image: 平静的湖面被一块落石砸出层层波纹，水下的水草被搅得东倒西歪
scene: 深夜的居民楼里，楼上的电钻声断断续续响了两个小时，楼下的老人终于上楼敲门。 The drilling upstairs caused a serious disturbance that brought the neighbours to the door.
sceneCN: 这里 disturbance 指「扰人安宁的行为」（第 1 个义项：打断他人平静与正常秩序的事件）；句意：楼上的电钻造成严重扰民，把邻居引到了门口。图中可辨识物件：居民楼走廊、电钻、敲门的手、墙上的挂钟。

pos.zh: 干扰；扰动；扰乱；骚乱；心神不安

derivatives.zh: 打扰；扰乱；搅动
受扰的；不安的
令人不安的
未受干扰的

senses.title: Breaking someone's peace
senses.titleCN: 扰人安宁：打断他人的平静
senses.definition: an act that interrupts another person's quiet or normal activity
senses.definitionCN: 打断他人安静或正常活动的行为
senses.example: The loud music at midnight was a disturbance for the whole block.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜的高声音乐扰了整条街。
senses.why: dis- here works as 'apart, in different directions' and turbare means to throw into disorder, so the act scatters a settled state.
senses.whyCN: dis- 在此表「散开、朝不同方向」，turbare 意为「搅乱」，因此这个行为把安定的状态打散。

senses.title: An ecological event that reshapes habitat
senses.titleCN: 生态扰动：重塑生境的事件
senses.definition: in ecology, an event such as fire, storm or grazing that changes the structure of an habitat
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指火灾、风暴、放牧等改变生境结构的事件
senses.example: A single windstorm was the disturbance that opened the forest floor to light.
senses.exampleCN: 一场风灾就是那次让林下见到阳光的扰动。
senses.why: ecology needed a neutral word for any event that breaks the existing order, so the everyday sense was extended.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要一个中性词来指任何打破既有秩序的事件，于是日常义被扩展过去。

senses.title: A disruption of normal function
senses.titleCN: 功能紊乱：正常运作被打断
senses.definition: an interruption of a bodily or mechanical function
senses.definitionCN: 身体或机械功能的正常运作被打断
senses.example: Long shift work causes a disturbance of the sleep cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 长期轮班工作会造成睡眠周期的紊乱。
senses.why: the same scattering applies to internal rhythms: what ran evenly now runs out of step.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「打散」也适用于内部节律：原本均匀运转的东西现在乱了拍子。

senses.title: Public disorder or a riot
senses.definition: a public outbreak of disorder, often involving a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 公共秩序失控的事件，常涉及人群聚集
senses.example: Troops were called in after a disturbance broke out in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 市场爆发骚乱后，军队被调来。
senses.why: when many people are thrown out of order at once, the individual interruption becomes a collective event.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时被抛离秩序，个体的打扰就变成集体事件。

senses.title: A deviation from equilibrium
senses.titleCN: 偏离平衡：系统上的扰动
senses.definition: a small push that moves a system away from its equilibrium state
senses.definitionCN: 使系统离开平衡态的小幅推动
senses.example: Engineers applied a small disturbance to test the control system.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师施加一个小扰动来测试控制系统。
senses.why: physics formalised the everyday word: any nudge that displaces a system counts, however small.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个日常词形式化：任何使系统偏离的推动都算，无论多小。

senses.title: A nuisance in law
senses.definition: in law, an interference with another person's quiet enjoyment of property
senses.definitionCN: 法律上对他人安静享用其财产权的妨害
senses.example: The factory was sued for disturbance caused by night-time noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂因夜间噪声造成的妨害被起诉。
senses.why: legal usage fixes the loose everyday sense into a claimable harm with a measurable effect.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把松散的日常义固定为可主张、可衡量的损害。

senses.title: A sudden shift in community structure
senses.titleCN: 群落突变：组成与结构骤变
senses.definition: a change that alters the species composition or physical structure of a community
senses.definitionCN: 改变群落物种组成或物理结构的变动
senses.example: The disturbance removed the dominant shrub and let grasses invade.
senses.exampleCN: 这次扰动除去了优势灌木，让草本入侵。
senses.why: the event matters less than its result: what was dominant loses its place, and the whole assembly reorganises.
senses.whyCN: 事件本身不如其结果重要：原来的优势者失去位置，整个组合重新编排。

senses.title: Inner unease in literary use
senses.definition: a state of mental or emotional unsettledness
senses.definitionCN: 精神或情绪上不安定的状态
senses.example: A strange disturbance in her chest kept her from sleeping.
senses.exampleCN: 胸口一种莫名的扰动让她睡不着。
senses.why: the outer scattering is turned inward, so the word can name a mind that will not stay still.
senses.whyCN: 外在的打散转向内部，于是这个词能指一个静不下来的心。

intro.en: Disturbance comes through Old French from Latin disturbare 'to throw into disorder', built on dis- and turbare 'to disturb', itself from turba 'turmoil, crowd'. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: disturbance 经古法语出自拉丁 disturbare「搅乱」，由 dis- 与 turbare「搅动」构成，后者源自 turba「骚动、人群」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Turba named a crowd or a turmoil. Its further origin is uncertain; any older form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: turba 指人群或骚动；其更早来源不确定，凡为它引出的更古形式均属重构形式。

items.en: The verb turbare meant 'to throw into confusion, to agitate', and gave English turbulent and disturb.
items.cn: 动词 turbare 意为「搅乱、使动荡」，并衍生英语 turbulent 与 disturb。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus turbare produced disturbare 'to scatter, to throw into disorder'.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 turbare 构成 disturbare「打散、使混乱」。

items.en: Old French destourber carried the word north, and English took it in the fourteenth century as disturben.
items.cn: 古法语 destourber 把词带到北方，英语于 14 世纪以 disturben 形式吸收。

items.en: The noun disturbance is recorded from the fourteenth century; the ecological sense is a twentieth-century extension.
items.cn: 名词 disturbance 自 14 世纪有记录；生态义是 20 世纪的扩展。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology made disturbance a technical term for any event that disrupts a community, with no implication of harm.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学把 disturbance 变成术语，指任何打断群落的事件，并不含「有害」之意。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built on the same Latin turbare; group two holds near meanings that stress a different part of the event.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 turbare 的形近词；第二组是侧重事件不同方面的近义词。

entries.definition: To break someone's peace or to upset a process. Disturbance is the event or state that results.
entries.definitionCN: 指打扰他人安宁或扰乱某一过程；disturbance 是它造成的事件或状态。

entries.definition: Describing someone or something already affected; it looks at the receiver, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 形容已受影响的人或物；着眼点在承受者，而不在事件。

entries.definition: From the same turbare, but it names ongoing swirling motion, as in turbulent water or times.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 turbare，但指持续翻滚的流动，如湍流或动荡的时代。

entries.definition: The state of swirling disorder, especially in air or water. It is a condition, not a single event.
entries.definitionCN: 指翻腾的紊乱状态，尤指气流或水流；是一种状态，不是单个事件。

entries.definition: A slight push away from a normal path, used in physics and mathematics; it is usually smaller and more precise than disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 指使系统偏离正常轨迹的轻微推动，用于物理与数学；通常比 disturbance 更小、更精确。

entries.definition: A temporary stop in speech, work or supply. It marks a pause, not a reshaping of structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指话语、工作或供应的暂时中断；强调停顿，而非结构被重塑。

entries.definition: A big, often social or political, shaking up. It implies deep change, while disturbance can be minor.
entries.definitionCN: 指大规模、常为社会或政治的剧变；暗含深层改变，而 disturbance 可以是轻微的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' + turbare 'to stir up': the settled state is stirred apart.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」+ turbare「搅动」：安定的状态被搅散。

normal.en: The family runs disturb, disturbance, disturbed, disturbing, turbulent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 disturb、disturbance、disturbed、disturbing、turbulent。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: ecological disturbance, human disturbance, cause a disturbance, disturbance regime.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：生态扰动、人为干扰、引起骚动、扰动格局。

normal.en: Ecology treats it as neutral: fire and storms are disturbances, not disasters.
normal.cn: 生态学把它当中性词：火灾与风暴是扰动，并不等于灾难。

normal.en: Physics pairs it with equilibrium: a small push away from rest.
normal.cn: 物理学把它与平衡配对：使其离开静止的小幅推动。

abstract.en: Picture a still pond hit by one stone: rings spread and the bottom mud lifts.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头砸进静水：涟漪散开，底部泥被扬起。

abstract.en: Picture a neatly stacked woodpile knocked over by a passing cart.
abstract.cn: 想象码得整齐的柴堆被路过的车撞倒。

abstract.en: Picture a sleeper woken by a door slamming in the next room.
abstract.cn: 想象隔壁关门声把睡着的人惊醒。

examples.en: A hurricane is a natural disturbance that can reset forest succession.
examples.cn: 飓风是一种自然扰动，能让森林演替重新开始。

examples.en: Even low levels of human disturbance can drive nesting birds away.
examples.cn: 即使轻度的人为干扰也能把筑巢的鸟赶走。

examples.en: The patient reported a disturbance in his sense of balance.
examples.cn: 病人诉说平衡感出现了紊乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「的士（dis）搅土（turb）→ 平静的地面被车轮搅乱」——打断秩序、搅乱生境 → 干扰、扰动

root: 拉丁 dis-「分开」+ turbare「搅动」，源自 turba「骚动、人群」（turba 更早来源不确定）→ disturbare「搅乱」；经古法语进入英语，生态学术语义为 20 世纪扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something settled is stirred apart, whether that is a neighbour's quiet, a forest floor, a sleep rhythm, a crowd, an equilibrium, a legal right, a community or a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：原本安定的东西被搅散，对象可以是邻居的安宁、林地、睡眠节律、人群、平衡态、法定权利、群落或心绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into still water, scattering the settled surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头砸入静水，把安定的水面打散。

branches.en: SOCIAL SURFACE: a person's peace or a crowd's order is the first thing disturbed.
branches.cn: 社会表面：最先被扰的是个人的安宁或人群的秩序。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL RESET: fire, wind or grazing rewrites the community's structure.
branches.cn: 生态重置：火、风或放牧改写群落结构。

branches.en: INNER RHYTHM: a body function or a mind falls out of step.
branches.cn: 内在节律：身体功能或心绪乱了拍子。

branches.en: EQUILIBRIUM PUSH: in physics even a tiny nudge counts as a disturbance.
branches.cn: 平衡推动：在物理中，哪怕极小的推动也算扰动。

branches.en: LEGAL CLAIM: the everyday nuisance becomes a harm that can be sued for.
branches.cn: 法律主张：日常的妨害变成可诉的损害。

intro.en: The noun is a Latin verb stem with the noun ending -ance; the prefix dis- keeps its older sense of 'apart'.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁动词词干加名词词尾 -ance；前缀 dis- 保留较古的「分开」义。

latinIntro.en: Latin turbare yields disturb, disturbance, turbulent, turbulence and perturb; turba itself gives the rare adjective turbid.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 turbare 衍生 disturb、disturbance、turbulent、turbulence 与 perturb；turba 本身还给出罕用的形容词 turbid。

items.meaning: the state or event of being thrown into disorder
items.example: The survey recorded every disturbance in the plot.
items.exampleCN: 调查记录了样地里的每一次扰动。

items.example: Do not disturb the nesting birds.
items.exampleCN: 不要打扰筑巢的鸟。

items.example: The disturbed soil sprouted weeds first.
items.exampleCN: 受扰的土壤先长出了杂草。

items.example: The survey found a disturbing decline in insects.
items.exampleCN: 调查发现昆虫数量下降，令人不安。

items.example: The core sample came from an undisturbed layer.
items.exampleCN: 这份岩芯取自未受扰动的层位。

items.example: Turbulent air shook the aircraft.
items.exampleCN: 湍流空气使飞机颠簸。

items.example: The aircraft hit turbulence over the mountains.
items.exampleCN: 飞机在山地上空遇到湍流。

items.meaning: to disturb greatly; to displace slightly
items.example: The moon perturbs the planet's orbit.
items.exampleCN: 月球使这颗行星的轨道发生偏离。

definition_zh: 构成；占（比例）；编造；化妆；和解；补足；凑齐；补做；铺床；排版
definition_en: to form a whole, to invent something untrue, to put on cosmetics, to become friendly again, or to supply what is missing
core_image: 一桌散落的零件被逐件拼回，最后拼成一台完整的机器
scene: 桌上散着一堆零件，工人一件件拾起拼装，最后拼成一台整机。 Ten parts make up the whole device.
sceneCN: 这里指零件合起来构成整台装置（第 1 个义项：构成整体）；句意为十个零件构成了整台装置。图中可辨识物件：零件、桌面、装好的机器。

pos.zh: 动词短语：构成；编造；化妆；和解
固定搭配：补足；凑齐

derivatives.zh: 由古英语「塑造、建造」动词而来，义为「做；使成为」
由该短语连写而成的名词，义为「化妆品；构成」
由该动词加表示施事者的名词尾构成，义为「制造者」
由「再」前缀加该动词构成，义为「重做；翻拍」
由该动词加名词尾构成，义为「制作；形成过程」

senses.title: To form a whole
senses.definition: to combine into a complete whole
senses.definitionCN: 合起来成为一个完整的整体
senses.example: Ten parts make up the whole device.
senses.exampleCN: 十个零件构成了整台装置。
senses.why: This is the oldest figurative sense: the parts, taken together, are the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的引申义：各部分合起来就是整体。

senses.title: To account for a share
senses.definition: to form a specified part of a total, often with a fraction or percentage
senses.definitionCN: 构成总量中的某一份额，常与分数或百分比连用
senses.example: Women make up half of the workforce in this sector.
senses.exampleCN: 在这一行业，女性占劳动力的一半。
senses.why: A share is a whole seen from inside, so the same verb serves counting and proportion.
senses.whyCN: 份额是从内部看的整体，因此同一动词兼管计数与比例。

senses.title: To invent something false
senses.definition: to create an untrue story or excuse
senses.definitionCN: 捏造不真实的故事或借口
senses.example: Children often make up a story when they are late.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子迟到时常常编一个故事。
senses.why: The invented thing is made as if assembled, which is how the verb slides from building to fabricating.
senses.whyCN: 编造之物仿佛被拼装出来，动词便从「建造」滑向「捏造」。

senses.title: To apply cosmetics
senses.definition: to put on cosmetics or to prepare an actor's face
senses.definitionCN: 涂抹化妆品，或为演员上妆
senses.example: The actors make up before every evening show.
senses.exampleCN: 演员每场晚场演出前都要化妆。
senses.why: Here the object is a face, and the verb means to build a surface appearance.
senses.whyCN: 这里对象是脸，动词意为「造出一层表面」。

senses.title: To become friendly again
senses.definition: to end a quarrel and become friends again
senses.definitionCN: 结束争吵并重新和好
senses.example: The two neighbours make up after every quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 这两位邻居每次争吵后都会和好。
senses.why: The image is repairing a broken whole, which links this sense to the first one.
senses.whyCN: 意象是修补破碎的整体，与第一个义项相连。

senses.title: To supply what is missing
senses.definition: to add what is needed to reach a required amount
senses.definitionCN: 添上所缺部分以达到所需数量
senses.example: A second grant will make up the shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 第二笔拨款将补足缺口。
senses.why: The missing amount is treated as a gap to be filled, so the verb keeps its building image.
senses.whyCN: 缺少的数额被当作待填的缺口，动词保留其建造意象。

senses.title: To assemble a group
senses.definition: to gather enough people or things to form a group
senses.definitionCN: 凑够人或物以组成一个团体
senses.example: We can make up a team from the volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以从志愿者中凑出一支队伍。
senses.why: This sense is close to the whole-forming one, but the emphasis is on gathering rather than resulting.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项接近「构成整体」，但重点在收集而非结果。

senses.title: To do missed work
senses.definition: to complete work or a test that was missed
senses.definitionCN: 完成错过的功课或考试
senses.example: Students can make up the missed test on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 学生可以在星期五补做错过的考试。
senses.why: The missed task is the gap, and the verb fills it, as in the compensation sense.
senses.whyCN: 错过的任务就是缺口，动词把它填上，与补偿义同理。

senses.title: To prepare a bed
senses.definition: to arrange a bed for use, especially in a hotel
senses.definitionCN: 把床铺整理好以供使用，尤指旅馆
senses.example: The staff make up the beds each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员每天早上整理床铺。
senses.why: Making a bed is literally assembling layers, which is why this sense survives in housekeeping.
senses.whyCN: 铺床字面上就是逐层拼装，因此这一义项保留在客房服务里。

senses.title: To lay out a printed page
senses.definition: in printing, to arrange text and images into a page
senses.definitionCN: 印刷中将文字与图像拼排成一页
senses.example: The editor will make up the front page tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑今晚会拼排头版。
senses.why: The trade sense treats a page as a whole assembled from blocks, the same pattern as the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 行业义把一页看作由版块拼成的整体，与第一个义项同一模式。

intro.en: Make is an Old English verb, macian, to form or construct, from a Germanic root reconstructed as makōjan. Up is the Old English adverb upp. The two-word verb is English, and its many senses grew in the modern period; first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: make 是古英语动词 macian，意为「塑造、建造」，出自日耳曼语重构词根；up 是古英语副词 upp。两词组合的动词属英语，众多义项在近代发展出来，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Macian meant to form, build or construct, and it was already used for both objects and arrangements.
items.cn: macian 意为「塑造、建造」，当时已用于实物与安排。

items.en: The reconstructed root makōjan underlies Dutch maken and German machen.
items.cn: 重构词根也是荷兰语与德语同义词的来源。

items.en: Upp is the adverb meaning upward, preserves the picture of completing an action.
items.cn: upp 是表示「向上」的副词，保留「把动作做完」的画面。

items.en: The combination make up appears in the early modern period with the sense of completing or assembling.
items.cn: 组合形式在近代早期出现，带「完成、拼合」之义。

items.en: Cosmetics, reconciliation, compensation and printing senses all develop later; exact dates are approximate.
items.cn: 化妆、和解、补偿与排版诸义都更晚出现，确切年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the verb or the spelling and changes the particle; the second group holds verbs that cover one of the many senses.
note.cn: 第一组共用该动词或同一拼写而更换小品词；第二组是分别覆盖某一义项的动词。

entries.definition: The extra for marks compensation for a loss, while bare make up only fills a gap.
entries.definitionCN: 多出的介词标出对损失的补偿，单独的短语只表示填补缺口。

entries.definition: It means to see, hear or understand with difficulty, or to write a cheque.
entries.definitionCN: 意为费力地看清、听清或理解，也指开票据。

entries.definition: It means to hurry away, often after taking something.
entries.definitionCN: 意为匆匆离开，常指拿了东西就走。

entries.definition: The single word is a noun for cosmetics or composition, never a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 连写的单词是名词，指化妆品或构成，不能作动词。

entries.definition: It states that parts form a whole, chiefly in formal or legal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 它说明部分构成整体，多见于正式或法律文字。

entries.definition: It names the whole and its parts, with the whole as subject.
entries.definitionCN: 它点出整体与部分，主语是整体。

entries.definition: It covers the false-story sense and also genuine creation.
entries.definitionCN: 它覆盖编造故事一义，也指真正的发明。

entries.definition: It is the formal verb for ending a quarrel, where make up is conversational.
entries.definitionCN: 它是结束争吵的正式说法，而本短语偏口语。

normalIntro.en: The normal associations use the real Old English pair, the particle contrast and the four core layers.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的古英语两词、小品词对比与四层核心义。

normal.en: Macian is to build, so the first sense is parts forming a whole.
normal.cn: 古英语动词意为「建造」，所以第一义是部分构成整体。

normal.en: Up completes the action, which is why the phrase also means filling a gap.
normal.cn: up 表示做完，因此短语也有「填上缺口」之义。

normal.en: The same verb covers counting a share and inventing a story.
normal.cn: 同一动词既管计数份额，也管编造故事。

normal.en: Cosmetics, reconciliation and printing are later layers on the same image.
normal.cn: 化妆、和解与排版都是同一意象上较晚的层次。

normal.en: The single-word noun is written solid, the verb stays two words.
normal.cn: 连写的是名词，动词保持两词。

abstract.en: Like scattered parts gathered on one table until a machine stands complete.
abstract.cn: 像散落零件在桌上被逐件拾起，直到整机立起来。

abstract.en: Like a torn page mended with tape, the break closed and the whole readable again.
abstract.cn: 像撕破的书页用胶带补好，裂口合上，整页又能读。

abstract.en: Like a face painted for the stage, a surface built layer by layer.
abstract.cn: 像为登台而化的妆，一层层造出表面。

examples.en: Five departments make up the research division.
examples.cn: 五个部门构成了这个研究分部。

examples.en: Imports make up a third of the country's food supply.
examples.cn: 进口占该国食品供应的三分之一。

examples.en: The two brothers make up soon after every argument.
examples.cn: 两兄弟每次争吵后很快就会和好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「梅克 阿普」——桌上散落的零件一件件拼起来，最后成一台整机：构成；拼合

root: make 是古英语动词 macian「塑造、建造」，出自日耳曼语重构词根；up 是古英语副词 upp。组合形式属英语，众多义项在近代发展出来，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses split the phrase into four core layers and six extensions: forming a whole, counting a share, inventing, cosmetics, reconciliation, compensation, assembling a group, doing missed work, making a bed and laying out a page.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项把短语分成四层核心义与六项延伸：构成整体、占份额、编造、化妆、和解、补偿、凑队、补做、铺床、拼版。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered parts gathered on a table until a complete machine stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落零件在桌上被拼成一台完整机器。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: parts, people or type blocks are assembled into one complete thing.
branches.cn: 整体：零件、人或版块被拼成一个完整之物。

branches.en: THE SHARE: the whole is viewed from inside as a fraction or percentage.
branches.cn: 份额：从内部把整体看作分数或百分比。

branches.en: THE FABRICATION: an untrue story is assembled as if it were real.
branches.cn: 捏造：不实故事被拼装得像真的。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: a face is built up layer by layer for the stage.
branches.cn: 表面：为登台把脸一层层造出来。

branches.en: THE REPAIR: quarrels, shortfalls, missed work and beds are all gaps to close.
branches.cn: 修补：争执、缺口、错过的功课与床铺都是待合的缺口。

intro.en: The phrase is native English, so the affix set traces the Old English verb and adverb rather than Latin elements.
intro.cn: 这个短语是英语本族组合，因此词缀部分追溯古英语动词与副词，而非拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon here; the root is the Old English verb macian and the adverb upp.
latinIntro.cn: 此处没有拉丁语词源；词根是古英语动词 macian 与副词 upp。

items.example: The verb applied to both objects and arrangements.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词既用于实物，也用于安排。

items.example: The reconstructed root is shared by Dutch and German.
items.exampleCN: 重构词根为荷兰语与德语共有。

items.example: The verb is one of the most productive in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语里最能产的之一。

items.example: The adverb adds completion to the verb.
items.exampleCN: 副词为动词加上「完成」义。

items.example: The solid spelling marks the noun.
items.exampleCN: 连写标示名词。

items.example: The agent noun is regular.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词规则。

items.example: The prefix repeats the action.
items.exampleCN: 前缀表示重复动作。

items.example: The phrase has grown a wide range of senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语长出了一大片义项。

化妆品；构成
制造者
重做；翻拍
制作；形成过程

definition_zh: 被隔离的；偏僻的；零星的；孤立无援的；医学隔离的；电气上隔离的；孤立系统的；分离提纯的
definition_en: separated from other people, places or things, so that little or no contact remains
core_image: 山间小屋在大雪之后与公路断了联系，补给只能靠直升机空投
scene: 大雪过后，山间那间小屋与公路断了联系，补给只能靠直升机空投。 The farm was isolated by the flood for five days.
sceneCN: 这里指与外界断绝往来、接不上联系（第 1 个义项：被隔开、失去接触）；句意为洪水让这座农场与外界隔绝了五天。

pos.zh: 孤立的；隔离的；偏僻的
零星的；单独的

derivatives.zh: 由「使隔离」的动词加表示动作结果的名词后缀构成，义为「隔离；孤立状态」
由拉丁「岛」的形容词形式经法语与意大利语进入英语，义为「使隔离；分离出」
由「使隔离」的动词加表示器械或施动者的名词后缀构成，义为「隔离器；隔离装置」
由「使隔离」的动词加表示「可……的」的形容词后缀构成，义为「可隔离的；可分离的」
由同一动词加更完整的「可……的」后缀构成，义为「可分离出来的」，常用于实验语境

senses.title: Cut off from contact
senses.definition: separated from others so that communication, supply or movement is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 与他人隔开，使通讯、补给或往来中断
senses.example: The village was isolated by the landslide for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 山体滑坡让这个村子与外界隔绝了一周。
senses.why: The root is the Latin word for an island: land entirely surrounded by water is the original picture of being cut off.
senses.whyCN: 词根是拉丁语的「岛」：四面环水的陆地，正是「被隔断」最初的那幅画。

senses.title: Far from other settlements
senses.definition: situated at a distance from towns and services, so that few people come near
senses.definitionCN: 离城镇与服务设施很远，因而很少有人靠近
senses.example: They bought an isolated cottage above the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山谷上方买下一间偏僻的小屋。
senses.why: Distance produces isolation, so a place with few neighbours is described by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 距离造成隔绝，因此邻居稀少的地方就用同一个词来形容。

senses.title: A single case standing apart
senses.definition: occurring singly and not as part of a pattern, so it is unlikely to repeat
senses.definitionCN: 单独发生，不属于某种模式的一部分，因而不太可能重演
senses.example: Officials called the outbreak an isolated case.
senses.exampleCN: 官员称这次疫情是一起孤立病例。
senses.why: One instance standing apart from a series is like one island standing apart from a coast.
senses.whyCN: 从一串事件中单独分出来的一个实例，就像脱离海岸的一座孤岛。

senses.title: Socially cut off from others
senses.definition: having little or no contact with family, friends or community, often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 与家人、朋友或社区几乎没有往来，常非出于自愿
senses.example: Many elderly residents feel isolated after moving here.
senses.exampleCN: 许多老年居民搬到这里后感到被孤立。
senses.why: A person can be an island too, with contact routes closed on every side.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是一座岛，四周的联系通道全部关闭。

senses.title: Kept apart to stop spread
senses.definition: separated from healthy people or animals to prevent a disease from spreading
senses.definitionCN: 与健康的人或动物分开，以防疾病扩散
senses.example: Patients with the fever were isolated in a separate ward.
senses.exampleCN: 发热病人被隔离在单独的病房里。
senses.why: Medicine deliberately makes a case an island so that infection cannot cross the water.
senses.whyCN: 医学有意把病例变成一座岛，让传染无法渡水而过。

senses.title: Electrically separated
senses.definition: said of a circuit or device that has no conductive path to another circuit
senses.definitionCN: 用于与另一电路之间没有导电通路的电路或装置
senses.example: An isolated supply protects the instrument from surges.
senses.exampleCN: 隔离电源能保护仪器免受电涌冲击。
senses.why: No conductive path means no bridging, the technical form of an island with no causeway.
senses.whyCN: 没有导电路径就没有桥接，这是「没有堤道相连的岛」的技术形态。

senses.title: Sealed off in thermodynamics
senses.titleCN: 热力学中与外界完全封隔
senses.definition: said of a system that exchanges neither matter nor energy with its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 用于与外界既不交换物质也不交换能量的系统
senses.example: An isolated system keeps its total energy constant.
senses.exampleCN: 孤立系统保持总能量不变。
senses.why: Physics pushes the island idea to its limit: nothing at all crosses the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把「岛」的想法推到极限：没有任何东西越过边界。

senses.title: Separated out in a laboratory
senses.titleCN: 在实验室中单独分离出来
senses.definition: obtained alone and free of other substances, as a compound, gene or strain
senses.definitionCN: 单独取得、不含其他物质，如化合物、基因或菌株
senses.example: The team isolated the protein from a few grams of tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 团队从几克组织里分离出了这种蛋白质。
senses.why: Taking one thing out of a mixture puts it on its own, which is isolation in the laboratory.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西从混合物中取出、让它单独存在，就是实验室里的隔离。

intro.en: Isolated comes through French isolé and Italian isolato from Latin insulatus 'made into an island', from insula 'island'. English adopted it in the eighteenth century. The chain is well recorded; first dates are approximate.
intro.cn: isolated 经法语 isolé 与意大利语 isolato 上溯拉丁 insulatus「被造成岛屿的」，后者源于 insula「岛」。英语十八世纪采用。构词链记录清楚，首见年代为约数。

items.en: Insula meant island, and it also named a block of buildings in Rome, each block like a separate island.
items.cn: insula 意为岛，也指罗马城中一栋独立的街区，每栋都像一座单独的岛。

items.en: The adjective meant made into an island or cut off as if by water, and it is the direct source of the whole family.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为「被造成岛、像被水隔开」，是整个词族的直接来源。

items.en: Italian used isolato for a person or place standing alone, and the word spread with Italian art and trade.
items.cn: 意大利语用这个词指独自存在的人或地点，该词随意大利艺术与贸易传播。

items.en: French isolé carried the sense of being set apart, and English borrowed the participle as isolated.
items.cn: 法语 isolé 带有「被分开放置」之意，英语把这个分词借为 isolated。

items.en: English first used it of places and buildings, then of people, cases and specimens.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指地点与建筑，后来扩展到人、案例与标本。

items.en: Medicine, electrical engineering and thermodynamics each gave the word a precise boundary that nothing may cross.
items.cn: 医学、电气工程与热力学各自给这个词一条不得越过的精确边界。

note.en: The first group shares the island stem; the second group holds words for apartness that come from distance, feeling or deliberate separation.
note.cn: 第一组共享「岛」词干；第二组是表示「分开」的词，来源分别是距离、感受或有意分隔。

entries.definition: The state or act of being set apart; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 被隔开的状态或行为；是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: To set something apart, or to separate a substance from a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物隔开，或从混合物中分离出某物质。

entries.definition: A device that keeps one part from affecting another; a technical object noun.
entries.definitionCN: 使一部分不受另一部分影响的装置；是技术性的器物名词。

entries.definition: Able to be separated out; it states a possibility rather than a state.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被分离出来；说的是可能性而非状态。

entries.definition: Far away in distance; it measures how far, not whether contact exists.
entries.definitionCN: 距离上很远；量的是远近，而不是有没有联系。

entries.definition: Feeling sad because one lacks company; it reports a feeling, not an objective separation.
entries.definitionCN: 因缺少陪伴而难过；说的是感受，而非客观的隔断。

entries.definition: Deliberately hidden away and quiet; it often suggests a chosen retreat.
entries.definitionCN: 有意隐藏、清静；常暗示主动选择的退居之处。

entries.definition: Physically or socially disconnected; the everyday phrase for the result the target word names.
entries.definitionCN: 在物理或社交上断开；是目标词所指结果的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin for island: to isolate is to make something an island.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语的「岛」：隔离就是把某物变成一座岛。

normal.en: The family runs isolate, isolation, isolator and isolable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括隔离、隔离状态、隔离器、可隔离的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the social side: isolated case, socially isolated.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出社会一面：个别案例、社会孤立。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark technical use: isolated system, isolated gene.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：孤立系统、分离出的基因。

normal.en: Two neighbours differ: remote measures distance, lonely measures feeling.
normal.cn: 两个近邻不同：remote 量距离，lonely 量感受。

abstract.en: Picture a house on a rock with water on every side and no bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子立在礁石上，四周都是水，没有桥。

abstract.en: Picture one red apple in a crate of green ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一箱青苹果里只有一只红的。

abstract.en: Picture a phone with every contact deleted except one.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手机，联系人删到只剩一个。

examples.en: The islanders live isolated from the mainland for half the year.
examples.cn: 这些岛民一年里有半年与大陆隔绝。

examples.en: Doctors isolated the virus before it could spread.
examples.cn: 医生在病毒扩散前把它分离了出来。

examples.en: His office is isolated from the rest of the team.
examples.cn: 他的办公室与团队其他成员隔开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱搜累他」——一个人被隔在小岛上，找不到人也靠不上，就是孤立

root: 拉丁 insula「岛」→ insulatus「被造成岛的、像被水隔开的」→ 意大利语 isolato、法语 isolé → 英语 isolated。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all make something an island: a place, a person, a single case, a patient, a circuit, a physical system or a compound taken out of a mixture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物变成一座岛：地方、人、单个案例、病人、电路、物理系统，或从混合物中取出的化合物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of land surrounded by water, with no bridge to the mainland.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块四面环水的陆地，没有桥连到大陆。

branches.en: THE SPATIAL SIDE: contact blocked, and a place far from any neighbour.
branches.cn: 空间一面：联系被阻断，以及远离任何邻居的地方。

branches.en: THE STATISTICAL SIDE: one case standing outside any pattern.
branches.cn: 统计一面：一个案例处在任何模式之外。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL SIDE: a person with almost no human contact.
branches.cn: 社会一面：几乎没有人类接触的人。

branches.en: THE LABORATORY SIDE: a patient kept apart to stop spread, and a substance taken out of a mixture.
branches.cn: 实验室一面：为阻断传播而隔开的病人，以及从混合物中取出的物质。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERED SIDE: no conductive path, and a system that exchanges nothing with its surroundings.
branches.cn: 工程一面：没有导电路径，以及与外界不交换任何东西的系统。

intro.en: Isolated is a Latin participle built on insula 'island'; English adds the endings of state, agent and possibility.
intro.cn: isolated 是建立在 insula「岛」之上的拉丁分词；英语再加表示状态、施动与可能的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Insula 'island' gives insulatus 'made into an island'; Italian isolato and French isolé pass it to English as isolate and isolated.
latinIntro.cn: insula「岛」给出 insulatus「被造成岛的」；意大利语 isolato 与法语 isolé 把它传给英语，成为 isolate 与 isolated。

items.example: The noun is the picture behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是每个义项背后的画面。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是词族的直接来源。

items.example: The ending carries the participle into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把分词带入英语。

items.example: The verb names the act of cutting off.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名「切断联系」的动作。

items.example: The participle became the everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了日常形容词。

items.example: The suffix gives isolation, the state of being apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出「隔离状态」。

items.example: The suffix gives isolator, the device.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出指装置的「隔离器」。

items.example: The suffix states that something can be separated out.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀说明某物可以被分离出来。

items.meaning: of an island; narrow in outlook
items.example: The same stem also gives a word for island narrowness.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干还给出表示「岛国狭隘」的词。

latinEntries.structure: insulatus, insulata, insulatum (participle used as adj.)

由拉丁「岛」的形容词形式进入英语，义为「使隔离」
由「使隔离」加施动或器物后缀构成，义为「隔离器」
由「使隔离」加「可……的」后缀构成，义为「可隔离的」
