definition_zh: 城市的；市政的；公民的；公民义务的；公民品德的
definition_en: relating to a city or town, or to the rights and duties of the people who belong to it
core_image: 一座石砌的市政厅立在广场一侧，台阶上贴着通知，市民从门前经过时抬头看那座钟
scene: 广场旁的老市场被改建成一座供市民集会、借书、听讲座的公共建筑。 The old market hall was restored as a civic centre for the town.
sceneCN: 广场旁的老市场被改建成一座供市民集会、借书、听讲座的公共建筑；句中这个词指「属于城市公共事务的」（第 1 个义项：与城市或城镇作为公共共同体相关的）。句意为老市场被修复成镇上的市民活动中心。可辨识物件：石砌立面、公告栏、钟、台阶上的人。

pos.zh: 城市的；市政的
公民的；公民义务与权利的

derivatives.zh: 公民课；市政学
以公民身份；就市政而言
有公民意识的
公民
公民身份

senses.title: Of a city as a place
senses.titleCN: 属于城市或城镇这个空间
senses.definition: relating to a city or town as a physical and social place
senses.definitionCN: 与城市或城镇作为实体与社会场所相关的
senses.example: The old market hall was restored as a civic centre for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 老市场被修复成镇上的市民活动中心。
senses.why: Latin civicus meant 'of a citizen', and English attached it first to the town that the citizens share.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 civicus 意为「公民的」，英语先把它附在公民共有的城镇上。

senses.title: Of municipal government
senses.definition: relating to the elected government and public services of a town
senses.definitionCN: 与城镇的民选政府及公共服务相关的
senses.example: The mayor opened the civic budget to public view.
senses.exampleCN: 市长把市政预算向公众公开。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the institution that runs the town, so civic means municipal as well as urban.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也附在管理城镇的机构上，因此既指「城市的」，也指「市政的」。

senses.title: Of a citizen's duties
senses.definition: relating to what people owe the community by virtue of belonging to it
senses.definitionCN: 与人们因属于共同体而对它应尽之事相关的
senses.example: Voting is treated as a civic duty, not a private hobby.
senses.exampleCN: 投票被视为公民义务，而不是私人爱好。
senses.why: The same adjective covers the member's side of the city, where belonging creates obligations.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词也覆盖成员这一侧，也就是归属产生义务的一面。

senses.title: Of a citizen's rights
senses.definition: relating to the rights people hold as members of a community
senses.definitionCN: 与人们作为共同体成员所持权利相关的
senses.example: The charter lists civic rights such as petition and assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 宪章列明请愿与集会等公民权利。
senses.why: Rights and duties are two faces of one membership, and English uses one adjective for both faces.
senses.whyCN: 权利与义务是同一成员身份的两面，英语用同一个形容词指这两面。

senses.title: Civic pride
senses.definition: a feeling of attachment to and satisfaction with one's town
senses.definitionCN: 对所在城镇的依恋与满意之情
senses.example: The clean square was a matter of civic pride.
senses.exampleCN: 广场保持整洁，是市民自豪感的一部分。
senses.why: Pride is the emotional form of belonging, so the adjective of the town also names a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 自豪是归属感的情感形态，因此城镇的形容词也用来指一种情感。

senses.title: Civic engagement
senses.definition: organized participation in public affairs, such as volunteering, campaigning or attending meetings
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地参与公共事务，如志愿服务、竞选活动或出席会议
senses.example: Civic engagement rose after the library began hosting debates.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆开始举办辩论会后，公民参与度上升了。
senses.why: Modern political language turns the adjective into a label for activity, and the label spreads through policy reports.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治语言把这个形容词变成活动的标签，这个标签又通过政策报告扩散开来。

senses.title: Civic education
senses.definition: instruction in how citizenship, laws and public institutions work
senses.definitionCN: 讲解公民身份、法律与公共机构如何运作的教育
senses.example: The school added a civic education module on local taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 学校增设了一个关于地方税收的公民教育单元。
senses.why: Curricula name the subject after the idea, so civic education sits beside history and geography.
senses.whyCN: 课程用这个理念给科目命名，于是公民教育与历史、地理并列。

senses.title: Civic style in building
senses.definition: the plain, monumental manner of buildings put up for public use
senses.definitionCN: 为公共用途而建的建筑所呈现的朴素、庄重风格
senses.example: The station was rebuilt in a plain civic style.
senses.exampleCN: 车站以朴素的市政风格重建。
senses.why: Buildings that serve the public are described by the public they serve, and the adjective becomes a style label.
senses.whyCN: 为公众服务的建筑，用它们所服务的公众来命名，这个形容词由此成为风格标签。

intro.en: Civic comes from French civique and Latin civicus 'of a citizen', built on civis 'citizen'. English took the adjective in the seventeenth century, later than it took the person-noun.
intro.cn: civic 来自法语 civique 与拉丁 civicus「公民的」，其词根为 civis「公民」。英语在十七世纪才借入这个形容词，晚于指人的名词。

items.en: Civis meant 'citizen, townsman'. Its deeper origin is not established; any older root offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: civis 意为「公民、城里人」。其更深来源未得到证明；为它给出的任何更早词根都是重构形式，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Civicus was the adjective 'of a citizen, of citizens'. Latin used it for the dress, the duty and the law of a citizen, so the word already carried both the town and the obligation.
items.cn: civicus 是形容词「公民的、属于公民的」。拉丁语用它指公民的衣着、义务与法律，因此这个词从一开始就同时带着「城市」与「义务」。

items.en: French civique continued the Latin adjective. It was used in political writing before English borrowed it, which is why the English word keeps a formal, civic tone.
items.cn: 法语 civique 延续了拉丁形容词。英语借入之前，它已用于政治写作，因此英语这个词带有正式、市政的语气。

items.en: English civic is recorded from the seventeenth century in the sense 'pertaining to a city or citizens'. The word entered through learned and political prose, not through everyday speech.
items.cn: 英语 civic 自十七世纪起有「属于城市或公民的」这一义项。这个词经学术与政治散文进入英语，而非通过日常口语。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective formed civic duty, civic pride and civic rights; the policy compounds civic engagement and civic education are later still. Source uncertain (first date): the earliest citation of each compound is not fixed.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词构成公民义务、市民自豪感与公民权利；政策用语中的公民参与、公民教育更晚。首见年代不确定：各复合词的最早书证并无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the civis root or a very close spelling; group two holds adjectives that also describe public or town life.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 civis 词根或拼写极近的词；第二组是同样描述公共或城市生活的形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin civilis 'of a citizen', but it means polite, non-military or belonging to ordinary law. A civil war is not a civic event, and civil manners are not municipal services.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 civilis「公民的」，但意为「有礼的、非军事的、属于民事法律的」。内战不是市政事件，礼貌也不是市政服务。

entries.definition: The person who holds citizenship; civic is only the adjective and never names a human being.
entries.definitionCN: 持有公民身份的人；civic 只是形容词，从不指人。

entries.definition: A person who is not a soldier. It shares the root but contrasts with military service, not with a town.
entries.definitionCN: 指不是军人的人。它同根，但对照的是军役，而非城市。

entries.definition: A large town; the noun names the place, while civic names what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指大城市；名词指地方，而 civic 指属于该地方的事物。

entries.definition: The plural-looking noun for the study of citizenship and government. It ends in -s but is singular in use.
entries.definitionCN: 这个看起来像复数的名词指对公民身份与政体的研究。词尾有 -s，实际作单数用。

entries.definition: Relating to the administration of a town, especially its council and services; narrower than civic, which also covers duties, pride and rights.
entries.definitionCN: 与城镇行政相关，尤其指市政会及其服务；比 civic 窄，civic 还涵盖义务、自豪感与权利。

entries.definition: Relating to a town as a built and populated area, in contrast with rural; it says nothing about citizenship or duties.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为建成并有人居住的区域的城市，与乡村相对；完全不涉及公民身份或义务。

entries.definition: Open to everyone or owned by the community; a public building may be civic in tone, but public stresses access rather than membership.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放或由共同体所有；公共建筑可能带市政气息，但 public 强调的是可及性，而非成员身份。

entries.definition: Shared by a group of people, often a small community; it stresses common ownership, not a town's formal institutions.
entries.definitionCN: 由一群人共享，常指较小共同体；它强调共同所有，而非城镇的正式机构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin adjective, a real French borrowing and real policy compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁形容词、真实的法语借词与真实的政策搭配。

normal.en: The root civis gives citizen, city, civic and civilian, one family with four faces.
normal.cn: 词根 civis 衍生出 citizen、city、civic 与 civilian，一个词族有四张面孔。

normal.en: The ending -ic means 'relating to', so civic is the relating-to-citizens word.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ic 意为「与……相关」，所以 civic 就是「与公民相关」的词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: civic duty, civic pride, civic engagement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：公民义务、市民自豪感、公民参与。

normal.en: The school subject is civics, a noun that ends in -s but takes a singular verb.
normal.cn: 学校科目叫 civics，词尾有 -s，却接单数动词。

normal.en: A civic centre is a building for the public, not a centre that belongs to a private firm.
normal.cn: 市民活动中心是为公众服务的建筑，而不是属于私营企业的中心。

abstract.en: Picture a town hall whose clock is set by the people who walk past it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座市政厅，它的钟由路过的人来校准。

abstract.en: Picture a square where every paving stone carries a name nobody reads.
abstract.cn: 想象一个广场，每块铺石上都刻着一个无人细看的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a public bench that becomes more comfortable the more it is shared.
abstract.cn: 想象一张公共长椅，越多人同坐就越舒适。

examples.en: Civic leaders met to plan the river cleanup.
examples.cn: 市政领袖开会筹划河道清理。

examples.en: The library runs civic education evenings for new residents.
examples.cn: 图书馆为新居民举办公民教育夜校。

examples.en: Civic pride showed in the freshly painted benches.
examples.cn: 市民自豪感体现在刚刷过漆的长椅上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「city（城市）+ ick（形容词尾）」——城市的、市政的；这只是一句谐音拆解，并非真实词源

root: 拉丁 civis「公民」→ civicus「公民的」→ 法语 civique → 英语 civic（十七世纪）。civis 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses stay close to one shared space: the town as a place, the council that runs it, the duties and rights of its members, the pride they feel, the engagement they show, the subject they study and the style they build.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕同一块共享空间：作为地方的城市、管理它的市政会、成员的义务与权利、他们感到的自豪、表现出的参与、学习的科目与建造的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone town hall on one side of a square, with notices on its steps and a clock that the passers-by keep looking up at.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场一侧的石砌市政厅，台阶上贴着通知，路过的人不时抬头看那座钟。

branches.en: The physical town and its public style are one thread: the building is the town made visible.
branches.cn: 实体城镇与它的公共风格是同一条线：建筑就是城镇的可见形态。

branches.en: The council is the town acting as an institution, so municipal government is civic in the narrowest sense.
branches.cn: 市政会就是作为机构行事的城镇，因此市政管理是最窄意义上的 civic。

branches.en: Membership runs both ways, and the same adjective names the duty to give and the right to claim.
branches.cn: 成员身份双向运行，同一个形容词既指付出的义务，也指主张的权利。

branches.en: Feeling and action support each other: pride supplies the motive, engagement supplies the deed.
branches.cn: 情感与行动相互支撑：自豪提供动机，参与提供行动。

branches.en: The idea becomes a subject when a school decides to teach it, and the adjective turns into a syllabus label.
branches.cn: 当学校决定教授这个理念时，它就变成一门科目，形容词也随之成为课程标签。

intro.en: Civic is a Latin adjective ending in -ic, and the same root also builds the person, the place, the abstract status and a school subject.
intro.cn: civic 是带 -ic 词尾的拉丁形容词，同一词根还构成指人的词、指地方的词、抽象身份与一门学校科目。

latinIntro.en: Latin civis and civicus supply the whole family; the -ic ending marks 'relating to', which is exactly the adjective's job.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 civis 与 civicus 提供整个词族；-ic 词尾标出「与……相关」，正是这个形容词的职责。

items.example: The root names the member of a town.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指城镇中的成员。

items.example: The adjective adds the relating-to ending to the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在词根后加上「与……相关」的词尾。

items.example: French carried the Latin adjective into modern political vocabulary.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个拉丁形容词带入现代政治词汇。

items.meaning: relating to a town or its citizens
items.meaningCN: 与城市或其公民相关的
items.example: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成表关系的形容词。

items.example: The plural-looking ending names a field of study.
items.exampleCN: 这个像复数的词尾用来命名一个研究领域。

items.meaningCN: 公民的；有礼的；非军事的
items.example: A second adjective from the same root widened in a different direction.
items.exampleCN: 同根的第二个形容词朝另一个方向扩展。

items.meaning: a member of a town or state
items.example: The person-noun is the base that the adjective describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个指人的名词是形容词所描述的基础。

items.meaning: a person not in the armed forces
items.example: The word contrasts ordinary life with military service.
items.exampleCN: 这个词把平常生活与军役相对。

definition_zh: 沼泽；湿地；盐沼；长着草与芦苇的浅水低地
definition_en: low-lying wet ground covered with grasses, reeds and soft mud, often flooded periodically
core_image: 潮水涨上来，芦苇只露出上半截，泥面被咸水没过，几条小水道在草间穿行
scene: 涨潮时，咸水漫过泥面，芦苇只露出半截。 At high tide the marsh fills with brackish water and the reeds stand half submerged.
sceneCN: 这里 marsh 指「长着草与芦苇、周期性被水淹的低洼湿地」（第 1 个义项：草本沼泽）；句意为涨潮时咸水灌满沼泽，芦苇半没水中。图中可辨识物件：半没的芦苇、泥面、潮水线、弯曲小水道。

pos.zh: 沼泽；湿地；盐沼（可数或不可数）

forms.label: 形容词（沼泽的；多沼泽的）

沼泽地

senses.title: Low wet ground with reeds and grass
senses.titleCN: 长着芦苇与草的低洼湿地
senses.definition: low-lying ground that is periodically flooded and carries grasses, reeds and soft mud rather than trees
senses.definitionCN: 周期性被淹、长草与芦苇、泥软而不长树的低洼地
senses.example: At high tide the marsh fills with brackish water and the reeds stand half submerged.
senses.exampleCN: 涨潮时咸水灌满沼泽，芦苇半没水中。
senses.why: marsh names wet ground by its soft, grassy cover, standing between open water and dry land.
senses.whyCN: marsh 按湿软、长草的覆盖来命名湿地，位于开阔水域与干地之间。

senses.title: Salt marsh at the coast
senses.definition: coastal wet ground flooded by tides, colonised by salt-tolerant grasses and cut by creeks
senses.definitionCN: 受潮汐淹没、由耐盐草类占据并被小水道切割的海岸湿地
senses.example: Salt marsh cordgrass traps sediment and builds the shore outward.
senses.exampleCN: 盐沼大米草拦住泥沙，把岸线向外造。
senses.why: the salt suffix marks the marine water source, which changes both the plants and the management.
senses.whyCN: salt 后缀标出海洋水源，这同时改变了植物与管理方式。

senses.title: Freshwater marsh inland
senses.definition: inland wetland fed by rain, streams or groundwater, with reeds, sedges and floating plants
senses.definitionCN: 由雨水、溪流或地下水补给的内陆湿地，长芦苇、莎草与浮水植物
senses.example: The freshwater marsh behind the dunes holds frogs all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 沙丘后的淡水沼泽整个夏天都有蛙。
senses.why: the same landform appears with fresh water, and the word covers both as long as the cover stays grassy.
senses.whyCN: 同样的地形也可由淡水形成；只要覆盖仍是草类，这个词两者都覆盖。

senses.title: Tidal creeks and the marsh platform
senses.definition: the marsh surface dissected by dendritic creeks that drain and refill with each tide
senses.definitionCN: 被树枝状潮沟切割、随每次潮汐排空与回灌的沼泽台面
senses.example: The marsh platform rises a few millimetres a year as sediment settles.
senses.exampleCN: 随着泥沙沉降，沼泽台面每年升高几毫米。
senses.why: marsh is not flat and static: its creeks and platform are built by the same tidal water that floods it.
senses.whyCN: 沼泽并非平坦静止：它的潮沟与台面正由淹没它的潮水造出。

senses.title: Habitat for waterbirds and amphibians
senses.titleCN: 水鸟与两栖动物的生境
senses.definition: the shallow, plant-rich wet ground used for nesting, feeding and shelter by birds, fish and amphibians
senses.definitionCN: 浅水、植物丰富的湿地，被鸟、鱼与两栖类用于筑巢、觅食与隐蔽
senses.example: The marsh hosts thousands of waders each migration.
senses.exampleCN: 每次迁徙，这片沼泽都接待成千上万的涉禽。
senses.why: the physical description becomes a habitat term once species are said to depend on it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦说某些物种依赖它，物理描述就变成生境术语。

senses.title: Drainage and reclamation
senses.definition: the historic conversion of marsh to farmland by ditches, pumps and embankments
senses.definitionCN: 历史上通过沟渠、抽水与堤坝把沼泽改为农田
senses.example: Reclamation turned the marsh into grazing land within two generations.
senses.exampleCN: 两代人之内，开垦就把沼泽变成牧场。
senses.why: the word carries a history of loss, because most European marsh was drained before it was valued.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着一段丧失史，因为欧洲多数沼泽在被重视之前就已排干。

senses.title: Marsh gas as methane
senses.definition: methane produced by decay under waterlogged, oxygen-poor conditions and released as bubbles
senses.definitionCN: 在积水缺氧条件下腐烂产生、以气泡释放的甲烷
senses.example: Marsh gas bubbled up when the spade broke the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 铁锹戳破泥面时，沼气冒了上来。
senses.why: the old name records an observable phenomenon before chemistry explained it.
senses.whyCN: 这个旧名记录了化学解释之前就能观察到的现象。

senses.title: Marsh as a mineral wetland class
senses.definition: in wetland classification, a mineral-soil wetland with grass or reed cover, as distinct from peat-forming bog and fen
senses.definitionCN: 湿地分类中，矿质土、以草或芦苇覆盖的湿地，区别于成泥炭的泥炭沼与矿质沼泽
senses.example: The survey separates marsh from fen by peat depth.
senses.exampleCN: 调查以泥炭厚度把沼泽与矿质沼泽分开。
senses.why: classification needs boundaries, so a common word is narrowed into a technical class defined by soil.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要边界，于是常用词被收窄为由土壤定义的技术类别。

intro.en: Marsh is a native Germanic word from Old English merisc, built on mere 'sea, lake'; Latin mare 'sea' is a cousin, not an ancestor.
intro.cn: marsh 是日耳曼本族词，来自古英语 merisc，由 mere「海、湖」构成；拉丁 mare「海」是远亲，而非祖先。

items.en: Merisc and mersc named marshy ground. The element mere meant 'sea, lake, pool', so the word began as 'water-land'.
items.cn: merisc 与 mersc 指沼泽地。其中 mere 意为「海、湖、池」，因此这个词原意是「水边的地」。

items.en: The Germanic stock is reconstructed as *marisk-, from *mari- 'sea, lake', a form not directly attested.
items.cn: 其日耳曼词干重构为 *marisk-，出自 *mari-「海、湖」，这一形式没有直接书证。

items.en: Latin mare 'sea' and English mere, marsh share the Indo-European root *mori- 'body of water'; they are cousins, not a borrowing.
items.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」与英语 mere、marsh 共享印欧词根 *mori-「水体」；它们是同源远亲，不是借词关系。

items.en: Middle English marsh kept both the wet ground and the plants cut from it; the place sense now dominates.
items.cn: 中古英语 marsh 兼指湿地与从其中割取的植物；如今地点义占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Germanic root *mori- is a reconstruction, and the exact first English citation is not securely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：日耳曼语之前的词根 *mori- 属重构；最早英语书证年代不可靠。

note.en: Group one separates marsh from its own derivatives and compounds; group two separates the wetland types by water source and cover.
note.cn: 第一组区分 marsh 与其派生、复合词；第二组按水源与覆盖区分湿地类型。

entries.definition: Describing ground that is soft, wet and like a marsh; it is a quality, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容地面湿软如沼泽；是性质，不是地点。

entries.definition: Marsh considered as a stretch of land, often used in mapping and conservation.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一片土地的沼泽，常用于制图与保护。

entries.definition: The coastal, tide-flooded type written as one word in ecology; it is a narrower term than marsh.
entries.definitionCN: 生态学中连写的海岸潮汐型；比 marsh 窄。

entries.definition: A pink-flowered plant of salty marshes whose root once flavoured confectionery, hence marshmallow.
entries.definitionCN: 盐沼中开粉花的植物，其根曾用于调味糖果，marshmallow 即由此来。

entries.definition: Wetland dominated by trees or shrubs; marsh is the grassy, reed-dominated counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 以乔木或灌木为主的湿地；marsh 是以草与芦苇为主的对应型。

entries.definition: Acid peatland fed only by rain; it is organic and nutrient-poor, unlike a mineral marsh.
entries.definitionCN: 仅靠雨水补给的酸性泥炭地；有机质、养分贫乏，与矿质沼泽不同。

entries.definition: Peatland fed by mineral-rich groundwater; it may look grassy but builds peat.
entries.definitionCN: 由富矿物地下水补给的泥炭地；看似长草，却在造泥炭。

entries.definition: The general legal and scientific class that includes marsh, swamp, bog and fen.
entries.definitionCN: 包含 marsh、swamp、bog、fen 的通用法律与科学类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mere 'sea, lake' + -isc: the wet edge of water.
normal.cn: mere「海、湖」+ -isc：水的湿边缘。

normal.en: Latin mare 'sea' is a cousin through Indo-European *mori-, not a source.
normal.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」经印欧 *mori- 与之同源，是远亲，不是来源。

normal.en: The family runs marsh, marshy, marshland, saltmarsh, marsh mallow.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marsh、marshy、marshland、saltmarsh、marsh mallow。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: salt marsh, freshwater marsh, tidal marsh, marsh gas.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：盐沼、淡水沼泽、潮汐沼泽、沼气。

normal.en: The image is reeds half submerged as the tide comes in.
normal.cn: 意象是涨潮时半没水中的芦苇。

abstract.en: Think of a floor that is solid in winter and liquid in spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一块冬天坚硬、春天液化的地板。

abstract.en: Think of a border zone where neither land nor water can claim the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一块陆与水的边界带，两者都不能宣称拥有它。

abstract.en: Think of a place that smells of mud and keeps the memory of old floods.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带着泥味、记得旧日洪水的地方。

examples.en: The marsh floods every spring and dries to cracked mud by August.
examples.cn: 这片沼泽每年春天被淹，到八月干成裂泥。

examples.en: Mosquitoes breed in the stagnant edges of the marsh.
examples.cn: 蚊子在沼泽滞留的水边繁殖。

examples.en: The old marsh was drained to make the airport runway.
examples.cn: 旧沼泽被排干，用来修机场跑道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marsh」谐音「马什」——马踩下去陷住的湿软地 → 沼泽

root: 古英语 merisc / mersc「沼泽」← mere「海、湖」+ -isc。与拉丁 mare「海」同出印欧词根 *mori-「水体」，属同源远亲而非借用；*mori- 为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from grassy wet ground to its coastal and freshwater forms, its creeks, its wildlife, its drainage history, its gas and its technical class.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从长草的湿软地，走向海岸与淡水形式、潮沟、野生动物、排水史、沼气与技术分类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft ground at the edge of water, held by reeds.
core.cn: 核心意象：水边由芦苇固住的软地。

branches.en: BASE: soft wet ground with grassy cover, whether inland or fresh.
branches.cn: 基底：长草的湿软地，无论内陆还是淡水。

branches.en: SEA EDGE: tides flood it, cut creeks and build the platform upward.
branches.cn: 海缘：潮汐淹没它，切出潮沟，又把台面向上造。

branches.en: LIFE AND LOSS: it shelters wildlife, and it has been drained for farmland.
branches.cn: 生命与丧失：它庇护野生生物，也曾被排干为农田。

branches.en: DECAY: waterlogged mud without oxygen produces methane.
branches.cn: 腐烂：缺氧的积水泥产生甲烷。

branches.en: CLASS: mineral soil and grassy cover separate marsh from peatland.
branches.cn: 分类：矿质土与草覆盖把沼泽与泥炭地分开。

intro.en: Marsh is a native noun with a productive -y adjective and a land compound; its older element mere survives in place names.
intro.cn: marsh 是本族名词，可构成 -y 形容词与 land 复合词；其较古成分 mere 仍见于地名。

latinIntro.en: Latin mare is a cognate through Indo-European, not a source; it is listed for comparison, not as an ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mare 经印欧语与之同源，并非来源；列出仅供比较，不是祖先。

items.example: The marsh is grazed only in dry summers.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽只在干旱夏季放牧。

items.meaning: like a marsh, soft and wet
items.example: Marshy ground stopped the tractor.
items.exampleCN: 湿软的地陷住了拖拉机。

items.example: Marshland borders the estuary.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽地紧邻河口。

items.example: Saltmarsh sheep graze on the seaward grass.
items.exampleCN: 盐沼羊在向海的草地上吃草。

items.example: Marsh gas can burn when it collects in a drain.
items.exampleCN: 沼气在沟中积聚时可燃。

items.example: Marsh mallow root was once boiled for sweets.
items.exampleCN: 药蜀葵根曾用来熬制糖果。

items.meaning: a bird that nests in reeds
items.example: The marsh wren sings from a reed stem.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽苇莺在苇茎上鸣唱。

items.example: Mere survives in lake names such as Windermere.
items.exampleCN: mere 仍见于 Windermere 等湖名。

definition_zh: 表达；表情；词语；表达方式；数学式；基因表达
definition_en: the act of showing thoughts or feelings, or the look on a face that shows them
core_image: 心里的东西被一股力量压出来，落在脸上、纸上或公式里
scene: 她听到消息后没有说话，脸上的神情却先变了，同事低声说： Her expression changed before she found the words.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「脸上显示情绪的神情」（第 2 个义项：面部神情）；句意为她还没找到话说，神情就先变了。

pos.zh: 表达；表情；词语；表达方式；数学式；基因表达

富于表现力的

senses.title: The act of showing thoughts or feelings
senses.titleCN: 把想法或情感表达出来的行为
senses.definition: the act of making thoughts, feelings or ideas known
senses.definitionCN: 把想法、情感或观点让人知道的行为
senses.example: Freedom of expression is protected by law.
senses.exampleCN: 表达自由受法律保护。
senses.why: The core image is pressing something inward out into the open, and the first sense is simply that outward movement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把里面的东西压到外面来，第 1 个义项就是这一向外的动作本身。

senses.title: The look on a face
senses.definition: the appearance of a person's face that shows a feeling or state of mind
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的脸部外观所显示的情绪或心理状态
senses.example: His expression softened when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息，他的神情柔和下来。
senses.why: The face is the most visible surface where inner feeling is pressed into public view.
senses.whyCN: 脸是内心情感被压到公众视野里最显眼的表面。

senses.title: A word or phrase
senses.definition: a particular word, phrase or way of saying something
senses.definitionCN: 某个特定的词、短语或说法
senses.example: A local expression puzzled the translator.
senses.exampleCN: 一个当地说法让译者困惑。
senses.why: A fixed group of words is a small package into which a meaning has already been pressed.
senses.whyCN: 一组固定的词就像一个小包裹，意义早已被压进其中。

senses.title: Vivid delivery in speech or music
senses.titleCN: 说话或演奏时的表现力
senses.definition: the quality of conveying feeling through voice, phrasing or performance
senses.definitionCN: 通过嗓音、措辞或表演传达情感的特质
senses.example: She read the poem with great expression.
senses.exampleCN: 她极富表现力地朗读了这首诗。
senses.why: Once the outward push is done with skill, the delivery itself becomes noticeable and can be praised.
senses.whyCN: 当向外的推送带有技巧时，表达方式本身就会变得显眼并值得称赞。

senses.title: A mathematical expression
senses.definition: a combination of numbers, symbols and operations that stands for a value
senses.definitionCN: 由数字、符号与运算组成、代表某个值的组合
senses.example: Simplify the expression before substituting values.
senses.exampleCN: 先化简表达式，再代入数值。
senses.why: Mathematics writes a value as a visible string of symbols, pressing an abstract quantity into a readable form.
senses.whyCN: 数学把一个值写成可见的符号串，把抽象量压成可读的形式。

senses.title: Gene expression in biology
senses.definition: the process by which information in a gene is turned into a working product
senses.definitionCN: 基因中的信息被转成可用产物的过程
senses.example: The gene's expression rises under heat stress.
senses.exampleCN: 在热应激下，这个基因的表达增强。
senses.why: A gene carries hidden instructions, and expression is the moment those instructions are pushed out into the cell.
senses.whyCN: 基因携带隐藏的指令，表达就是这些指令被推到细胞里发挥作用的时刻。

senses.title: Pressing out juice or oil
senses.definition: the physical act of squeezing liquid out of fruit, seeds or peel
senses.definitionCN: 从果实、种子或果皮中挤出液体的物理动作
senses.example: Cold expression of the peel releases the essential oil.
senses.exampleCN: 冷榨果皮能释放出精油。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense: the word's root literally means to press out, and liquids are pressed from plants.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的具体义：词根字面就是「压出来」，而液体正是从植物中被压出的。

senses.title: A manifestation or sign
senses.titleCN: 某种态度或品质的显现
senses.definition: an act or thing that shows a quality, attitude or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 显示某种品质、态度或情感的行为或事物
senses.example: The grant is an expression of confidence in the team.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资助是对该团队信心的体现。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the push: an inner attitude becomes visible through an outer act.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「推送」一般化：内在态度通过外在行为变得可见。

intro.en: Expression comes through Old French from Latin expressio, a noun of action from exprimere 'to press out', built on ex- 'out' and premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expression 经古法语来自拉丁语 expressio，这是动词 exprimere「压出」的行为名词，由拉丁语表示「向外」的前缀与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press'. Its deeper origin is not established, and the Indo-European root sometimes proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: premere 意为「压」。其更深来源未得到证明，有人为它提出的印欧词根只是重构形式。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus premere produced exprimere 'to press out, squeeze out'; it also developed the sense 'to represent or portray'.
items.cn: 表示「向外」的拉丁前缀加 premere 构成 exprimere「压出、挤出」；它还发展出「表现、描绘」的意义。

items.en: The action noun expressio named both a physical pressing out and a representation in words or art.
items.cn: 行为名词 expressio 既指物理上的压出，也指用词语或艺术的表现。

items.en: Old French expression entered English in the fourteenth century, first as the act of expressing and as an utterance.
items.cn: 古法语 expression 在十四世纪进入英语，最初指表达的行为与说出的话。

items.en: The facial sense took shape in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, while algebra adopted the word for a symbolic string and biology adopted it for gene activity in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 面部义在十七至十八世纪成形；代数学采用这个词指符号串，生物学则在二十世纪用它指基因活动。

items.en: Source uncertain: the date of the facial sense is not exact, and the pre-Latin origin of premere remains unsettled, so every proposed root form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：面部义的确切年代不确定，premere 在拉丁语之前的来源也仍未确定，因此提出的各种词根形式都属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built with the same pressing root but different prefixes; group two holds near neighbours in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「压」这一词根、但前缀不同的词；第二组是语义相近的词。

entries.definition: Built with 'in' rather than 'out': something presses into the mind and leaves an impression, not an outward expression.
entries.definitionCN: 用的是「向内」而非「向外」的前缀：某物压进心里留下印象，而不是向外的表达。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'together': it names pressing something into a smaller space, with no idea of showing meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「共同」：指把某物压进更小的空间，与显示意义无关。

entries.definition: The prefix means 'under': it names holding something down or stopping it, often feelings or information.
entries.definitionCN: 前缀意为「在下」：指把某物压住或制止，常指情感或信息。

entries.definition: It looks as if it should belong to the pressing family, but its root means 'to appease or atone', not 'to press'.
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像属于「压」这个词族，其实词根意为「安抚、赎罪」，并非「压」。

entries.definition: A plain word for the appearance of a face; expression adds the idea that the look reveals inner feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 指脸部外观的朴素词；expression 多了「神情显示内心情感」这一层。

entries.definition: A group of words forming a unit; expression can also mean a fixed saying, but it is broader and more idiomatic.
entries.definitionCN: 构成一个单位的词组；expression 也可指固定说法，但范围更宽、更习语化。

entries.definition: A technical term for a unit of speech; expression points more to the meaning being conveyed than to the sound produced.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个言语单位的技术术语；expression 更指向被传达的意义，而不是发出的声音。

entries.definition: A formal word for something that makes an inner quality visible, close to the eighth sense of expression.
entries.definitionCN: 指使内在品质变得可见的正式用词，接近 expression 的第 8 个义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the pressing root, the prefix contrasts and the real technical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「压」的词根、前缀对比与真实的技术用法。

normal.en: The root means 'press', so expression is a pressing outward of what was inside.
normal.cn: 词根意为「压」，因此这个词就是把里面的东西向外压出来。

normal.en: Prefix contrast: outward pressing gives expression, inward pressing gives impression.
normal.cn: 前缀对比：向外压得到「表达」，向内压得到「印象」。

normal.en: Face use: the same word names the look that shows feeling.
normal.cn: 面部用法：同一个词也命名显示情感的神情。

normal.en: Technical spread: algebra uses it for a symbolic string, biology for gene activity.
normal.cn: 技术延伸：代数学用它指符号串，生物学用它指基因活动。

normal.en: Everyday phrase: freedom of expression names the right to make ideas public.
normal.cn: 日常搭配：表达自由指把想法公开的权利。

abstract.en: Picture a hand squeezing a fruit until the juice lands in a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手挤压果子，汁水落进杯子里。

abstract.en: Picture an inner feeling rising to the surface of a face like water to a well.
abstract.cn: 想象内心的情感升到脸的表面，像水升到井口。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence folded into a small box that can be handed to someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被折进一个小盒子，可以递给别人。

examples.en: The court treated the letter as an expression of intent.
examples.cn: 法院把这封信视为意向的表达。

examples.en: Her expression did not match the cheerful words she used.
examples.cn: 她的神情与她使用的欢快词语并不一致。

examples.en: The software evaluates each expression before running the program.
examples.cn: 软件在运行程序前先求值每一个表达式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「向外」加「压」——把心里的东西压出来 → 表达、表情

root: 拉丁语 exprimere「压出」= 表示「向外」的前缀 + premere「压」，其行为名词为 expressio；premere 更深来源不确定，相关印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward push: the act itself, the face that shows it, the phrase that packages it, the delivery, the formula, the gene, the pressed juice and the visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次向外的推送展开：行为本身、显现在脸上、被包进词语、表现方式、公式、基因、榨出的汁液以及可见的迹象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something inside is pressed outward and becomes visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：里面的东西被向外压出，变得可见。

branches.en: OUTWARD ACT: making an inner state public and letting it appear as a sign are the same push seen at two levels.
branches.cn: 向外的行为：把内在状态公开，与让它显现为迹象，是同一个推送在两个层面上的样子。

branches.en: FACE: the most visible surface on which feeling is pressed into view.
branches.cn: 脸：情感被压到视野里最显眼的表面。

branches.en: PACKAGED WORDS: a fixed phrase is a small box that already holds a meaning.
branches.cn: 被包好的词语：一个固定短语就是一只已经装着意义的小盒子。

branches.en: FORCE AND DELIVERY: the pressure that squeezes oil also shapes the skilled delivery of a line.
branches.cn: 力量与表现：挤压油液的压力，也塑造一句台词的熟练表达。

branches.en: SYMBOLIC AND BIOLOGICAL EXPRESSION: a formula makes a value readable, and a gene makes its instructions active.
branches.cn: 符号与生物表达：公式让数值可读，基因让指令发挥作用。

intro.en: Expression is made of a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun suffix, and the same parts build a whole family of show-and-press words.
intro.cn: expression 由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个名词后缀构成，同样的部件构成了一整族表示「压出与表现」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere 'to press' and ex- 'out' produce exprimere and its noun expressio; English adds the suffixes that build the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「压」的词根与表示「向外」的前缀构成 exprimere 及其名词 expressio；英语再加上构成词族的后缀。

items.example: The prefix directs the action away from the inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作引向外部。

items.example: The root supplies the physical force in the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供意象中的物理力量。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a name for its action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成其行为的名词。

items.example: The expression of grief took the form of silence.
items.exampleCN: 悲伤的表达采取了沉默的形式。

items.meaning: to press out; to say or show
items.example: He expressed his thanks in a short letter.
items.exampleCN: 他用一封短信表达了感谢。

items.example: Her expressive reading held the room.
items.exampleCN: 她富有表现力的朗读抓住了全场。

items.example: His expressionless face gave nothing away.
items.exampleCN: 他面无表情，没有泄露任何信息。

items.meaning: an art movement that distorts form to show feeling
items.meaningCN: 为表现情感而扭曲形式的艺术运动
items.example: Expressionism used violent colour to show inner states.
items.exampleCN: 表现主义用强烈的色彩显示内心状态。

items.example: The expressionist painted faces as blocks of colour.
items.exampleCN: 这位表现主义画家把脸画成色块。

definition_zh: 捕食性的；掠夺性的；剥削性的
definition_en: describing an animal or behaviour that hunts and kills, or an act that exploits a weaker party for gain
core_image: 一只鹰在上升气流中盘旋，影子掠过地面，田鼠立刻钻进洞里
scene: 这里指「捕食性的」。 Predatory birds circle above the marsh, forcing the rodents to stay under cover.
sceneCN: 这里 predatory 指「捕食性的」（第 1 个义项：以猎杀其他动物为生）；捕食性鸟类在沼泽上空盘旋，迫使啮齿动物躲在掩护下。图中可辨识物件：鹰、上升气流、田鼠洞、沼泽。

pos.zh: 捕食性的；掠夺性的；剥削性的（比较级 more predatory，最高级 most predatory）

senses.title: Hunting for food
senses.titleCN: 捕食性：以猎杀其他动物为生
senses.definition: describing an animal or species that hunts and kills other animals for food
senses.definitionCN: 描述以猎杀其他动物获取食物的动物或物种
senses.example: Predatory fish control the smaller species in the reef lagoon.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食性鱼类控制着礁湖中的小型物种。
senses.why: This is the literal base: the adjective marks a hunting way of life rather than a particular species.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面本义：这个形容词标出的是一种狩猎式的生活方式，而不是某个特定物种。

senses.title: Predatory pricing
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性定价：低价挤垮对手再抬价
senses.definition: in competition law, pricing below cost in order to eliminate rivals and then raise prices
senses.definitionCN: 竞争法中指以低于成本的价格消灭对手、随后再抬价的作法
senses.example: The airline was fined for predatory pricing on one regional route.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司因在一条区域航线上掠夺性定价而被罚款。
senses.why: The adjective marks intent: the low price is not generosity but a trap for competitors.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出意图：低价不是慷慨，而是给竞争者设的陷阱。

senses.title: Predatory lending
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性放贷：以不公平条件套住借款人
senses.definition: describing loans with unfair terms, hidden fees or interest designed to trap vulnerable borrowers
senses.definitionCN: 描述条款不公、费用隐蔽或利息设计成套住弱势借款人的贷款
senses.example: The regulator banned several predatory lending practices in the payday market.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者禁止了发薪日贷款市场中的若干掠夺性放贷做法。
senses.why: The prey here is a borrower, and the trap replaces the teeth: the harm comes from contract terms, not force.
senses.whyCN: 这里的猎物是借款人，合同条款代替了牙齿：伤害来自条文，而非暴力。

senses.title: Exploitative behaviour
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性行为：对弱势者的系统性剥削
senses.definition: describing conduct that targets vulnerable people and treats them as objects to be used
senses.definitionCN: 描述以弱势者为目标、把他们当作可使用之物的行为
senses.example: The inquiry found a pattern of predatory behavior toward young recruits.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现了一种针对年轻新人的掠夺性行为模式。
senses.why: The adjective carries moral weight in this sense: it says the stronger party selected weakness on purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在此义带有道德重量：它表明强势方是有意挑选弱者的。

senses.title: Predatory journal
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性期刊：收费而不审稿的出版陷阱
senses.definition: describing a publisher that charges authors fees while providing no real peer review or editorial service
senses.definitionCN: 描述只向作者收费、却不提供真正同行评审或编辑服务的出版方
senses.example: The librarian warned students away from predatory journals.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆员提醒学生远离掠夺性期刊。
senses.why: Academic publishing borrowed the word because the target is a researcher's need for publication, not their wallet alone.
senses.whyCN: 学术出版借用这个词，因为目标不只是钱包，还有研究者对发表的迫切需求。

senses.title: Predatory acquisition
senses.titleCN: 掠夺性收购：买下并拆解目标公司
senses.definition: describing a takeover whose aim is to strip assets or eliminate a competitor rather than to run the business
senses.definitionCN: 描述以剥离资产或消灭竞争者而非经营企业为目的的收购
senses.example: Workers called the takeover predatory because the buyer had already closed two rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 工人称这次收购是掠夺性的，因为买家此前已关掉两家对手。
senses.why: The financial sense keeps the hunting frame: the acquired firm is consumed, not merged with.
senses.whyCN: 金融义保留了捕猎框架：被收购的公司是被吞食，而不是被合并。

senses.title: Predatory instincts
senses.titleCN: 捕食本能：行为层面的猎杀冲动
senses.definition: describing innate behavioural drives in an animal that lead it to stalk, chase and kill
senses.definitionCN: 描述动物身上导致其跟踪、追逐与杀死的先天行为驱力
senses.example: The kitten's predatory instinct appeared before it could hunt successfully.
senses.exampleCN: 幼猫的捕食本能在它真正会狩猎之前就已显现。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes an internal drive rather than an ecological role, moving from the food web to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词描述内在驱力而非生态角色，从食物网移到行为学。

senses.title: Predatory in nature writing
senses.titleCN: 自然写作中的掠食意象：美学化的猛禽
senses.definition: used in nature writing and poetry to describe the beauty and threat of a hunter, often with admiration
senses.definitionCN: 在自然写作与诗歌中描述猎手的美感与威胁，常带赞赏
senses.example: The poem fixes on the predatory stillness of the hawk before it drops.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗聚焦于鹰俯冲前那种捕食者的静止。
senses.why: The same adjective can be admiring rather than condemnatory when the context is wild nature instead of markets.
senses.whyCN: 当语境是荒野而非市场时，同一个形容词可以是赞赏而非谴责。

intro.en: Predatory comes from Latin praedatorius 'of plunder', an adjective on praedator. English first used it of raiding and later of hunting.
intro.cn: predatory 出自拉丁语 praedatorius「劫掠的」，是 praedator 的形容词。英语先用它指劫掠，后用于捕猎。

items.en: The adjective praedatorius described what belongs to plunder or a plunderer. Its stem is praeda 'booty'.
items.cn: 形容词 praedatorius 描述属于劫掠或劫掠者的事物，其词干是 praeda「战利品」。

items.en: Predatory entered English in the seventeenth century in the sense of plundering. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: predatory 在 17 世纪进入英语，取劫掠义；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: As natural history grew in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, the adjective shifted toward animals that live by hunting.
items.cn: 随着 18、19 世纪博物学发展，这个形容词转向指以狩猎为生的动物。

items.en: Twentieth-century law produced predatory pricing and predatory lending, where the adjective marks deliberate harm to weaker parties.
items.cn: 20 世纪法律造出掠夺性定价与掠夺性放贷，此时形容词标出对弱势方的有意伤害。

items.en: The phrase predatory journal spread in the twenty-first century with open-access publishing, and its boundaries are still debated.
items.cn: 掠夺性期刊这一说法随开放获取出版在 21 世纪扩散，其边界至今仍有争论。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adjective from its noun relatives; the near-meaning group separates predatory from merely aggressive or parasitic.
note.cn: 形近组把这个形容词与名词同族词分开；近义组区分掠夺性与单纯强势或寄生。

entries.definition: The animal or party that hunts. It is a count noun, so it cannot stand where an adjective is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 指狩猎的动物或一方。它是可数名词，不能放在需要形容词的位置。

entries.definition: The process of killing and eating. Predatory describes the quality; predation names the process.
entries.definitionCN: 指杀死并取食的过程。predatory 描述性质，predation 命名过程。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective with the same hunting sense, now mostly used of insects. It is not interchangeable with the noun predator.
entries.definitionCN: 较罕见的同义形容词，如今多用于昆虫。它不能与名词 predator 互换。

entries.definition: Means grasping and greedy, usually of people or institutions. It condemns appetite for gain and is never used for a hawk.
entries.definitionCN: 意为贪婪攫取的，通常用于人或机构。它谴责对利益的贪欲，从不用于鹰。

entries.definition: Describes unfair use of others. It is the plain-language equivalent of figurative predatory, without the animal image.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不公平地利用他人。它是比喻义 predatory 的平实说法，不含动物意象。

entries.definition: Describes feeding on a host that usually survives. Predatory behaviour kills or destroys, while parasitic behaviour drains.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以通常仍存活的宿主为食。掠夺性行为会杀死或摧毁，寄生性行为则慢慢吸取。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: predator + -y: having the nature of a predator.
normal.cn: predator + -y：具有捕食者性质的。

normal.en: Typical phrases: predatory pricing, predatory lending, predatory behavior, predatory journal.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：掠夺性定价、掠夺性放贷、掠夺性行为、掠夺性期刊。

normal.en: The family runs predator, predation, predacious, predatorily and predatoriness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 predator、predation、predacious、predatorily、predatoriness。

normal.en: Rapacious is greedy; predatory is hunting. Only the first names an appetite.
normal.cn: rapacious 指贪婪；predatory 指捕猎。只有前者命名一种欲望。

normal.en: The same adjective can condemn a lender or admire a hawk, depending on context.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词可以谴责放贷者，也可以赞赏鹰，取决于语境。

abstract.en: Picture a hawk circling without moving its wings, a shadow sliding over the marsh.
abstract.cn: 想象鹰不扇翅地盘旋，影子滑过沼泽。

abstract.en: Picture a payday office on a poor street, its sign promising cash and its contract hiding fees.
abstract.cn: 想象贫困街区的一家发薪日贷款门店，招牌承诺现金，合同却藏着费用。

abstract.en: Picture a journal that accepts a paper in two days and sends an invoice the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一本期刊两天内接收论文，第二天就寄来账单。

examples.en: Predatory birds keep the marsh rodents under dense cover.
examples.cn: 捕食性鸟类让沼泽里的啮齿动物躲在密丛下。

examples.en: The court found the below-cost pricing predatory.
examples.cn: 法院认定这种低于成本的定价属掠夺性定价。

examples.en: Students were warned about predatory journals that mimic legitimate titles.
examples.cn: 学生们被提醒警惕那些模仿正规刊名的掠夺性期刊。

dict_mnemonic.text: predator（捕食者）+ y（……的）→ 像捕食者一样的 → predatory 掠夺性的

root: 拉丁 praeda「战利品」→ praedator「劫掠者」→ praedatorius「劫掠的」→ 英语 predatory；后由「劫掠」转为「捕食」与「掠夺性」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all modify something with a hunting quality: a bird, a price, a loan, a journal or an instinct.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都用这个形容词修饰某种带有捕猎性质的东西：鸟、价格、贷款、期刊或本能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hawk circling over the marsh while a shadow slides across the grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：鹰在沼泽上空盘旋，影子滑过草地。

branches.en: THE INSTINCT: a hunting drive written into behaviour.
branches.cn: 捕食本能：写进行为层面的猎杀驱力。

branches.en: MARKETS: price and credit become traps set for rivals and borrowers.
branches.cn: 市场：价格与信贷变成给对手和借款人设下的陷阱。

branches.en: CONDUCT: the adjective condemns deliberate targeting of vulnerability.
branches.cn: 行为：这个形容词谴责有意挑选弱点下手。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: journals and acquirers consume the party they pretend to serve.
branches.cn: 机构：期刊与收购方吞食它们声称服务的对象。

branches.en: DOUBLE TONE: literal hunting and poetry's admiring eye share one adjective.
branches.cn: 双重语气：字面的猎食与诗歌里欣赏的目光共用同一个形容词。

intro.en: Predatory is a Latin adjective ending in -ory, built on the agent noun for a plunderer.
intro.cn: predatory 是以 -ory 结尾的拉丁形容词，建立在表示劫掠者的施动名词之上。

latinIntro.en: Praeda is the root, -ator the agent, and -orius the adjective suffix meaning 'belonging to'.
latinIntro.cn: praeda 是词根，-ator 是施动成分，-orius 是意为「属于……」的形容词后缀。

items.meaning: of or like a plunderer or hunter
items.meaningCN: 属于劫掠者或猎手的，或像其一样的
items.example: The firm's predatory tactics drew scrutiny.
items.exampleCN: 该公司的掠夺性策略引来审查。

items.example: The predator waited at the water hole.
items.exampleCN: 捕食者在水坑边等待。

items.example: Predation fell after the pack moved north.
items.exampleCN: 狼群北迁后捕食减少。

items.example: Predacious mites eat pest eggs.
items.exampleCN: 捕食性螨虫吃害虫卵。

items.structure: Old French preie, from Latin praeda
items.example: The prey ran for the treeline.
items.exampleCN: 猎物朝林线奔去。

items.example: Depredation by gulls emptied the nests.
items.exampleCN: 海鸥的劫掠清空了鸟巢。

items.example: The lender acted predatorily toward desperate borrowers.
items.exampleCN: 放贷者对走投无路的借款人采取掠夺性做法。

items.example: Critics noted the predatoriness of the business model.
items.exampleCN: 批评者指出了该商业模式的掠夺性。

items.example: Rapacious landlords raised rents twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 贪婪的房东一年涨两次租。

definition_zh: 遗传变异；遗传差异
definition_en: differences in genes and gene frequencies among individuals of a population
core_image: 同一批种子撒进同一块田，长出的植株却高矮不一、叶色深浅不同
scene: 同一批种子撒在同一块田里，长出的植株却高矮不一。研究员记录： Genetic variation within the population helps it survive drought.
sceneCN: 这里指「群体内部的遗传变异」（第 1 个义项：同一群体个体间基因与等位基因频率的差异）；句意为群体内的遗传变异有助于它度过干旱。

pos.zh: 遗传变异；遗传差异（不可数；指多种变异时偶用复数 genetic variations）

derivatives.zh: 基因
遗传学
遗传学家
遗传的；基因的
变异；变化
变化；使不同

senses.title: Differences within a population
senses.definition: differences in genes and gene frequencies among members of one population
senses.definitionCN: 同一群体成员之间基因与等位基因频率的差异
senses.example: Genetic variation within the population helps it survive drought.
senses.exampleCN: 群体内的遗传变异有助于它度过干旱。
senses.why: The phrase joins a cause (genes) to a result (difference), naming the raw diversity that a population already carries.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把原因（基因）与结果（差异）并置，命名群体已经携带的原始多样性。

senses.title: Differences between individuals
senses.definition: genetic differences between two or more individuals
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个个体之间的基因差异
senses.example: Genetic variation between the twins came from different mutations.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎之间的遗传差异来自不同的突变。
senses.why: At the smallest scale the phrase compares individuals, and any two genomes differ at many positions.
senses.whyCN: 在最小尺度上，这个短语比较个体，而任意两个基因组在许多位置上都有差异。

senses.title: Genetic diversity of a species
senses.titleCN: 物种层面的遗传多样性
senses.definition: the total genetic diversity carried by a species across its range
senses.definitionCN: 一个物种在其分布范围内携带的全部遗传多样性
senses.example: The species retains high genetic variation across its mountain range.
senses.exampleCN: 该物种在整条山脉中保持着高度的遗传变异。
senses.why: Summed over many populations, individual differences become a species-level resource.
senses.whyCN: 把许多群体加总，个体差异就变成物种层面的资源。

senses.title: Heritable variation
senses.definition: variation that can be passed from parents to offspring
senses.definitionCN: 能够由亲代传给后代的变异
senses.example: Only heritable genetic variation responds to selection.
senses.exampleCN: 只有可遗传的遗传变异才会回应选择。
senses.why: The adjective genetic narrows variation to what sits in the genes, so it can be inherited.
senses.whyCN: 形容词「遗传的」把变异限定在基因之中，因此它可以被继承。

senses.title: Its sources: mutation and recombination
senses.definition: the new variation produced by mutation, recombination and gene flow
senses.definitionCN: 由突变、重组与基因流动产生的新变异
senses.example: Mutation creates the genetic variation on which recombination acts.
senses.exampleCN: 突变产生遗传变异，重组再对它起作用。
senses.why: Variation is not self-generating: the phrase points back to the processes that write new differences into DNA.
senses.whyCN: 变异不会自己产生：这个短语回溯到那些把新差异写进脱氧核糖核酸的过程。

senses.title: A measurable quantity
senses.definition: a quantity estimated from allele frequencies or trait measurements
senses.definitionCN: 由等位基因频率或性状测量估算出的量
senses.example: The team measured genetic variation at a thousand sites.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在一千个位点上测量了遗传变异。
senses.why: Once variation is counted, it becomes a number that can be compared across populations and years.
senses.whyCN: 一旦变异被计数，它就成了可以在群体与年份之间比较的数值。

senses.title: The raw material of evolution
senses.definition: the differences that natural selection can act on over generations
senses.definitionCN: 自然选择可以在世代间作用其上的差异
senses.example: Without genetic variation, a population cannot adapt.
senses.exampleCN: 没有遗传变异，群体就无法适应。
senses.why: Evolution needs alternatives to sort; genetic variation supplies those alternatives.
senses.whyCN: 进化需要可供筛选的备选，遗传变异提供这些备选。

senses.title: The basis of breeding selection
senses.definition: the variation that breeders use to improve crops or livestock
senses.definitionCN: 育种者用来改良作物或畜禽的变异
senses.example: Breeders depend on genetic variation to raise yield.
senses.exampleCN: 育种者依靠遗传变异来提高产量。
senses.why: Artificial selection is natural selection put to work, and it also needs heritable differences to choose among.
senses.whyCN: 人工选择是被投入使用的自然选择，同样需要可遗传的差异可供挑选。

intro.en: Genetic goes back to Greek genesis 'origin, generation', while variation comes from Latin variare 'to change'. The phrase became standard with population genetics in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: genetic 追溯到希腊 genesis「起源、生成」，variation 来自拉丁 variare「改变」。这个短语随 20 世纪的群体遗传学成为标准说法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Genesis meant 'origin, source, generation'. It comes from gignesthai 'to be born' and is related to genos 'race, kind'.
items.cn: genesis 意为「起源、来源、生成」，出自 gignesthai「出生」，与 genos「种族、种类」相关。

items.en: The adjective genetic entered English in the nineteenth century; the noun genetics for the science is generally dated to about 1905 and is associated with William Bateson.
items.cn: 形容词 genetic 在 19 世纪进入英语；指这门科学的名词 genetics 一般定在 1905 年前后，与 William Bateson 相关。

items.en: Variation comes from Latin variare 'to change' and varius 'varied'; it names difference rather than origin.
items.cn: variation 来自拉丁 variare「改变」与 varius「多样的」，命名的是差异，而非起源。

items.en: The exact phrase genetic variation spread in the early twentieth century with the study of allele frequencies in populations.
items.cn: genetic variation 这一确切短语在 20 世纪初随群体中等位基因频率的研究而传播。

items.en: Modern biology treats the phrase as a measurable property and links it to mutation, recombination, gene flow and selection.
items.cn: 现代生物学把这个短语当作一种可测属性，并把它与突变、重组、基因流动和选择联系起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates and root): the earliest printed use of the full phrase is not established, and the deeper origin of Latin varius is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与词根）：完整短语的最早印刷使用没有定论；拉丁 varius 的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built on the same gene or variation stock that are easily swapped; group two holds neighbouring concepts that also describe biological difference.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 gene 或 variation 词干、容易被替换的短语；第二组是同样描述生物差异的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The variety of genes within a group, viewed as a resource or a state; genetic variation stresses the differences themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个群体内基因的多样，被看作资源或状态；genetic variation 强调差异本身。

entries.definition: A difference between two particular genomes; the phrase genetic variation is collective and population-level.
entries.definitionCN: 指两个具体基因组之间的差别；genetic variation 是集体的、群体层面的。

entries.definition: Variation in observable traits, which may or may not be genetic; the two are often confused.
entries.definitionCN: 指可观察性状的变异，可能来自基因也可能不是；两者常被混淆。

entries.definition: A single change in DNA; genetic variation is the accumulated differences that many mutations help create.
entries.definitionCN: 指脱氧核糖核酸中的一次改变；genetic variation 是许多突变共同造成的累积差异。

entries.definition: The proportion of a particular allele in a population; it is how genetic variation is often quantified.
entries.definitionCN: 指某个等位基因在群体中的比例，是量化遗传变异的常用方式。

entries.definition: The total set of alleles in a population; it is the container that holds the variation.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个群体中全部等位基因的集合，是容纳变异的容器。

entries.definition: The presence of two or more distinct forms in a population; it is a pattern, while variation is the general property.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体中存在两种或更多明显形式；它是一种格局，而 variation 是一般属性。

entries.definition: The proportion of trait variation due to genetic differences; it measures the genetic share of variation.
entries.definitionCN: 指性状变异中由基因差异造成的比例，衡量变异里遗传所占的份额。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: gen- 'birth, origin' + -etic 'relating to': relating to what is born from parents.
normal.cn: gen-「出生、起源」+ -etic「与……相关的」：与从亲代出生相关。

normal.en: vari- 'different' + -ation 'the act of': the act of differing.
normal.cn: vari-「不同」+ -ation「……的行为」：表现出差异的行为。

normal.en: Genetic variation is the raw material; mutation, recombination and gene flow supply it.
normal.cn: 遗传变异是原材料；突变、重组与基因流动提供它。

normal.en: The phrase pairs with selection: variation is what selection sorts.
normal.cn: 这个短语与选择配对：变异正是选择所筛选的对象。

normal.en: Measured by allele frequencies, it becomes a number for comparison.
normal.cn: 通过等位基因频率测量，它成为可供比较的数值。

abstract.en: Picture a field of seedlings of slightly different heights, all from one seed lot.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田里的苗高矮略有不同，却都来自同一批种子。

abstract.en: Picture a deck of cards where every hand is dealt a different combination.
abstract.cn: 想象一副牌，每一手都发到不同的组合。

abstract.en: Picture a library where each copy of a book has a few handwritten corrections.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每本书都有几处手写修改。

examples.en: Genetic variation lets a population answer a new disease.
examples.cn: 遗传变异让一个群体能够回应一种新疾病。

examples.en: The island's genetic variation fell after a century of isolation.
examples.cn: 经过一个世纪的隔离，这座岛的遗传变异减少了。

examples.en: Conservation plans try to protect genetic variation, not just species numbers.
examples.cn: 保护计划试图保护遗传变异，而不只是物种数量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「基因的变样」——同一批种子长出的苗各有各的样子 → 遗传变异

root: 希腊 genesis「起源、生成」（经 genetic）+ 拉丁 variare「改变」与 varius「多样的」；拉丁 genus「出生、族类」为同源词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one resource: differences written in genes are counted within individuals, populations and species, then read as evolution's material and as a breeding tool.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一种资源展开：写在基因里的差异，先在个体、群体与物种层面被计数，再被读成进化的材料与育种的工具。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one seed lot growing into plants of different heights.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一批种子长成高低不同的植株。

branches.en: INDIVIDUAL AND POPULATION: pairwise differences add up to a population property.
branches.cn: 个体与群体：成对的差异累加为群体属性。

branches.en: SPECIES SCALE AND MEASURE: the stored diversity becomes a quantity estimated from samples.
branches.cn: 物种尺度与测量：储存的多样性成为由样本估算的量。

branches.en: HERITABLE AND GENERATED: only inherited variation counts, and mutation plus recombination writes it.
branches.cn: 可遗传与来源：只有可继承的变异才算数，突变与重组把它写入。

branches.en: EVOLUTION: selection needs alternatives, and this is the supply.
branches.cn: 进化：选择需要备选，而这就是供应。

branches.en: BREEDING: artificial selection puts the same supply to work.
branches.cn: 育种：人工选择让同一供应发挥作用。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective of origin to a Latin-derived noun of difference; both are free words, and the compound is a technical collocation rather than a prefixed root.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊来源的「起源」形容词接在拉丁来源的「差异」名词上；两者都是自由词，整个短语是专业搭配，而非前缀加词根。

latinIntro.en: The Greek family gives gene, genetics and genetic, while Latin gives variation, variable and vary; Latin genus is a cognate of Greek genos, not its source.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词族提供 gene、genetics 与 genetic，拉丁词族提供 variation、variable 与 vary；拉丁 genus 与希腊 genos 同源，但不是后者的来源。

items.structure: Greek genos (race, kind) / gignesthai (to be born)
items.example: The element opens gene, genesis and genetics.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分出现在 gene、genesis 与 genetics 开头。

items.example: Genetic means relating to origin and inheritance.
items.exampleCN: genetic 意为与起源和遗传相关。

items.example: One gene may have many alleles.
items.exampleCN: 一个基因可以有许多等位基因。

items.example: Genetics began with breeding experiments.
items.exampleCN: 遗传学始于育种实验。

items.example: The geneticist mapped the trait.
items.exampleCN: 遗传学家定位了该性状。

items.example: The element opens variation and variable.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分出现在 variation 与 variable 开头。

items.example: Variation is the result of varying.
items.exampleCN: variation 是变化的结果。

items.example: Variation in height is easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 高度的差异很容易看见。

items.example: Allele frequencies vary by region.
items.exampleCN: 等位基因频率因地区而异。

items.example: Genetic variation is the raw material of selection.

senses.title: Shaped like or arranged along a line
senses.definition: forming a straight line or arranged in a line, with no bend or branch
senses.definitionCN: 构成一条直线或排成一行，没有弯折或分支
senses.example: The chairs stood in a linear row along the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子沿墙排成一条直线。
senses.why: Linearis comes from linea 'a line', so the first sense simply repeats the shape of a drawn line.
senses.whyCN: linearis 出自 linea「线」，第一义就是把一条画出的线的形状说出来。

senses.title: Arranged in a fixed order
senses.definition: proceeding step by step in one fixed order, said of stories, arguments or processes
senses.definitionCN: 按一个固定次序一步步推进，用于故事、论证或流程
senses.example: The film tells a linear story from childhood to old age.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片按线性顺序讲一个从童年到老年的故事。
senses.why: A line has a direction, so a sequence that never jumps back and forth is pictured as a line.
senses.whyCN: 线有方向，因此从不来回跳跃的顺序就被想象成一条线。

senses.title: Changing by a constant rate
senses.definition: increasing or decreasing by a fixed amount for each unit of change in the other quantity
senses.definitionCN: 另一个量每变化一个单位，就按固定数量增加或减少
senses.example: Their savings showed linear growth of fifty pounds a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的存款每月固定增加五十英镑，呈线性增长。
senses.why: On a graph a constant rate draws a straight line, so the arithmetic of equal steps is called linear.
senses.whyCN: 在图上固定速率画出来就是直线，因此等步长的算术关系被称为线性。

senses.title: First-degree in algebra
senses.definition: containing variables only to the first power, with no squares, products or higher terms
senses.definitionCN: 变量只出现一次方，没有平方、乘积或更高次项
senses.example: Solve the linear equation before trying the quadratic one.
senses.exampleCN: 先解这个一次方程，再去碰二次方程。
senses.why: A first-degree equation plots as a straight line, which is why algebra borrowed the geometric name.
senses.whyCN: 一次方程画出来是直线，代数因此借用了几何的名字。

senses.title: Plain and uncomplicated reasoning
senses.definition: simple and direct, moving from one point to the next without side branches
senses.definitionCN: 简单直接，从一点推到下一点，不绕旁支
senses.example: A linear approach works here, with no need for negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 这里用简单直接的思路就行，不必反复磋商。
senses.why: Thinking that never loops back is pictured as walking a straight path, the same image as the geometry.
senses.whyCN: 不绕回来的思考被想象成走一条直路，与几何义是同一幅画。

senses.title: Measured in one dimension
senses.definition: measured along a single dimension, such as length, rather than area or volume
senses.definitionCN: 沿单一维度测量，如长度，而非面积或体积
senses.example: The survey recorded linear measure in metres, not area.
senses.exampleCN: 这次测量记录的是以米计的长度，而不是面积。
senses.why: A line has length but no width, so a one-dimensional quantity is naturally called linear.
senses.whyCN: 线有长度没有宽度，一维的量自然被称为线性。

senses.title: Direct descent in a family
senses.definition: descending in an unbroken direct line from an ancestor, without collateral branches
senses.definitionCN: 从祖先一脉直传，不分出旁支
senses.example: The estate passed down the linear descent of the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业沿长子的直系血脉传下去。
senses.why: A family tree drawn as a single unbroken line gives the word its genealogical sense.
senses.whyCN: 把家谱画成一条不断的线，就得到这个词的谱系义。

senses.title: Proportional output in electronics
senses.definition: producing an output that rises or falls in direct proportion to the input, with no distortion
senses.definitionCN: 输出随输入按正比升降，不发生失真
senses.example: A linear amplifier keeps the wave shape unchanged.
senses.exampleCN: 线性放大器让波形保持不变。
senses.why: An undistorted signal keeps a one-to-one relation with its input, the electronic form of a straight line.
senses.whyCN: 不失真的信号与输入保持一一对应，就是直线关系在电子学里的形态。

intro.en: Linear is Latin linearis 'of a line', built on linea 'line, thread', which itself comes from linum 'flax'. English adopted the adjective in the seventeenth century, and mathematics later extended it to equations and proportional relations. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: linear 出自拉丁 linearis「线的」，由 linea「线、线绳」构成，而 linea 又出自 linum「亚麻」。英语十七世纪引入这个形容词，数学后来把它扩展到方程与比例关系。年代均为约数。

items.en: Linum meant 'flax', the plant whose fibres made the thread; linen also comes from this word.
items.cn: linum 意为「亚麻」，其纤维可以搓成线；linen 也出自这个词。

items.en: Linea was first a linen thread and then any drawn line; the physical thread is the origin of the geometric line.
items.cn: linea 最初指亚麻线，后来指任何画出的线；实体的线绳是几何直线的来源。

items.en: Linearis meant 'belonging to a line'; it described things laid out along a line before it described equations.
items.cn: linearis 意为「属于线的」，先形容沿直线排布的事物，后才用于方程。

items.en: English took the adjective from Latin, first for shapes and rows, and later for anything arranged in sequence.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语借入这个形容词，先用于形状与排列，后用于按顺序展开的事物。

items.en: The coordinate method of the seventeenth century showed that first-degree equations plot as straight lines, fixing the mathematical sense of linear.
items.cn: 十七世纪的坐标法证明一次方程画出来是直线，从而固定了 linear 的数学含义。

items.en: First English citation uncertain: the direct source is Latin linearis, attested in the classical language, so the word itself is not in doubt; only the exact date of its first English use is not recorded. The deeper origin of linum is not established, and no reconstructed root is asserted here.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：直接来源是有据可查的拉丁语 linearis，词本身并不存疑；只是英语最早用例的年代没有记录。linum 的更早来源没有定论，此处不给出重构词根。

note.en: Group one shares the linea stock, where Latin thread and line produce English words for straightness, ancestry and alignment; group two holds words that name the same simple geometry from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组共享 linea 词干，拉丁语的线与线绳衍生出表示笔直、血统与对齐的英语词；第二组从别的角度命名同一种简单几何。

entries.definition: Descending in a direct line from an ancestor; it keeps the family-tree sense but not the equation sense.

entries.definition: A feature or outline of a face or landscape, from the same Latin line; it never means proportional.
entries.definitionCN: 面部或地貌的轮廓线条，同出拉丁 linea；从不表示成比例。

entries.definition: From French aligner, ultimately linea: to bring things onto a shared line, the verb behind alignment.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语 aligner 上溯到 linea：把东西排到同一条线上，也是 alignment 的动词。

entries.definition: Having no bend; it describes the shape but not proportional change or first-degree equations.
entries.definitionCN: 没有弯折；只描述形状，不表示比例变化或一次方程。

entries.definition: Following in order, one after another; it covers the narrative sense without the geometric one.
entries.definitionCN: 按次序一个接一个；覆盖叙事义，但不含几何义。

entries.definition: Changing by a fixed ratio; close to the growth sense but says nothing about a drawn line.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定比率变化；接近增长义，但不涉及画出的线。

entries.definition: Having a single dimension; it matches the length sense and is never used for algebra.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个维度；对应长度义，从不用于代数。

abstract.cn: 想象一根线从板子的一角拉到另一角。

abstract.en: Picture equal steps on a staircase, never wider and never narrower.

abstract.en: Picture a story told from birth to old age with no flashback.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从出生讲到老年、没有倒叙的故事。

examples.en: The data fit a linear model far better than a curved one.
examples.cn: 数据与线性模型的吻合程度远好于曲线模型。

examples.en: She preferred a linear plot because the audience could follow it easily.
examples.cn: 她偏爱线性情节，因为观众容易跟上。

examples.en: The engineer checked that the amplifier stayed linear across the whole range.

root: 拉丁 linearis「线的」= linea（线、亚麻线，出自 linum「亚麻」）+ -alis（属于……的）。英语十七世纪借入。同根词有 line、lineal、lineament、align。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep to one line: a drawn straight shape, a fixed sequence, a constant rate, a first-degree equation, plain reasoning, one-dimensional measure, direct descent and an undistorted electronic output.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一条线：画出的直线形状、固定顺序、固定速率、一次方程、简单思路、一维长度、直系血统，以及不失真的电子输出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread stretched straight, with no bend, fork or loop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被拉直的线，不弯、不分叉、不打圈。

branches.en: SHAPE AND MEASURE: a line has length but no breadth, so the drawn form and the one-dimensional quantity are the same object.
branches.cn: 形状与度量：线有长度没有宽度，画出的形状与一维的量正是同一个对象。

branches.en: UNBROKEN ORDER: a story with no flashback and a family with no side branch are both single continuous lines.
branches.cn: 不断的顺序：没有倒叙的故事与没有旁支的家族，都是唯一一条连续的线。

branches.en: RATE AND EQUATION: equal steps give a constant slope, and a first-degree equation plots as that slope.
branches.cn: 速率与方程：等步长给出固定斜率，一次方程画出来就是这条斜线。

branches.en: PLAIN THINKING: reasoning that never loops back walks the same straight path with the feet of the mind.
branches.cn: 简单思路：不绕回来的推理，是用心思的脚步走同一条直路。

branches.en: FAITHFUL OUTPUT: an undistorted signal keeps a one-to-one relation with its input, a straight line in electronics.
branches.cn: 忠实输出：不失真的信号与输入保持一一对应，就是电子学里的直线。

intro.en: Linear is a Latin adjective built on a noun and a suffix, and the same pieces also build the geometry, the family words and the everyday verb for alignment.
intro.cn: linear 是由名词加后缀构成的拉丁形容词，同样的构件也造出几何词、家族词与表示对齐的日常动词。

latinIntro.cn: linea「线绳」衍生 line、lineal、lineament 与 align；-alis「属于……」在英语留下 -al，non- 则否定整个形容词。

intro.en: Drudgery is drudge plus -ery, the ending that names a kind of work or a place of work; a drudge is the person bent over the task, and drudgery is the task itself.
intro.cn: drudgery 由 drudge 加 -ery 构成，这个后缀指称某类工作或工作场所；drudge 是弓着背干活的人，drudgery 就是那份活本身。

items.en: Old English dreogan means to endure or to carry out a task.
items.cn: 古英语 dreogan 意为忍受或完成一项任务。

items.en: Middle English druggen means to drag or to pull heavily.
items.cn: 中古英语 druggen 意为拖或沉重地拉。

items.en: English drudge appears for a person who does mean servile work.
items.cn: 英语 drudge 出现，指做低贱苦役的人。

items.en: The noun drudgery is formed with -ery for the work such a person does.
items.cn: 名词 drudgery 用 -ery 构成，指这样的人所做的活。

items.en: Writers use drudgery for the dull labour that machines begin to replace.
items.cn: 作家用 drudgery 指机器开始替代的单调劳动。

items.en: The word now covers housework, form filling and any joyless repeated task.
items.cn: 这个词如今涵盖家务、填表以及任何无乐趣的重复任务。

note.en: Drudgery shares its heavy opening with drubbing and drugging, while its neighbours name other kinds of joyless labour.
note.cn: drudgery 与 drubbing、drugging 共用沉重的开头，而它的近义词则指别的无乐趣劳动。

definition_en: describing a relationship or partner in which both sides gain, especially in ecology, and by extension any arrangement built on reciprocal benefit

senses.title: Both sides profit
senses.titleCN: 双方获利：关系本身是加加评分
senses.definition: describing a relationship in which each participant receives a net benefit from the other
senses.definitionCN: 描述每一方都从对方获得净收益的关系
senses.example: The cleaner fish and the reef fish have a mutualistic relationship.
senses.exampleCN: 清洁鱼与礁鱼之间是互利共生关系。
senses.why: The adjective attaches the plus-plus score to a specific relationship, so it answers the question of what kind of association this is.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把「加加评分」挂到具体关系上，用来回答这究竟是怎样一种关系。

senses.title: Describing a partner
senses.titleCN: 描述伙伴：作为其中一方的属性
senses.definition: describing one organism as a beneficial partner that supplies a service or resource to another
senses.definitionCN: 描述某个生物作为有益伙伴，向另一方提供服务或资源
senses.example: Certain fungi are mutualistic partners that help tree roots absorb phosphorus.
senses.exampleCN: 某些真菌是互利共生伙伴，帮助树根吸收磷。
senses.why: The same adjective can modify the partner rather than the pair, because a partnership is named from the side that gives as well as from the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词既可以修饰伙伴、也可以修饰整对关系，因为伙伴关系既能从整体命名，也能从给予的一方命名。

senses.title: Coevolved traits
senses.titleCN: 共同演化的性状：解剖结构彼此匹配
senses.definition: describing traits that have been shaped by reciprocal selection, such as matching flower depth and insect tongue length
senses.definitionCN: 描述被相互选择塑造出的性状，如花管深度与昆虫舌长彼此匹配
senses.example: The long proboscis is a mutualistic adaptation to the deep flower tube.
senses.exampleCN: 长口器是对深花管的一种互利共生适应。
senses.why: The adjective extends from the relationship to its anatomical footprint, marking a history of reciprocal selection.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从关系扩展到它留下的解剖学痕迹，标示一段相互选择的历史。

senses.title: Microbial partnership
senses.titleCN: 微生物伙伴：菌群与宿主的互惠
senses.definition: describing microbes that supply nutrients or protection to a host while receiving habitat and food
senses.definitionCN: 描述向宿主提供养分或保护、同时获得栖息地与食物的微生物
senses.example: The gut hosts a mutualistic community that digests fibre for its animal host.
senses.exampleCN: 肠道中栖居着一个互利共生群落，替动物宿主消化纤维。
senses.why: Microbiology borrowed the adjective because the accounting is the same as in a reef: both the bug and the body gain.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学借用这个形容词，因为账目与礁石上相同：细菌与身体都获益。

senses.title: Economic reciprocity
senses.titleCN: 经济互惠：组织之间的互利安排
senses.definition: describing a commercial or institutional arrangement in which each party supplies something the other needs
senses.definitionCN: 描述商业或机构安排中，每一方都提供对方所需之物
senses.example: The two firms formed a mutualistic alliance to share distribution networks.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司结成互利联盟，共享配送网络。
senses.why: The biological adjective travels into business because the test is unchanged: each side must leave better off, or the alliance is not mutualistic.
senses.whyCN: 这个生物学形容词进入商业领域，因为检验标准没变：双方必须都更受益，否则联盟就称不上互利。

senses.title: Social cooperation
senses.titleCN: 社会合作：互助组织的互惠性质
senses.definition: describing cooperation among people or groups that is organised so that every participant gains
senses.definitionCN: 描述人与人、团体与团体之间被组织成让每个参与者都获益的合作
senses.example: The village's mutualistic grain bank lent seed in spring and received grain after harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的互惠粮库春天借出种子，秋收后收回粮食。
senses.why: Once people copy the ecological pattern, the adjective describes a designed institution rather than a natural symbiosis.
senses.whyCN: 当人们仿照生态模式行事，这个形容词描述的就是被设计出来的制度，而非自然共生。

senses.title: The contrastive label
senses.titleCN: 对照标签：与偏利、寄生相对
senses.definition: used to classify a relationship when it is placed beside commensal or parasitic ones
senses.definitionCN: 在把关系与偏利共生、寄生并列分类时使用的标签
senses.example: Field data showed the association was mutualistic rather than commensal.
senses.exampleCN: 野外数据表明这段关系是互利共生的，而不是偏利的。
senses.why: Classification needs an adjective, not a noun phrase: mutualistic marks the plus-plus cell of the three-cell table.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要一个形容词而不是名词短语：mutualistic 标出三分表格里的「加加」格。

senses.title: Figurative mutual benefit
senses.titleCN: 比喻式互利：抽象关系也可用
senses.definition: used figuratively of abstract exchanges, such as a writer and an editor who each improve the other's work
senses.definitionCN: 比喻地用于抽象交换，如作者与编辑互相提升对方的工作
senses.example: Their long collaboration was mutualistic: each made the other sharper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们长期合作是互利的：彼此都让对方更敏锐。
senses.why: The metaphor survives because there is still a measurable trade, even though neither side is a species.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻站得住，因为仍存在可衡量的交换，即便双方都不是物种。

intro.en: Mutualistic is the adjective built on mutualism with -istic, so its history is the history of mutuus plus two layers of suffix.
intro.cn: mutualistic 是在 mutualism 上加 -istic 构成的形容词，它的历史就是 mutuus 加两层后缀的历史。

items.en: Mutuus meant reciprocal or exchanged, and it names the core of every later form in this family.
items.cn: mutuus 意为相互的、交换的，它命名了这一词族后世所有形式的核心。

items.en: Old French mutuel brought the adjective into English by the fifteenth century, where it first described shared feelings and duties.
items.cn: 古法语 mutuel 在 15 世纪把这个形容词带进英语，最初描述共同的情感与义务。

items.en: The noun added -ism to name a system of reciprocity, first in political economy and later in ecology.
items.cn: 名词形式加 -ism，用来命名一套互惠体系，先见于政治经济学，后用于生态学。

items.en: The suffix -istic descends from Greek -istikos through Latin -isticus, forming adjectives for people or things that practise or embody something.
items.cn: 后缀 -istic 经拉丁语 -isticus 源自希腊语 -istikos，构成表示「从事或体现某事」的形容词。

items.en: The adjective became common in ecology in the twentieth century as textbooks needed to classify relationships quickly. Its first use is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学教科书需要快速给关系分类，这个形容词因而普及；其首见年代没有精确记载。

note.en: The look-alike group differs only by suffix but changes part of speech; the near-meaning group names the neighbouring relationship types.
note.cn: 形近组只差后缀却改变词性；近义组则列出相邻的关系类型。

entries.definition: The relationship or doctrine itself. You can study mutualism, but you cannot say that a pair of species is mutualism.
entries.definitionCN: 指关系或学说本身。可以说研究 mutualism，但不能说一对物种是 mutualism。

entries.definition: A noun for one partner or one supporter. It is a person or organism, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指一方伙伴或一名支持者，是人或生物，而非性质。

entries.definition: The abstract quality of being reciprocal. It cannot describe a species or a relationship type.
entries.definitionCN: 指相互性的抽象性质，不能用来描述某个物种或某类关系。

entries.definition: Describes any close lasting association, whether mutualistic, commensal or parasitic. It does not commit to who gains.
entries.definitionCN: 描述任何紧密持久的共处，无论互利、偏利还是寄生，不判定谁获益。

entries.definition: Describes the plus-zero case. Using it where both sides gain understates the benefit to the second partner.
entries.definitionCN: 描述加零情形。若双方都获益却用这个词，就低估了第二方的收益。

entries.definition: Describes the plus-minus case. It is the opposite of mutualistic in ecological scoring.
entries.definitionCN: 描述加减情形，在生态学评分上是互利共生的反面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: mutualism + -istic: the adjective form of the plus-plus system.
normal.cn: mutualism + -istic：加加体系的形容词形式。

normal.en: The chain runs mutual, mutualism, mutualist, mutualistic, mutualistically.
normal.cn: 词族链条是 mutual、mutualism、mutualist、mutualistic、mutualistically。

normal.en: Typical collocations: mutualistic relationship, mutualistic symbiosis, mutualistic interaction.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：互利共生关系、互利共生、互利互动。

normal.en: Contrast the three adjectives: mutualistic, commensal, parasitic.
normal.cn: 对照三个形容词：互利、偏利、寄生。

normal.en: The suffix -istic builds adjectives from -ism nouns, as in capitalistic and mutualistic.
normal.cn: 后缀 -istic 从 -ism 名词构成形容词，如 capitalistic 与 mutualistic。

abstract.en: Picture a cleaner fish leaving a host's mouth fed, while the host leaves clean.
abstract.cn: 想象清洁鱼从宿主口中离开时吃饱了，宿主也变干净了。

abstract.en: Picture two tree roots locked together, each sending the other a mineral it cannot make.
abstract.cn: 想象两条树根缠在一起，各自送出对方无法制造的矿物。

abstract.en: Picture two companies swapping warehouse space, both cutting costs without hiring anyone.
abstract.cn: 想象两家公司互换仓库空间，双方都降了成本，却没多雇一个人。

examples.en: The fig-wasp relationship is mutualistic because the insect both pollinates and reproduces.
examples.cn: 榕树与榕小蜂的关系是互利共生的，因为昆虫既完成授粉又完成繁殖。

examples.en: A mutualistic fungus can supply a tree with phosphorus in exchange for sugar.
examples.cn: 互利共生真菌能向树木供应磷，以换取糖分。

examples.en: The report called the joint venture mutualistic rather than merely contractual.
examples.cn: 报告称这家合资企业是互利性质的，而不只是合同关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: mutual（相互的）+ istic（……的）→ 相互受益的 → mutualistic 互利共生的

root: 拉丁 mutuus「相互的」→ mutual → mutualism（互利共生）+ 希腊来源后缀 -istic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question with an adjective: in this particular relationship, does each participant gain?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都用同一个形容词回答同一个问题：在这段具体关系里，每个参与者是否都获益？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cleaner fish at a host's mouth, fed on parasites, with the host left clean.
core.cn: 核心意象：清洁鱼停在宿主嘴边，以寄生虫为食，宿主因此变干净。

branches.en: DEFINITION: the adjective scores a relationship as plus-plus.
branches.cn: 定义：这个形容词把一段关系评为加加。

branches.en: EMBODIMENT: the benefit can sit in a partner, in a trait, or in a microbe.
branches.cn: 体现：收益可以落在伙伴身上、落在某个性状上，或落在微生物身上。

branches.en: EXTENSION: firms and villages copy the pattern on purpose.
branches.cn: 延伸：公司与村庄有意复制这一模式。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: the adjective locates a case in the three-cell table.
branches.cn: 分类：这个形容词把个案定位到三分表格中。

branches.en: METAPHOR: abstract exchanges still require a measurable gain on both sides.
branches.cn: 比喻：抽象交换仍要求双方都有可衡量的收益。

intro.en: The word carries two suffixes stacked on a Latin stem: -ism makes the system, -istic makes the adjective that describes it.
intro.cn: 这个词在拉丁词干上叠了两层后缀：-ism 造出体系，-istic 造出描述该体系的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Mutuus is Latin, while -ismus and -isticus arrived through Greek; English added the final -al and -ly layers.
latinIntro.cn: mutuus 是拉丁语，而 -ismus 与 -isticus 经希腊语传入；英语又加上了 -al 与 -ly 两层。

items.example: The two ants and the plant are mutualistic.
items.exampleCN: 这两种蚂蚁与植物是互利共生的。

items.example: Obligate mutualism binds the pair for life.
items.exampleCN: 专性互利共生把这一对终身绑定。

items.example: The two services are mutually reinforcing.

items.example: Mutuality of benefit is the test of the partnership.
items.exampleCN: 收益的相互性是这段伙伴关系的检验标准。

items.meaning: feeding at another's table without harm
items.meaningCN: 在同桌取食而不造成伤害的
items.example: A commensal barnacle rides on the whale.
items.exampleCN: 偏利共生的藤壶搭在鲸身上。

items.example: Symbiotic partners may or may not both gain.
items.exampleCN: 共生伙伴未必双方都获益。

items.meaningCN: 以牺牲他人为代价取食的
items.example: A parasitic wasp lays eggs inside its host.
items.exampleCN: 寄生蜂把卵产在宿主体内。

items.meaningCN: 展示同样的 -ism 到 -istic 构词模式
