senses.title: Making stronger
senses.titleCN: 加强：使原有力量或效果更强
senses.definition: the act of making something stronger or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物更强或更有效的行动
senses.example: The evidence was a reinforcement of the earlier claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据加强了先前的说法。
senses.why: The noun is re- 'again' + in- 'in' + fortis 'strong' + -ment: literally a making strong again from within.
senses.whyCN: 该名词由 re-「再次」、in-「向内」、fortis「强」与 -ment 构成，字面是「再从内部使强」。

senses.title: Military reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 军事增援：增派兵力或装备
senses.definition: the sending of additional troops or equipment to strengthen a force
senses.definitionCN: 增派部队或装备以加强某支力量
senses.example: Reinforcements arrived before the second assault.
senses.exampleCN: 增援在第二次进攻前抵达。
senses.why: The oldest concrete sense is military: a force is made strong again by adding fresh units.
senses.whyCN: 最早的具体义项是军事：通过加入新生力量，让一支部队重新变强。

senses.title: Positive reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 正向强化：以奖励提高行为频率
senses.definition: in behavioural psychology, the delivery of a reward that increases the likelihood of a behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 行为心理学中给予奖励、从而提高某行为出现概率的做法
senses.example: Positive reinforcement made the pupils keep raising their hands.
senses.exampleCN: 正向强化让学生们持续举手。
senses.why: Behaviourism borrowed the strengthening image: a stimulus follows a behaviour and makes that behaviour more likely to recur.
senses.whyCN: 行为主义借用了「加强」意象：刺激跟在行为之后，使该行为更可能再次出现。

senses.title: Negative reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 负向强化：撤走厌恶刺激来提高行为频率
senses.definition: in behavioural psychology, the removal of an unpleasant stimulus that increases the likelihood of a behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 行为心理学中撤走不愉快刺激、从而提高某行为出现概率的做法
senses.example: Turning off the loud alarm after the correct move was negative reinforcement.
senses.exampleCN: 正确操作后关掉刺耳警报属于负向强化。
senses.why: The label is about removal, not punishment: taking away something unpleasant strengthens the behaviour that made it stop.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签讲的是「撤走」而非惩罚：去掉不快之物，强化了使其中止的行为。

senses.title: Structural reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 结构加固：给建筑补入承载构件
senses.definition: the addition of steel, fibre or other material to make a structure carry more load
senses.definitionCN: 加入钢材、纤维或其他材料，使结构承受更大荷载
senses.example: Steel reinforcement runs through the concrete floor slab.
senses.exampleCN: 钢筋混凝土楼板中布有钢筋。
senses.why: Engineering uses the same logic physically: extra material is put inside so the whole can bear more force.
senses.whyCN: 工程在物理层面沿用同一逻辑：把额外材料放进内部，使整体承受更大力量。

senses.title: Reinforcement learning
senses.titleCN: 强化学习：靠奖励信号调整策略
senses.definition: in machine learning, a method in which an agent improves its decisions from rewards and penalties
senses.definitionCN: 机器学习中智能体依据奖励与惩罚改进决策的方法
senses.example: Reinforcement learning trained the robot to walk on rough ground.
senses.exampleCN: 强化学习训练机器人在地面不平处行走。
senses.why: The algorithm receives a score after each action, so successful actions are reinforced in the policy.
senses.whyCN: 算法在每次行动后得到评分，因此成功的行动在策略中被强化。

senses.title: Social reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 社会性强化：靠赞许与关注维持行为
senses.definition: the strengthening of behaviour through approval, attention or status from other people
senses.definitionCN: 通过他人的赞许、关注或地位来加强行为
senses.example: A nod from the group is powerful social reinforcement.
senses.exampleCN: 群体的一次点头就是有力的社会性强化。
senses.why: Humans add a social layer to the reward model: approval itself can act as the reward.
senses.whyCN: 人类在奖励模型上加了社会一层：赞许本身就能充当奖励。

senses.title: Reinforcing a lesson
senses.titleCN: 巩固：重复与补充使知识更牢
senses.definition: the act of repeating or adding material so that learning or an argument is better retained
senses.definitionCN: 通过重复或补充材料，使学习或论证更牢固的行为
senses.example: The homework is reinforcement of the morning's lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 这份作业是对上午课程的巩固。
senses.why: Education borrows the strengthening metaphor: practice makes a skill hold, as if a wall were buttressed.
senses.whyCN: 教育借用了「加固」隐喻：练习让技能站得住，仿佛给墙加了扶壁。

intro.en: Reinforcement comes from reinforce, which entered English through French renforcer, from re- 'again' and enforcer 'to strengthen', ultimately from Latin fortis 'strong'.
intro.cn: reinforcement 出自 reinforce，后者经法语 renforcer 进入英语，由 re-「再次」与 enforcer「使强」构成，最终源于拉丁 fortis「强壮的」。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, powerful'. Its descendants include fort, fortress, effort, comfort and reinforce.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮的、有力的」，其后代包括 fort、fortress、effort、comfort、reinforce。

items.en: Old French renforcer meant 'to strengthen, make firm'. The prefix re- has an intensive force here, 'thoroughly', rather than simply 'again'.
items.cn: 古法语 renforcer 意为「加强、使坚固」。此处前缀 re- 带加强语气，意为「彻底」，而不只是「再次」。

items.en: English reinforce appears in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, first in military and structural contexts.
items.cn: 英语 reinforce 于 14 至 15 世纪出现，最早用于军事与结构语境。

items.en: Reinforcement adds -ment, the noun suffix from Latin -mentum, naming the act or the added material.
items.cn: reinforcement 加 -ment，即出自拉丁 -mentum 的名词后缀，命名动作或所加材料。

items.en: Twentieth-century behaviourism gave the word its learning sense: a consequence that strengthens a response.
items.cn: 20 世纪行为主义赋予该词学习义：强化某一反应的结果。

items.en: The exact first English date is uncertain, and the relative weight of the French re- as 'again' or as an intensifier is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（前缀语义与首见年代）：英语首见确切年代存疑；法语 re- 究竟表「再次」还是加强语气，仍有争论。

note.en: The first group separates the reinforce family; the second gives near-synonyms for strengthening and for reward.
note.cn: 第一组区分 reinforce 词族；第二组给出关于加强和奖励的近义词。

entries.definition: To make stronger or send more support. Reinforcement is the act or the added support.
entries.definitionCN: 指使更强或增派支援；reinforcement 是动作或所加支援。

entries.definition: Describing material or a structure that has been strengthened, such as reinforced concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 形容被加强的材料或结构，如钢筋混凝土。

entries.definition: In psychology, the reward itself; in construction, the strengthening element. It is the thing, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 心理学中指奖励物本身；建筑中指加固件。它是物，不是过程。

entries.definition: Physical power or a body of troops. It lacks the prefix that marks added strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指物理力量或一支部队；缺少表示「额外加强」的前缀。

entries.definition: Any process that makes something stronger. Reinforcement often implies adding something from outside or inside.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指使某物更强的过程；reinforcement 常暗示从外部或内部添加某物。

entries.definition: Bearing weight or giving help. It may be passive, while reinforcement actively adds strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指承重或给予帮助，可以是被动的；reinforcement 则主动增加强度。

entries.definition: Something given for behaviour. In psychology it is the content of positive reinforcement.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某行为给予的东西；心理学中它是正向强化的内容。

entries.definition: Combining parts into a firm whole. It stresses unity, while reinforcement stresses added strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指把部分合成坚固整体，强调统一；reinforcement 强调增加强度。

entries.definition: Extra people or resources held ready. It overlaps military reinforcement but suggests a reserve role.
entries.definitionCN: 指备用的额外人员或资源；与军事增援重叠，但暗示预备角色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- + in- + fortis 'strong' + -ment: strength put back inside.
normal.cn: re- + in- + fortis「强」+ -ment：把强度重新放进内部。

normal.en: The family runs reinforce, reinforced, reinforcer, fort, fortress, effort.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reinforce、reinforced、reinforcer、fort、fortress、effort。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: positive reinforcement, steel reinforcement, military reinforcement, reinforcement learning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：正向强化、钢筋加固、军事增援、强化学习。

normal.en: Negative reinforcement removes something unpleasant; punishment adds something unpleasant.
normal.cn: 负向强化撤走不快之物；惩罚则加入不快之物。

normal.en: In concrete, steel reinforcement sits inside the slab and carries tension.
normal.cn: 混凝土中，钢筋位于板内并承受拉力。

abstract.en: Picture a wall leaning outward until a diagonal brace is bolted to its face.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙向外倾斜，直到一条斜撑被栓到墙面上。

abstract.en: Picture a star sticker placed on a chart each time a hand goes up.
abstract.cn: 想象每次举手都在图表上贴一颗星。

abstract.en: Picture a player receiving a score after each move and slowly favouring the winning move.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手每走一步都得到评分，慢慢偏爱制胜的那一步。

examples.en: The bridge needed reinforcement after the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震之后，这座桥需要加固。

examples.en: The teacher used praise as positive reinforcement, not as a bribe.
examples.cn: 老师把表扬当作正向强化，而不是贿赂。

examples.en: The agent learned the maze through reinforcement learning.
examples.cn: 智能体通过强化学习学会了走迷宫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ in（进）+ force（力量）」——再往里面加力 → reinforcement 加强、强化

root: 拉丁 fortis「强壮的」→ 古法语 renforcer「加强」→ 英语 reinforce + -ment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses add strength in different materials: a claim, an army, a behaviour, a habit, a slab, an algorithm, a social group, and a lesson.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同对象上增加强度：主张、军队、行为、习惯、楼板、算法、群体与课程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diagonal brace bolted to a leaning wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：斜撑被栓到倾斜的墙面上。

branches.en: MORE STRENGTH: an argument or an army is made stronger by addition.
branches.cn: 更强：主张或军队靠添加而变强。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR: a reward increases a response, or the removal of something unpleasant does.
branches.cn: 行为：奖励提高反应概率，撤走不快之物也能如此。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: steel inside concrete carries the load.
branches.cn: 结构：混凝土中的钢筋承担荷载。

branches.en: MACHINE LEARNING: scores after actions reshape the policy.
branches.cn: 机器学习：行动后的评分重塑策略。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND LESSONS: approval from others, and practice, hold behaviour in place.
branches.cn: 人与课程：他人的赞许与练习把行为固定住。

intro.en: Reinforcement combines a French-derived verb of strengthening with the Latin noun suffix -ment; the base fortis also yields fort and fortress.
intro.cn: reinforcement 把法语来源的「加强」动词与拉丁名词后缀 -ment 结合；词基 fortis 还衍生出 fort 与 fortress。

latinIntro.en: The fortis family includes fort, fortress, effort, comfort, reinforce and fortitude; all centre on strength, either physical or moral.
latinIntro.cn: fortis 词族包括 fort、fortress、effort、comfort、reinforce、fortitude，核心都是力量，或物理或道德。

items.example: The wall needs reinforcement before winter.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙入冬前需要加固。

items.meaning: to make stronger or add support
items.example: The results reinforce our earlier finding.

items.example: Reinforced concrete resists bending.
items.exampleCN: 钢筋混凝土抗弯。

items.meaning: the reward or material that strengthens
items.meaningCN: 起强化作用的奖励或材料

items.exampleCN: 表扬可以充当强化物。

items.example: The fort guarded the harbour.

senses.title: Using analysis as a method
senses.definition: using the method of analysis, in which a complex whole is broken into its parts in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 使用分析的方法，即把一个复杂的整体拆成各部分以理解它
senses.example: She took an analytical approach to the problem instead of guessing.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有靠猜，而是用分析的方法处理这个问题。
senses.why: Greek analyein meant 'to loosen up, release', and analysis is a 'breaking up'. The adjective names any method that performs this loosening: the whole is taken apart before it is explained.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 analyein 意为“松开、释放”，analysis 就是“拆开”。这个形容词命名任何执行这种松开的办法：整体先被拆开，然后才被解释。

senses.title: A mind that habitually analyses
senses.definition: of a person or mind, naturally inclined to examine things by separating them into parts and testing the relations between them
senses.definitionCN: 指人或头脑天生倾向于把事物分开、检验各部分关系的
senses.example: He has an analytical mind and notices inconsistencies quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 他有一颗善于分析的头脑，很快就能发现不一致之处。
senses.why: A method can become a habit. When the loosening is done repeatedly by the same person, analytical stops describing a procedure and starts describing a temperament.
senses.whyCN: 方法可以变成习惯。当同一个人反复进行这种“松开”时，analytical 就不再描述一种程序，而开始描述一种性情。

senses.title: A detailed, dissecting account
senses.definition: of a text, report, or account, organized by careful separation and examination of its subject rather than by mere description
senses.definitionCN: 指文本、报告或叙述按对研究对象的细致分离与检验来组织，而不只是描述
senses.example: The report offers an analytical account of the market rather than a summary.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对市场作了分析性论述，而不是只给摘要。
senses.why: The product of analysis carries the name of the method. An account is called analytical when you can see the joints where the subject was cut, instead of a smooth surface of description.
senses.whyCN: 分析的产物继承了方法的名字。当你能看见研究对象被切开的接缝、而不是一层平滑的描述表面时，这篇论述就被称为 analytical。

senses.title: The analytic tradition in philosophy
senses.definition: relating to analytic philosophy, the tradition that treats the clarification of language and logical analysis as central to philosophy
senses.definitionCN: 与（英美）分析哲学有关的，这一传统把语言澄清与逻辑分析视为哲学的核心
senses.example: Analytical philosophy often begins with a careful distinction between two uses of a word.
senses.exampleCN: 分析哲学常常从一个词两种用法的细致区分开始。
senses.why: If philosophy's troubles come from confused language, then the cure is to loosen the words and see their parts. The school is named for exactly that procedure, which is why analytical here names a tradition, not just a style.
senses.whyCN: 如果哲学的麻烦来自混乱的语言，那么解药就是松开词语、看清其部件。这个学派正是因这一程序得名，所以这里的 analytical 命名的是一种传统，而不只是一种风格。

senses.title: Chemistry that resolves substances
senses.titleCN: 把物质分解开来的化学
senses.definition: relating to analytical chemistry, the branch that identifies and measures the components of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 与分析化学有关的，这一分支鉴定并测量物质的组成成分
senses.example: Analytical chemistry identified traces of lead in the water sample.
senses.exampleCN: 分析化学检出了水样中的微量铅。
senses.why: This is the most literal scientific use: the sample is physically resolved into its elements. The loosening is no longer a metaphor but a laboratory operation with instruments and numbers.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的科学用法：样品被实际分解成元素。松开不再是比喻，而是有仪器、有数值的实验室操作。

senses.title: Languages built from separate words
senses.definition: in linguistics, describing a language that shows grammatical relations with particles and word order rather than with inflection
senses.definitionCN: 在语言学中，描述一种用虚词和词序而非屈折变化来表达语法关系的语言
senses.example: Chinese is often described as an analytic language.
senses.exampleCN: 汉语常被描述为分析型语言。
senses.why: Such a language does not fuse grammar into the word's endings; it keeps the pieces separate and lets word order do the joining. The term was applied to languages from 1830, and it extends the image of parts laid out rather than merged.
senses.whyCN: 这种语言不把语法融进词尾，而是让各个成分保持分离，由词序来完成连接。这一术语从 1830 年起用于语言，它延伸了“零件摊开而非熔合”的意象。

senses.title: Geometry and solutions by algebra
senses.titleCN: 用代数处理的几何与解
senses.definition: in mathematics, using algebraic or calculus methods to study figures and to obtain exact solutions, as in analytic geometry
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，用代数或微积分方法研究图形并获得精确解，如解析几何
senses.example: Analytic geometry turns a curve into an equation.
senses.exampleCN: 解析几何把一条曲线变成一个方程。
senses.why: A geometric whole is broken into coordinates and variables, then reassembled as an equation. The method earns the name because the figure is resolved into measurable parts that can be calculated.
senses.whyCN: 一个几何整体被拆成坐标与变量，再被重组成方程。这种方法配得上这个名字，因为图形被分解成可计算的量。

senses.title: Jung's analytical psychology
senses.definition: relating to analytical psychology, Carl Jung's school, which analyses unconscious material such as symbols, dreams and archetypes
senses.definitionCN: 与分析心理学有关的，即荣格学派，分析象征、梦与原型等无意识材料
senses.example: The seminar introduced Jung's analytical psychology.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课介绍了荣格的分析心理学。
senses.why: The psyche is treated as a whole that must be taken apart into its images and complexes. The school takes the same word as chemistry and philosophy, but the material being loosened is inner life.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作一个必须拆成意象与情结的整体。这个学派与化学、哲学共用同一个词，但被松开的材料是内在生活。

senses.title: Reasoning measured by tests
senses.titleCN: 被测验衡量的推理能力
senses.definition: of a test, task, or skill, requiring step-by-step logical reasoning rather than memory or intuition
senses.definitionCN: 指测验、任务或技能要求逐步的逻辑推理，而不是记忆或直觉
senses.example: The exam tests analytical reasoning rather than vocabulary.
senses.exampleCN: 这项考试考查分析性推理，而不是词汇。
senses.why: Once the method is a trainable skill, institutions begin to measure it. Analytical reasoning names the ability to take a stated whole apart, inspect the steps, and reach a conclusion that can be checked.
senses.whyCN: 当方法成为可训练的 skill，机构就开始测量它。analytical reasoning 指把一个给定的整体拆开、检查各步骤、并得出可核查结论的能力。

intro.en: Analytical is the adjective from Greek analytikos 'skilled in dissolving', which goes back to analyein 'to loosen, release' (ana- 'up, back, throughout' + lysis 'a loosening'). It entered English in the 1520s through Medieval Latin analyticus, while the noun analysis is first recorded only in the 1580s. So English analytical is not simply 'analysis + -al': the adjective arrived first from the Greek-Latin family, and analyze followed around 1600.
intro.cn: analytical 是希腊语 analytikos“善于拆解的”的形容词，后者上溯 analyein“松开、释放”（ana-“向上、向后、贯穿”加 lysis“松开”）。它于 16 世纪 20 年代经中世纪拉丁语 analyticus 进入英语，而名词 analysis 直到 16 世纪 80 年代才被记录。所以英语的 analytical 并非简单的“analysis + -al”：形容词先随希腊—拉丁词族进来，analyze 约在 1600 年才出现。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'employing analytic methods', formed with -al from Medieval Latin analyticus, which goes back to Greek analytikos. The adjective is therefore older in English than the noun analysis.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“使用分析方法的”，由 -al 加中世纪拉丁语 analyticus 构成，后者上溯希腊语 analytikos。因此在英语里，形容词比名词 analysis 更古老。

items.en: Analytikos 'analytical' comes from analytos 'dissolved', from analyein 'to unloose, release, set free'. In Aristotle the verb also means 'to analyze', and the image is loosening a complex thing until its parts separate.
items.cn: analytikos“分析的”来自 analytos“被分解的”，再上溯 analyein“松开、释放、使自由”。在亚里士多德那里，这个动词也有“分析”之义；意象是把复杂之物松开，直到各部分分离。

items.en: Anayein is ana- 'up, back, throughout' + lysis 'a loosening', from lyein 'to unfasten', from PIE *leu- 'to loosen, divide, cut apart'. The second element is lysis, not a piece that sounds like 'nalysis'; the word is not 'a + nalysis'.
items.cn: anayein 是 ana-“向上、向后、贯穿”加 lysis“松开”，后者来自 lyein“解开”，再上溯原始印欧语 *leu-“松开、分开、切开”。第二成分是 lysis，而不是某个听起来像“nalysis”的部分；这个词不是“a + nalysis”。

items.en: The noun analysis is recorded from the 1580s, via Medieval Latin from Greek, meaning 'resolution of anything complex into simple elements'. The verb analyze follows c.1600 from French analyser, which was itself formed from the noun analyse.
items.cn: 名词 analysis 记录于 16 世纪 80 年代，经中世纪拉丁语来自希腊语，意为“把复杂之物分解成简单元素”。动词 analyze 约在 1600 年随后出现，来自法语 analyser，而法语动词本身又由名词 analyse 构成。

items.en: In linguistics, the term is applied from 1830 to languages that use particles and auxiliaries rather than inflections to show grammatical relations. The same adjective now names a language type, not a procedure.
items.cn: 在语言学中，这一术语从 1830 年起用于那些用虚词和助词而非屈折变化来表示语法关系的语言。同一个形容词此时命名的是一种语言类型，而不是一种程序。

items.en: Analytical chemistry resolves compounds into elements; analytic philosophy clarifies language and argument; analytical psychology analyses symbols and dreams; analytic geometry turns figures into equations. Keep the family apart: analytics is analysis + -ics (data analysis), not a plural of analytic, and analogical comes from analogy and logos, not from lysis.
items.cn: 分析化学把化合物分解成元素；分析哲学澄清语言与论证；分析心理学分析象征与梦；解析几何把图形变成方程。要把词族分清：analytics 是 analysis + -ics（数据分析），不是 analytic 的复数；analogical 来自 analogy 与 logos，而不是来自 lysis。

note.en: The first group separates the short variant analytic, the unrelated-looking analytics, the verb analyze and the look-alike analogical; the second compares adjectives that also praise careful thinking but do not mean 'breaking into parts'.
note.cn: 第一组区分短变体 analytic、看似无关却形近的 analytics、动词 analyze，以及形似而不同源的 analogical；第二组比较同样称赞“细致思考”、却不含“拆成部分”之意的形容词。

entries.definition: the shorter variant of analytical, used especially in fixed terms such as analytic philosophy and analytic geometry. It is the same adjective, not a different root.
entries.definitionCN: analytical 的较短变体，尤用于 analytic philosophy、analytic geometry 等固定术语。它是同一个形容词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: the systematic analysis of data, especially by software. It is analysis + -ics, a separate noun, not the plural of analytic.
entries.definitionCN: 对数据的系统分析，尤指借助软件。它是 analysis + -ics 构成的独立名词，不是 analytic 的复数。

entries.definition: to break something down in order to understand it. It is the verb of the family, while analytical is the adjective describing the method or the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 为理解某物而把它拆解。它是该词族的动词，而 analytical 是描述方法或头脑的形容词。

entries.definition: based on analogy. It looks close to analytical but comes from analogy and logos 'ratio', not from analysis and lysis 'a loosening'.
entries.definitionCN: 基于类比的。它看起来接近 analytical，却来自 analogy 与 logos“比例”，而不是来自 analysis 与 lysis“松开”。

entries.definition: done according to a fixed system or plan. Systematic stresses order and coverage; analytical stresses taking the whole apart to see how it works.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定体系或计划进行的。systematic 强调秩序与覆盖面；analytical 强调把整体拆开以看清其运作。

entries.definition: following the rules of valid reasoning. Logical stresses the correctness of the steps; analytical stresses the act of decomposition that produces the steps.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循有效推理规则的。logical 强调步骤的正确性；analytical 强调产生这些步骤的拆解动作。

entries.definition: examining something in order to judge its merits and faults. Critical adds evaluation; analytical examination can remain neutral and descriptive.
entries.definitionCN: 为判断优缺点而审视某物。critical 多了一层评价；分析性审视可以保持中性、描述性。

entries.definition: including many facts or small features. Detailed says there is a lot of information; analytical says the information is organized by reasoning about parts and relations.
entries.definitionCN: 包含许多事实或细微特征的。detailed 说的是信息量大；analytical 说的是信息按部分与关系的推理被组织起来。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: ana- 'up, back' plus lysis 'a loosening', the analysis/analyze family, and the two look-alikes that are not relatives, analytics and analogical.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：ana-“向上、向后”加 lysis“松开”、analysis/analyze 词族，以及两个并非同族的形似词 analytics 与 analogical。

normal.en: ana- means 'up, back, throughout' and lysis means 'a loosening'. Analytical is the habit of loosening a whole until its parts show.
normal.cn: ana- 意为“向上、向后、贯穿”，lysis 意为“松开”。analytical 就是把整体松开、直到部件露出来的习惯。

normal.en: The same *leu- root gives analysis, paralysis, dissolve and solve, so analytical belongs with 'loosening', not with 'learning'.
normal.cn: 同一 *leu- 词根给出 analysis、paralysis、dissolve、solve，所以 analytical 属于“松开”这一族，与“学习”无关。

normal.en: The adjective is older in English than the noun: analytical 1520s, analysis 1580s, analyze c.1600. It is not simply analysis + -al.
normal.cn: 在英语里形容词比名词更老：analytical 是 16 世纪 20 年代，analysis 是 80 年代，analyze 约 1600 年。它不是简单的 analysis + -al。

normal.en: Three specialized homes: analytical chemistry (resolves substances), analytic geometry (turns figures into equations), analytical psychology (dissects the psyche).
normal.cn: 三个专门归宿：分析化学（分解物质）、解析几何（把图形变成方程）、分析心理学（剖析心灵）。

normal.en: analytics is analysis + -ics, a data noun; analogical is analogy + -ical, from logos. Neither is a form of analytical.
normal.cn: analytics 是 analysis + -ics 的数据名词；analogical 是 analogy + -ical，来自 logos。两者都不是 analytical 的形式。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket watch taken apart on a cloth: every wheel is separated, and only then can you say how the watch keeps time.
abstract.cn: 想象一只怀表被拆开摊在布上：每个齿轮都被分开，只有这时你才能说出这只表如何走时。

abstract.en: The same loosening can be done to water, to a sentence, to a curve, to a dream or to an argument. The material changes; the gesture does not.
abstract.cn: 同一种松开可以施于水样、句子、曲线、梦或论证。材料变了，动作没变。

abstract.en: When the gesture becomes reliable enough to teach and test, it turns into a skill, and analytical reasoning becomes something an exam can measure.
abstract.cn: 当这个动作可靠到可以教授和测验，它就变成一种技能，analytical reasoning 也就成了考试可以测量的东西。

examples.en: Her analytical skills made her the first person to spot the error.
examples.cn: 她的分析能力使她成为第一个发现错误的人。

examples.en: The paper gives an analytical overview of the last ten years of research.
examples.cn: 这篇论文对过去十年的研究作了分析性综述。

examples.en: Analytical chemistry can detect amounts far below what the eye can see.
examples.cn: 分析化学能检测到远低于肉眼可见量的物质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安纳利替扣」——安纳利把扣子拆成一根根线来查，看清它怎么扣上 → analytical 分析的、解析的

root: 来自希腊语 analytikos，经中世纪拉丁语 analyticus 进入英语；上溯 analyein“松开、拆解”（ana-“向上／拆开”加 lysis“松开”），核心是“拆开整体以看清结构”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of analytical, all one gesture: loosen a whole until its parts are visible. The whole can be a problem, a mind, a report, a language, a compound, a figure, a psyche or a test item.
sensesIntro.cn: analytical 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把整体松开，直到各部分可见。这个整体可以是问题、头脑、报告、语言、化合物、图形、心灵或一道考题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole is loosened until its parts lie open to view.
core.cn: 核心意象：把整体松开，直到各部件摊开可见。

branches.en: METHOD AND PRODUCT: the procedure of analysis, and the written account that shows the joints it cut.
branches.cn: 方法与产物：分析的程序，以及显露出切割接缝的书面论述。

branches.en: THE MIND AND THE TEST: a settled habit of analysis, and the measurable skill that institutions test.
branches.cn: 头脑与测验：稳定的分析习惯，以及机构测量的可测量技能。

branches.en: SCHOOLS: analytic philosophy and analytical psychology are named for the same loosening, applied to language and to the psyche.
branches.cn: 学派：分析哲学与分析心理学因同一种松开而得名，分别施于语言与心灵。

branches.en: EXACT SCIENCES: chemistry resolves substances into elements, and geometry resolves figures into equations.
branches.cn: 精确科学：化学把物质分解成元素，几何把图形分解成方程。

branches.en: LANGUAGE TYPE: an analytic language keeps its grammatical pieces separate instead of fusing them into endings.
branches.cn: 语言类型：分析型语言让语法成分保持分离，而不是熔进词尾。

intro.en: Analytical is analytic + -al; analytic came from Medieval Latin analyticus, from Greek analytikos. The living English suffix here is -al, while the Greek core is ana- 'up, back' + lysis 'a loosening'. English also forms analytically with -ly, analysis and analyze by other routes, and analytics with -ics.
intro.cn: analytical 是 analytic + -al；analytic 来自中世纪拉丁语 analyticus，再上溯希腊语 analytikos。这里活的英语后缀是 -al，而希腊内核是 ana-“向上、向后”加 lysis“松开”。英语还以 -ly 构成 analytically，以其他路径构成 analysis 与 analyze，并以 -ics 构成 analytics。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin analyticus is the immediate source, and Latin analysis (from Greek) is the noun. Greek analyein 'to loosen' and lysis 'a loosening' are the deepest elements; they are Greek, not Latin, and are listed here because they explain the family.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是中世纪拉丁语 analyticus，名词则是拉丁语 analysis（来自希腊语）。最深层的成分是希腊语 analyein“松开”与 lysis“松开”；它们是希腊语而非拉丁语，列在这里是因为它们解释了整个词族。

items.structure: analytic + -al (adjective), from Medieval Latin analyticus < Greek analytikos
items.meaningCN: 分析的；使用分析方法的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The team needs a more analytical approach.
items.exampleCN: 团队需要一种更重分析的方法。

items.meaning: the shorter variant, common in fixed terms
items.meaningCN: 较短变体，常见于固定术语（同义）
items.example: Analytic geometry links algebra and shape.
items.exampleCN: 解析几何把代数与图形联系起来。

items.meaningCN: 以分析的方式（-ly 构成方式副词）
items.example: She read the proposal analytically.
items.exampleCN: 她以分析的方式读了这份提案。

items.structure: ana- (up, back, throughout) + lysis (a loosening) + -is (noun ending)
items.meaning: the resolution of a complex whole into its elements
items.meaningCN: 把复杂整体分解成元素；分析（-is 构成名词）
items.example: The analysis took three weeks.
items.exampleCN: 这项分析花了三周。

items.meaning: to break something down in order to understand it
items.example: They analyzed the samples in the lab.
items.exampleCN: 他们在实验室分析了样品。

items.meaningCN: 分析者；分析师（-ist 类人物名词）
items.example: The analyst compared the two markets.
items.exampleCN: 分析师比较了两个市场。

items.structure: analysis + -ics (noun of a field or practice)
items.meaningCN: 数据分析（-ics 构成领域名词，不是 analytic 的复数）
items.example: The company hired a data analytics team.
items.exampleCN: 公司雇了一个数据分析团队。

items.meaning: the property of being analytic, especially of a statement true by meaning
items.meaningCN: 分析性；解析性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: Philosophers debated the analyticity of such statements.
items.exampleCN: 哲学家们争论这类陈述的分析性。

items.meaningCN: 精神分析的（psycho- 心灵 + analytical）
items.example: He wrote a psychoanalytical reading of the novel.
items.exampleCN: 他写了一篇对这部小说的精神分析解读。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 松开；释放；使自由（希腊语来源）

definition_en: a series of lessons; the way something moves or develops over time; one part of a meal
core_image: 一条从起点流向终点的路
scene: 新学期第一节数学课前，老师把课本发给了大家。 Our maths course will last the whole term.
sceneCN: 这里 course 是「课程」（第 1 个义项：一连串有安排的课）；句意是我们的数学课将持续整个学期。

senses.title: A series of lessons on a subject
senses.definition: a planned set of lessons or studies on one subject
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一个科目的有计划的课程或学习安排
senses.example: She signed up for a summer swimming course.
senses.exampleCN: 她报名参加了暑期游泳课程。
senses.why: The core image is a path from start to finish, and a course of study is exactly that path walked through lessons.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是起点到终点的路径，而课程正是用一节节课走完的学习之路。

senses.title: The way something develops over time
senses.definition: the natural movement or development of something
senses.definitionCN: 事物自然的运动或发展过程
senses.example: The disease ran its course, and he soon got better.
senses.exampleCN: 病程自然走完，他很快好转了。
senses.why: Because the word first meant running or flowing onward, it fits anything that moves forward over time.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词最初指奔跑或流动向前，所以适合描述随时间推进的过程。

senses.title: A path or line of movement
senses.definition: the direction or line along which something moves
senses.definitionCN: 物体移动所沿的方向或路线
senses.example: The ship changed course to avoid the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 船改变航线以避开风暴。
senses.why: A runner follows a course across a field; a ship follows one across the sea, so the route sense keeps the image.
senses.whyCN: 跑步者沿路径穿过田野，船沿航线穿越大海，所以路线义保留了这一意象。

senses.title: One part of a meal served in order
senses.definition: one of the parts of a meal, served one after another
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序端上的一餐中的一部分
senses.example: For the main course we had fish and rice.
senses.exampleCN: 主菜我们吃了鱼和米饭。
senses.why: Dishes arrive one after another along the meal's path, so each stage is a course.
senses.whyCN: 菜肴沿着这顿饭的路径一道道端上来，所以每一道都叫 a course。

intro.en: Course goes back to a Latin verb that meant to run.
intro.cn: course 可追溯到拉丁语中意为「跑」的动词。

items.en: The Latin verb currere meant to run, giving the noun cursus, a running or course.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 currere 意为奔跑，派生名词 cursus，指奔跑、行程。

items.en: Old French carried it over as cors, meaning a running or an onward path.
items.cn: 古法语将其变为 cors，意为奔跑、前行的路径。

items.en: English borrowed cours in the thirteenth century for onward movement.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 cours，指向前的运动。

items.en: Its senses widened to a path of travel, a way of life and a planned study.
items.cn: 词义扩展为行进路线、生活方式和有计划的学习。

items.en: Today course covers lessons, routes, processes and meal stages.
items.cn: 如今 course 覆盖课程、路线、过程和菜式。

note.cn: 这些词共享「奔跑」词根，或指路线与课程。

normal.en: curs- means run: current, cursor and course all run.
normal.cn: 词根 curs- 意为跑：current、cursor、course 都在跑。

normal.en: of course: things run as expected, so it means surely.
normal.cn: of course：事情照常运转，所以意为当然。

normal.en: A swimming course runs from first lesson to last.
normal.cn: 游泳课程从第一节课跑到最后一节课。

normal.en: Main course arrives after the starter in a meal's run.

normal.cn: discourse 加 dis-，指来回交流的谈话。

abstract.en: Picture a runner with a flag moving from start line to finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象一名举着小旗的跑者从起点线奔向终点线。

abstract.en: See a ship's dotted line on the sea map bending to a new direction.

examples.en: Our plane changed course because of the wind.

definition_zh: 敌意；仇恨；憎恶
definition_en: strong hostility or active hatred toward someone
core_image: 胸腔里鼓动的黑风：看谁都不顺眼的火气
scene: 两个家族多年互不往来。 Old animosity between the two families kept them apart for decades.
sceneCN: 这里 animosity 是「敌意、仇恨」（第 1 个义项：强烈的敌对情绪）；句意为：两家的宿怨使他们几十年互不往来。

pos.zh: 敌意；仇恨；憎恶

derivatives.zh: 同根拉丁借词，义为「敌意；（存心不良的）意图」

senses.title: Strong hostility toward someone
senses.definition: a feeling of strong dislike and active ill will toward a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体的强烈厌恶与敌对情绪
senses.example: Years of rivalry turned into open animosity.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的较量演变为公开的敌意。
senses.why: The root spirit or breath became spirit roused against another spirit.
senses.whyCN: 词根本义「气息、精神」引申为「被激起而与对方作对的精神」。

senses.title: Bitter resentment kept alive over time
senses.definition: hostility that persists and festers over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期持续、不断发酵的敌对情绪
senses.example: The animosity between the rivals outlived their careers.
senses.exampleCN: 两位对手之间的积怨在退役后仍未消散。
senses.why: Spirit, once stirred against another, keeps breathing on its own.
senses.whyCN: 精神一旦被激起与对方作对，便会自行延续，如气息不熄。

senses.title: Ill will behind actions
senses.definition: hostile intention visible in what one does or says
senses.definitionCN: 从言行中透露出的敌对意图
senses.example: There was more animosity than logic in his objection.
senses.exampleCN: 他的反对里恶意多于道理。
senses.why: Inner spirit shows itself in outward acts, so the word names the motive force.
senses.whyCN: 内在精神会显露于外在行为，此词便指这种动机力量。

senses.title: Animosity between groups
senses.definition: hostility dividing communities, factions, or nations
senses.definitionCN: 使社区、派系或国家相互对立的敌意
senses.example: Border wars left a residue of animosity between the two nations.
senses.exampleCN: 边境战争在两国间留下仇视的余绪。
senses.why: What begins between persons scales up to whole peoples.
senses.whyCN: 始于个人的敌意可放大到整个民族。

senses.title: Open expression of hatred
senses.definition: hostility openly shown rather than hidden
senses.definitionCN: 公开表露而非隐藏的敌意
senses.example: She made no attempt to hide her animosity at the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不掩饰会上的敌意。
senses.why: Breath becomes speech; stirred spirit speaks out.
senses.whyCN: 气息化为言语，被激起的精神自会出口。

senses.title: Animosity in public life
senses.definition: hostility in politics, sports, or professional rivalries
senses.definitionCN: 政治、体育或职业竞争中的敌对
senses.example: The election season was marked by unusual animosity.
senses.exampleCN: 这次选举季充满罕见的敌对气氛。
senses.why: Contests for shared prizes breed stirred spirits on all sides.
senses.whyCN: 对共同奖赏的争夺使各方精神都被激起。

senses.title: Animosity as feeling versus action
senses.definition: the inner feeling itself, whether or not it leads to deeds
senses.definitionCN: 内心情绪本身，无论是否付诸行动
senses.example: He felt animosity but spoke with perfect courtesy.
senses.exampleCN: 他心怀敌意，言谈却彬彬有礼。
senses.why: Spirit exists inside the chest before it reaches the hands.
senses.whyCN: 精神在抵达双手之前，先在胸腔里存在。

senses.title: Deadly animosity: enmity to the extreme
senses.definition: hatred intense enough to admit no reconciliation
senses.definitionCN: 强烈到无法和解的仇恨
senses.example: The feud ended in deadly animosity between the houses.
senses.exampleCN: 这场世仇以两族间不共戴天的敌意收场。
senses.why: When stirred spirit refuses to settle, hostility becomes absolute.
senses.whyCN: 被激起的精神拒绝平息，敌意便走向绝对化。

intro.en: Animosity shares its breathing root with animal and animate: it is spirit roused against another.
intro.cn: animosity 与 animal、animate 共享「气息」词根：它是被激起而与人对立的精神。

items.en: The root *h₂enh₁- meant to breathe, giving Latin animus, breath, spirit, and mind.
items.cn: 印欧词根 *h₂enh₁- 义为「呼吸」，派生出拉丁语 animus（气息、精神、心神）。

items.en: Animositas meant boldness and high spirit, later violent feeling against someone.
items.cn: 拉丁语 animositas 意为「大胆、气盛」，后指针对他人的激烈情绪。

items.en: Old French carried animosite, keeping the sense of violent feeling.
items.cn: 古法语作 animosite，保留「激烈情绪」之义。

items.en: English adopted animosity in the fifteenth century, at first meaning courage or vigor.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪借入 animosity，最初意为「勇气、活力」。

items.en: The hostile sense prevailed by the seventeenth century, fixing the modern meaning of hatred and ill will.
items.cn: 至十七世纪敌对义占上风，确立了现代「仇恨、敌意」之义。

note.en: Words below are grouped by shared roots and by neighboring words of hostility.
note.cn: 以下按共享词根与敌意近义词分组。

entries.definition: hostile feeling or intention; also mind and spirit in Latin
entries.definitionCN: 敌意；（拉丁语中）心神，与 animosity 同根且语义直接相关

entries.definition: liveliness or the art of animated films
entries.definitionCN: 活力；动画，同根但词义相反方向（生气而非敌意）

entries.definition: a living breathing creature
entries.definitionCN: 动物，共享「有气息之物」词根

entries.definition: unfriendly feeling or opposition
entries.definitionCN: 敌对；敌意，最常见近义词

entries.definition: deep-seated aversion
entries.definitionCN: 反感；厌恶，偏本能的排斥

entries.definition: the state of being an enemy
entries.definitionCN: 仇敌关系；敌意，更正式更持久

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real breathing root anim- and its word family.
normalIntro.cn: 以下记忆钩子基于真实的 anim-（气息）词根及其词族。

normal.en: anim- = breath, spirit; animosity is spirit stirred up against someone.
normal.cn: anim- 表「气息、精神」；animosity 是被激起而针对他人的精神。

normal.en: Same root: animal (breathing thing), animate (give breath to), unanimous (one spirit).
normal.cn: 同根词：animal（有气息之物）、animate（赋予气息）、unanimous（同一心神）。

normal.en: Animus names the hostile intent; animosity the hostile feeling.
normal.cn: animus 指敌对意图；animosity 指敌对情绪。

normal.en: Unanimous is the opposite mood: many people, one spirit, no animosity.
normal.cn: unanimous 恰是相反氛围：众人心神一致，毫无敌意。

normal.en: Collocation memory: bear animosity toward someone.
normal.cn: 搭配记忆：bear animosity toward someone（对某人怀有敌意）。

abstract.en: Picture a black wind swirling inside the chest every time a rival's name is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象每当听到对手的名字，胸腔里便卷起黑风。

abstract.en: See two old neighbors never greeting each other across the fence for decades.
abstract.cn: 想象两位老邻居隔着篱笆几十年互不寒暄。

abstract.en: Feel the heat rising in the face before a single harsh word is said.
abstract.cn: 感受一句重话未出口前脸上先升起的燥热。

examples.en: Despite the animosity between them, they worked together for ten years.
examples.cn: 尽管彼此有敌意，他们还是共事了十年。

examples.en: The animosity between the two clubs goes back a century.
examples.cn: 两家俱乐部之间的宿怨可追溯到一个世纪前。

examples.en: He bore no animosity toward his former partner.
examples.cn: 他对前合伙人毫无敌意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱你莫提」——都到「爱你」都不敢提的地步了，只剩 animosity（敌意）。

root: 拉丁语 animus（气息、心神，源自一般认为的印欧词根 *h₂enh₁-「呼吸」）+ -ositas（名词后缀）→ animositas「气盛；激烈情绪」→ 古法语 animosite → 英语 animosity（15 世纪，最初义为「勇气」，17 世纪转为「敌意」）。

sensesIntro.en: From roused spirit, the word fans out into personal hatred, long-fed grudges, group hostility, and hatred expressed or merely felt.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「被激起的精神」出发，词义铺展为个人仇恨、经年积怨、群体敌对，以及表露于外或仅存于心的恨意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black wind of spirit blowing against someone
core.cn: 核心意象：吹向他人的黑色精神之风

branches.en: hostility felt and shown
branches.cn: 心存且表露的敌意

branches.en: grudges that time makes worse
branches.cn: 随时间加深的积怨与死仇

branches.en: ill will behind words and deeds
branches.cn: 言行背后的恶意

branches.en: hostility between groups and in public life
branches.cn: 群体间与公共领域的敌对

branches.en: feeling kept inside without action
branches.cn: 仅存于内的情绪

intro.en: The anim- family is one of Latin's largest: breath becomes life, mind, courage, and here hostility.
intro.cn: anim- 词族是拉丁语最庞大的词族之一：气息化为生命、心神、勇气，在此则化为敌意。

latinIntro.en: Latin animus supplied all members of the family, each suffix tilting the meaning its own way.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 animus 供应该词族所有成员，不同后缀使词义各自偏移。

items.example: Every anim- word starts from breathing.
items.exampleCN: 每个 anim- 词都始于「呼吸」。

items.example: Curiosity and generosity share this ending.
items.exampleCN: curiosity 与 generosity 共用此词尾。

items.example: Animal once meant simply anything alive.
items.exampleCN: animal 曾泛指一切活物。

items.example: The coach animated the tired team.
items.exampleCN: 教练使疲惫的队伍重燃斗志。

items.example: The vote was unanimous.
items.exampleCN: 投票一致通过。

items.example: She spoke without animus.
items.exampleCN: 她发言不带敌意。

items.example: A magnanimous winner praised the loser.
items.exampleCN: 获胜者宽宏地称赞了败者。

items.example: A pusillanimous retreat avoided the battle.
items.exampleCN: 怯懦的撤退避开了战斗。

derivatives.zh: animosity 的复数形式，指多股敌意

definition_zh: 努力；费力的一次尝试；费尽心力做出的成果；集体的协同行动；（物理学）作用力
definition_en: the physical or mental energy used when trying to do something
core_image: 一个人推着装满石头的木车，青筋鼓起，车轮在地面上压出一道痕
scene: 山路太陡，几个人一起推同一辆货车，车轮才勉强往前走。 Their combined effort moved the cart only a few metres before they had to rest.
sceneCN: 这里 effort 指「为达成一件事而付出的体力或脑力」（第 1 个义项：付出力气去做）；句意为他们合力只把车推动了几米就不得不停下。图中可辨识物件：木车、陡坡、被压出的车辙、几双用力的腿。

pos.zh: 努力；尝试；费力得到的成果；协同行动
（机械学）作用力、施力

derivatives.zh: 由名词加表示「充满」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「力气」转为「需要使力气的」
在形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「费力的」转为「以费力方式」
加表示「缺少」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「力气」转为「看起来不费力气」
在否定式形容词后加副词后缀构成，语义由「不费力的」转为「毫不费力地」
在否定式形容词后加名词后缀构成，语义由「不费力」转为「不费力这一特质」

senses.title: Energy spent on a task
senses.titleCN: 为做成一件事付出的力气
senses.definition: the physical or mental energy that someone uses in trying to do something
senses.definitionCN: 某人为做成某件事而投入的体力或脑力
senses.example: Their combined effort moved the cart only a few metres before they had to rest.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合力只把车推动了大约几米，就不得不停下休息。
senses.why: the word descends from a Latin verb meaning to strengthen, so the first sense is simply the strength that a task draws out of a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自一个意为「使有力」的拉丁动词，所以第一个义项就是一件事从人身上抽出的那股力。

senses.title: A single attempt
senses.definition: one act of trying to do something, viewed as a countable attempt
senses.definitionCN: 试着做某事的一次行动，可以按次计数
senses.example: He made three efforts to lift the lid before asking for help.
senses.exampleCN: 他试着揭开盖子三次，才去求助。
senses.why: once energy is spent it can be counted as a try, so the noun shifts from the fuel to the event that burns it.
senses.whyCN: 力气一旦花出去，就可以说成「一次尝试」，于是名词从燃料转向烧掉燃料的那件事。

senses.title: A piece of work produced
senses.definition: a result or piece of work judged by how much care and labour went into it
senses.definitionCN: 按投入的心血与劳动来评价的成果或作品
senses.example: Her essay was a serious effort, even if the argument faltered.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章是一份认真写就的成果，尽管论证有些摇晃。
senses.why: we praise a thing by naming the labour inside it, so the word can stand for the product rather than the process.
senses.whyCN: 人们通过点出其中所含的劳动来称赞一件东西，于是这个词可以用产物代替过程。

senses.title: Organized collective action
senses.definition: a coordinated campaign in which many people work toward one public aim
senses.definitionCN: 许多人朝同一个公共目标协作推进的行动
senses.example: The relief effort reached the valley two days after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后两天，救援行动抵达了山谷。
senses.why: when many people spend energy on one aim, the countable noun becomes the whole campaign rather than any single exertion.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人把力气投向一个目标时，这个可数名词指的就是整场行动，而不是任何单次用力。

senses.title: Force applied in a machine
senses.definition: in mechanics, the force applied to a machine or load, as opposed to the resistance it moves
senses.definitionCN: 力学中施加于机械或负载的力，与它所推动的阻力相对
senses.example: A longer lever increases the effect of the effort on the load.
senses.exampleCN: 较长的杠杆会增大作用力对负载的效果。
senses.why: the technical sense keeps the plain meaning exactly: the force a worker puts in, measured against what the machine must move.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术义保留了最朴素的意思：人使出的那股力，与机器要移动的东西相对而量。

senses.title: Degree of strain involved
senses.definition: the amount of strain a task demands, considered as a property of the task
senses.definitionCN: 任务所要求的紧张程度，作为任务本身的属性来看
senses.example: The climb costs little effort if you start early.
senses.exampleCN: 如果早点出发，这段爬坡并不费多少力气。
senses.why: instead of the energy itself, the word can name the quantity of it that a job requires, which is why one asks how much effort a task takes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不指力气本身，而指一件事所需的力气分量，所以人们会问一项任务要花多少努力。

senses.title: National mobilization
senses.definition: the total organized activity of a country or a large body in wartime or emergency
senses.definitionCN: 战时或紧急状态下，一国或一个大型机构投入的全部组织性活动
senses.example: The war effort drew factories, farms and railways into one plan.
senses.exampleCN: 战时动员把工厂、农场与铁路都纳入一个计划。
senses.why: this is the collective sense enlarged to the scale of a whole society, where every exertion feeds a single campaign.
senses.whyCN: 这是集体义被放大到整个社会的规模：每一份力气都汇入同一场行动。

senses.title: An attempt judged kindly
senses.titleCN: 值得称许的一次尝试（即使未成）
senses.definition: an attempt that is praised for the honesty of the trying even though it falls short
senses.definitionCN: 即便未达到目标，也因尝试本身认真而受到赞许的一次努力
senses.example: The team lost, but it was a brave effort by every player.
senses.exampleCN: 球队输了，但每位队员的这次努力都很勇敢。
senses.why: because effort measures what was given rather than what was gained, the word becomes a way of honouring a failure.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词量的是付出而非所得，它就成了给失败留体面的一种说法。

intro.en: Effort comes through Old French esforz from the verb esforcier 'to force, exert', which rests on a Vulgar Latin verb reconstructed as exfortiare, from Latin fortis 'strong'. The deeper origin of fortis is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语 esforz 来自动词 esforcier「用力、使力」，后者基于一个被重构为 exfortiare 的俗拉丁动词，其词根为拉丁 fortis「强壮」。fortis 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, mighty, firm'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link proposed to a root for 'height' or 'mountain' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮、有力、坚固」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「高度」或「山」的词根相联系的看法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: A spoken-Latin verb reconstructed as exfortiare 'to put forth strength' carried the root into the everyday speech of the late empire; the form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 一个被重构为 exfortiare 的口语拉丁动词「使出力气」，把词根带入帝国晚期日常口语；这一形式属重构，并非有书证的词。

items.en: Old French esforcier 'to force, strive, exert oneself' produced the noun esforz, which named both the strain and the try.
items.cn: 古法语 esforcier「用力、奋力、施展」产生名词 esforz，兼指那份紧张与那次尝试。

items.en: Middle English took the noun as effort in the fourteenth century, still close to the sense of a strong exertion of the will.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪把这个名词吸收为 effort，仍贴近「意志强力施展」的意思。

items.en: From the nineteenth century mechanics used effort for the applied force in a simple machine, set against the load it moves.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，力学用这个词指简单机械中施加的力，与被移动的负载相对。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of fortis and the exact spoken form): any Indo-European form offered for fortis is a reconstruction, and the earliest noun use has no securely dated citation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（fortis 的更深来源与那个口语形式的确切面貌）：凡为 fortis 给出的印欧语形式均为重构形式；这个名词最早用法也没有确切年代的出处。

note.en: Group one collects words that look like effort but come from other roots; group two collects near neighbours that measure exertion differently.
note.cn: 第一组是形近而异源的词；第二组是语义相近、但衡量「付出」方式不同的词。

entries.definition: Its negation: work done without visible strain, so the strain is precisely what has vanished.
entries.definitionCN: 该词的否定形式：不显费力的工作，消失的正是那份紧张。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus fortis: what strengthens someone, hence ease and consolation, not exertion.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 fortis 构成：使人强健之物，因此指舒适与安慰，而非付出。

entries.definition: Fortis 'strong' plus facere 'to make': to make strong, as a wall or a body.
entries.definitionCN: 由 fortis「强壮」加 facere「做」构成：使变强，如城墙或身体。

entries.definition: Strength of mind under pain or pressure; it names the capacity rather than its spending.
entries.definitionCN: 痛苦或压力下心志的坚强；指那份能力，而不是它的耗费。

entries.definition: From for- 'outside' plus a Germanic root for a fine: to lose something as a penalty, with no link to strength.
entries.definitionCN: 由 for-「在外」加一个表示罚金的日耳曼词根构成：作为惩罚而失去某物，与「强壮」无关。

entries.definition: The activity of labouring, named by what is done rather than by the strain it costs.
entries.definitionCN: 指劳动这项活动，以「做了什么」命名，而不以耗费多少力气命名。

entries.definition: A formal word for strong physical or mental strain; effort is its everyday counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示强烈体力或脑力紧张的正式词；effort 是它日常的对应说法。

entries.definition: A try at something, with the outcome unknown; it says nothing about how much energy was spent.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事的尝试，结果未知；不含花费了多少力气之意。

entries.definition: A sustained, purposeful effort, often on something public or grand; it carries a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 持久的、有目的的付出，多用于公共或宏大的事；语气正式。

entries.definition: Hard physical work, especially of a manual or repetitive kind; it stresses the grind.
entries.definitionCN: 艰苦的体力劳动，尤指手工或重复性工作；强调辛苦本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin fortis 'strong', so effort is strength brought out and spent.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁 fortis「强壮」，因此这个词就是被使出来、被花掉的力气。

normal.en: The family runs effort, effortless, effortful, effortlessly, effortlessness.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、肯定与否定两个形容词、副词与抽象名词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the spending: make an effort, put effort into, spare no effort.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这份耗费：作出努力、投入心力、不遗余力。

normal.en: The technical use appears in the lever: effort acts on one arm, the load on the other.
normal.cn: 技术义出现在杠杆里：施力作用于一端，负载作用于另一端。

normal.en: Relatives outside the word still carry the same root: fortify, fortitude, comfort.
normal.cn: 词外的同族词仍然带着同一词根：加固、坚毅、安慰。

abstract.en: Picture a hand squeezing water out of a cloth until the drops stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把布里的水拧出来，直到不再滴。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled taut between two posts, humming with the strain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子在两根柱子之间被拉紧，绷得发出声。

abstract.en: Picture a candle burned down to a stub because it was kept lit all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛因为整夜点着，只剩下一小截。

examples.en: It took a full day of effort to clear the blocked channel.
examples.cn: 清理这条堵塞的水道花了整整一天的力气。

examples.en: The rescue effort involved boats, dogs and six villages.
examples.cn: 这次救援行动动用了船只、犬只与六个村庄的人手。

examples.en: A lever lets a small effort lift a heavy load.
examples.cn: 杠杆使小小的作用力能抬起沉重的负载。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一夫」推车——一个人使出全身力气推车 → 努力、费力

root: 古法语 esforz「力气、奋力」→ 俗拉丁重构形式 exfortiare「使出力气」→ 拉丁 fortis「强壮、有力」；fortis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: strength is drawn out of a body, counted as a try, then read into the thing made, into the group that shares it, into the machine that measures it, into the size of the demand, into a whole nation's campaign and finally into the praise given to a losing attempt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：力气从身体里被抽出，先被数成一次尝试，再被读进做出的东西、共担的群体、量它的机械、需求的大小、举国的动员，最后读进给失败尝试的那份称许。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body braced against a loaded cart, strength visibly leaving it and entering the work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体抵着装满货物的车，力气看得见地从身体里流出，进入那件活里。

branches.en: THE SUPPLY AND ITS SIZE: energy itself, and the amount of it a task calls for.
branches.cn: 储备与其分量：力气本身，以及一件事要调用多少。

branches.en: THE COUNTED TRY: one attempt, and the same attempt judged generous even when it fails.
branches.cn: 被数出的尝试：一次尝试，以及这次尝试即便落空也被评得宽厚。

branches.en: THE THING MADE: labour can be read back out of the result.
branches.cn: 做出的东西：劳动可以从成果里被读回来。

branches.en: THE SHARED CAMPAIGN: many bodies push one aim, from a rescue to a whole nation.
branches.cn: 共担的行动：许多身体推同一个目标，从一次救援到一个国家。

branches.en: THE MEASURED FORCE: mechanics turns the body's push into a quantity on one arm of a lever.
branches.cn: 被量住的力：力学把身体的推力化成一个落在杠杆一端的量。

intro.en: Effort is a noun taken whole from Old French, so it has no live prefixes for English speakers; what grows from it are suffixes and a root that still builds other words.
intro.cn: 这个词是从古法语整体借入的名词，对英语使用者来说没有可拆的活前缀；从它长出来的是后缀，以及一个仍在构成别的词的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis 'strong' also gives fortify, fortitude and comfort; the suffix -less and -ful build the two opposite adjectives from the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」还衍生出 fortify、fortitude 与 comfort；后缀 -less 与 -ful 从名词造出两个相反的形容词。

items.example: The root supplies the sense of strength.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「力量」的意思。

items.structure: Old French esforz, noun of esforcier
items.example: The effort cost them a whole day.
items.exampleCN: 这份努力花了他们一整天。

items.example: An effortful climb ended at the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 一段费力的攀登在岭上结束。

items.example: She breathed effortfully on the last stretch.
items.exampleCN: 最后一段她呼吸得很费力。

items.example: His stroke looked effortless.
items.exampleCN: 他的划水看起来毫不费力。

items.example: The glider rose effortlessly.
items.exampleCN: 滑翔机毫不费力地升了上去。

items.example: The effortlessness was the result of years of drill.
items.exampleCN: 这种毫不费力是多年苦练的结果。

items.example: They fortified the bank against the current.
items.exampleCN: 他们加固了堤岸以抗水流。

items.example: She met the loss with fortitude.
items.exampleCN: 她以坚毅面对这次损失。

items.example: The blanket gave the child comfort.
items.exampleCN: 这条毯子给了孩子安慰。
